title: Transmigrated as a Vicious Supporting Female Lead? The Male Lead Insists on Marrying Me!
author: Qi Bu Long Dong
synopsis: The moment Cui Mingyu opened her eyes, she found she had transmigrated into a novel as a vicious supporting female lead who was obsessed with love and constantly stirring up trouble. Seeing that she was on the verge of being loathed and purged by the male lead, she decisively pulled back from the brink and turned to look for a better match. But who would have thought that the male lead, who had previously looked at her with disdain, would start looking at her with an increasingly strange expression... Has he lost his mind?

chapters.title: A Chance Encounter in the Woods
chapters.content:
On the 16th day of the ninth month of the seventh year of Shengwu, at the Lishan Hunting Grounds.

With a "whoosh," a long arrow tore through the air and pinned itself into the trunk of a cypress tree, the fletching vibrating.

Gu Yuechan, seemingly unsatisfied, reached for another arrow to shoot at the tree.

"Yuechan, why bother taking your anger out on that tree?" Sima Yu rode her horse to her side. "Second Young Master Ye is blind; you might as well shoot those two dog eyes of his."

Gu Yuechan angrily put down her arrow and looked at the woman beside her who loved to stir up trouble: "Your Highness, your words are light and airy, but I fear if I actually did as you suggested, I would be thrown into prison immediately."

Sima Yu chuckled and pinched her flushed cheek: "Didn't you say Second Young Master Ye was obedient to your every word? How did he end up entangled with that Xie Peiluo again?"

The two had grown up together; Gu Yuechan was both her study companion and her cousin, so they spoke freely.

Gu Yuechan huffed. Her appearance was delicate and gorgeous; dressed in red riding gear, she looked even more stunning than a blooming peony. To say she was the most beautiful in the capital would not be an exaggeration—even Sima Yu couldn't help but marvel at her.

How could an ordinary man not be captivated?

"My father has been back from his mourning period for nearly half a year, yet there is still no news from the Ministry of Personnel. I heard from my mother and the nannies that many of his former colleagues have been avoiding him, perhaps because of her identity." Gu Yuechan’s expression dimmed. "I fear his mother is just like those other bureaucrats, avoiding the Gu family at all costs. But the Sage did not wipe out my maternal grandfather’s entire family; perhaps the Sage no longer holds a grudge about what happened back then."

It was rumored that the Sage had been sent to a Taoist temple by the late Emperor in his youth because of the slanders of Noble Consort Zheng, and Gu Yuechan’s mother was the biological sister of Noble Consort Zheng. The powerful in the capital dared not gamble on the Sage’s true thoughts.

Sima Yu was the daughter of Noble Consort Zheng, so she understood this well.

Fortunately, before the late Emperor passed away, he had already arranged her future. She lived in the Princess’s Mansion and had her own fief for support, so she did not need to worry about the new Emperor’s moods.

"If you are deeply in love with that Second Young Master Ye, there are ways," Sima Yu pondered for a moment. "How about I send my guards to kidnap Xie Peiluo?"

Gu Yuechan looked at her listlessly: "Who is deeply in love with that heartless man? I am just unwilling to let it go. Besides, the Xie family is currently at the height of their power; there is no need for you to take risks for me, cousin."

Just as she was about to feign indifference, the sound of hooves approached from behind. She turned her head, and upon seeing the faces of the two people in the lead, her expression instantly fell.

A man and a woman, both dressed in sky-blue nomadic clothing, rode side by side like a golden boy and a jade girl.

"Your Highness." Xie Peiluo reined in her white horse, first nodding in greeting to Sima Yu, then turning her gaze to Gu Yuechan, saying gently: "Lady Gu, just now Young Master Ye was worried about your safety. Now that we see you are well, we can rest easy."

Gu Yuechan glared at the man who looked full of worry: "There is no need for you to worry. You should just focus on teaching Lady Xie how to ride."

"Sixth Sister." Seeing her anger, Ye Zheng was flustered: "Don't misunderstand, it’s just that Mother said..."

Seeing him acting like a man who only listened to his mother made Gu Yuechan irritable. She turned around, flicked her riding crop, and headed straight into the woods, too lazy to pay attention to the people behind her.

Seeing this, Ye Zheng also wanted to swing his whip, but the woman beside him let out a cry. He looked to the side and saw Xie Peiluo seemingly startled by her horse, swaying as she clutched the reins.

Ye Zheng had no choice but to steady her, though his gaze couldn't help but follow the woman riding away.

"Young Master Ye, don't worry. Later, I will explain everything clearly to Lady Gu." Xie Peiluo steadied herself and consoled him in a soft voice: "Lady Gu will surely understand you."

Ye Zheng sighed and muttered: "That is all I can do."

Sima Yu looked at the pair and sneered: "Young Master Ye, take care of yourself." She then turned around, swung her whip, and went to find the person who had left in a huff.

Gu Yuechan was an excellent rider, and her horse was a fine breed gifted by a foreign land. Sima Yu was only a few steps behind, but she could no longer see her shadow.

Although the hunting grounds had been cleared, it was getting late. If she got lost in the woods, what would happen to a delicate young lady like Gu Yuechan if something went wrong?

"Lin Qi, follow me. The others, split up and search. You must bring Lady Gu back safely."

Deep in the woods, after Gu Yuechan calmed down, she noticed that the scenery around her was completely unfamiliar. She didn't know where she had run to and gradually became uneasy.

At that moment, a deer ran past her. She had no interest in hunting and was waiting for it to pass so she could find her way back, when an arrow from an unknown direction suddenly struck the deer in the head.

The blood-red arrowhead pierced through the deer’s dark eye, and in an instant, the deer collapsed.

Gu Yuechan screamed, and her horse, a Lion-maned steed, paced uneasily.

"Who is there?"

A deep male voice came from ahead. Not long after, a man in black nomadic clothing rode out from the trees. When he saw Gu Yuechan’s face, his gaze faltered.

"And you are..." Gu Yuechan suddenly noticed another horse to his right, hidden by the leaves, making it hard to see clearly.

She pursed her lips and changed her question: "And who are you?"

"Yun Qi."

The man in the shadows called out. His voice was clear and cold, like a mountain spring, gentle and pleasant to the ear.

The man called Yun Qi seemed startled, immediately coming to his senses. He said with a solemn expression: "Young Lady, you had better leave quickly. This is not a place for you to be."

Gu Yuechan thought to herself, what a big ego.

The Lishan Hunting Grounds were imperial land. Could he be the Sage himself, to be able to drive others away?

This autumn hunt, specially organized by Princess Lehua, was rumored to be because the Princess was worried about the Sage’s lack of heirs and had invited eligible young ladies from the capital to select concubines for him. Unfortunately, the Sage had not come.

Although she felt this person’s attitude was unreasonable, she was alone, so her own confidence naturally waned. She carefully examined his attire and had a guess.

She blinked pitifully, softening her vibrant appearance, which only added to her pitiable charm.

"But, I cannot find the way back."

Yun Qi looked into the woods, looking troubled.

The sound of hooves rang out, and the man in the woods finally revealed his true appearance.

His hair was tied with a jade crown, his face as handsome as jade, and a white Taoist robe draped over his tall, slender frame. As the wind lifted his robes, it only brought four words to mind—ethereal and otherworldly.

Only his eyes were extremely cold, completely ruining the gentle aura around him.

Gu Yuechan looked him over twice and realized with a start: "You must be a Taoist priest from some temple."

Yun Qi was about to reply, but was interrupted by the man in the Taoist robe: "Indeed. If the young lady wishes to return, follow this path forward, and the guards of the hunting grounds will lead you back to the palace."

Seeing that he spoke much more gently than the previous man, the dimples at the corners of Gu Yuechan’s mouth deepened: "Thank you, Priest. May I ask which temple you are from? I can send my servants to add some incense to your temple."

"Yong'an Temple." The man’s deep eyes rested on her porcelain-like face: "Young Lady, there is no need for such formalities."

Such a familiar name.

Gu Yuechan lowered her eyes to think for a moment. When she remembered why Yong'an Temple sounded familiar, the look in her eyes as she looked at him changed instantly.

Wasn't that the place where the Sage had been imprisoned in his youth?

She had heard people mention that the Sage was quite close to the Taoist priests of Yong'an Temple, and the current Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was a priest from that very temple.

No wonder his attendant had such a big ego. She had thought he was just from a high-ranking family, never expecting him to be a confidant of the Sage.

She felt a moment of resentment toward the people in the court who were suppressing her father’s career because they were guessing the Sage’s likes and dislikes, and then she thought, if someone could put in a good word for her in the Sage’s ear, perhaps her family could overcome this crisis.

Gu Yuechan’s heart stirred. She drove her horse forward, her dark, pure eyes looking at him, the tear mole at the corner of her eye shining brightly.

"I wonder if it would be convenient for you to give me a ride?"

She had never been refused such a simple request before.

The man in the Taoist robe remained silent for a long time, just looking into her eyes without a word.

Just as Gu Yuechan thought she was about to fail, the man in the Taoist robe nodded: "Very well."

chapters.title: Traveling Together
chapters.content:
A red horse and a black horse rode side by side. Yun Qi followed behind, feeling utterly perplexed—since when had the Sage become so easy to talk to?

"I hear the Sage practiced at Yongan Temple in his youth," Gu Yuechan said in a sweet, soft voice. "The Daoist priest does not look very old; I wonder if you have ever spent time with the Sage?"

The man in the Daoist robe gave an ambiguous grunt.

Gu Yuechan’s fingertips, gripping the reins, tightened and then relaxed. After a few moments, she asked, "Have you ever heard the Sage mention Grand Tutor Gu?"

Her tone was filled with both anticipation and fear; if he had been mentioned, perhaps it meant the Sage still cherished the memory of her grandfather’s service.

However, there was another possibility, though she felt that since her grandfather was such a gentle man, the Sage surely would not hold a grudge against him.

The man in the Daoist robe turned his head, his gaze lingering for a moment on her slightly pursed, vermilion lips. "Grand Tutor Gu?"

It seemed he had never mentioned him.

Well, that made sense. He was, after all, just a Daoist priest; why would the Sage discuss court trivialities with him? Her expression dimmed. "He was my grandfather. If you haven't heard of him, then never mind."

Yun Qi, following behind, could not hide his shock.

Nine years ago, when the Sage was restored to the position of Crown Prince, the late Emperor had appointed Master Gu, then the Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, as the Crown Prince’s Grand Tutor, sending him into the Eastern Palace to instruct the Prince.

Grand Tutor Gu was related by marriage to the Zheng family. When the late Emperor had him instruct the Prince, it was surely with the intention of fostering harmony between the Prince and the then-living Noble Consort Zheng.

But the Sage never showed his true feelings on the surface. How could he have genuinely regarded Grand Tutor Gu as a teacher in his heart, considering that Noble Consort Zheng had done everything in her power to prevent the Sage from returning to the palace?

To think this girl was a member of the Gu family...

He looked at the Sage’s back, feeling the chill radiating from him growing heavier. He only hoped this young Lady Gu would say no more.

Perhaps his silent prayer was answered, for neither of them spoke again.

The sun hung low, dim and fading. The autumn wind swept up yellowing, precarious leaves. Amidst the desolation, only the rhythmic clatter of hooves remained.

Gu Yuechan felt dejected for a while, but she was unwilling to give up just like that. It was not easy to encounter someone who was on good terms with the Sage, and he didn't seem like an unreasonable person—just a man of few words.

She rallied her spirits and looked at him with a smile. "Then when will you return to Yongan Temple, Daoist? I would like to go and thank you for showing me the way today."

"No need. It was a small matter."

Although the man in the Daoist robe’s expression remained unchanged, Gu Yuechan keenly sensed that his tone seemed a bit colder than before.

"You... have you ever heard the Sage speak my grandfather's name?" Gu Yuechan tilted her head to look at him, her voice honeyed. "Won't you tell me the truth? Next time I go to Yongan Temple, I will certainly donate plenty of incense money."

The man in the Daoist robe’s gaze swept over her charming, naive face. After a moment, he spoke flatly: "What if I have? What if I haven't?"

Gu Yuechan’s heart leapt, and she hurriedly poured out her words: "My grandfather has been deceased for three years. My father returned after his mourning period, but for some reason, the Ministry of Personnel has not reappointed him to an official post. I just wanted to know, is the Sage dissatisfied with my father for some reason?"

"The Ministry of Personnel’s agenda for official appointments is cumbersome. You need only wait patiently."

After saying this, the man in the Daoist robe gave a light flick of his wide sleeves and pointed ahead. "Young lady, you may go on your own from here."

The figures of the guards were already visible in the distance. Just as Gu Yuechan was about to thank him, she saw him turn his horse around and gallop into the forest along a small path, his attendants following closely behind, leaving only swirling dust in their wake.

She blinked, then suddenly patted her head in annoyance. He hadn't even answered when he would be at the temple, and she didn't even know his name.

But he was already long gone. She had no choice but to seek out the guards of the hunting grounds. Once one of them escorted her back to the temporary palace, Sima Yu’s maidservant hurriedly sent someone to inform the Princess that the Sixth Lady of the Gu family had returned.

Sima Yu rushed back upon receiving the news. She had been searching for half a day, her heart filled with anxiety. As soon as she entered the room, she saw the young woman sitting on the chaise longue, happily eating a jade-dew cake. Sima Yu walked over and gave her a swat on the head. "You really scared me to death! If something had actually happened, outsiders would say that Lady Gu Sixth was jealous and fought with others, only to lose her life in vain. You would have truly made a name for yourself in the capital then."

Gu Yuechan knew she had been too impulsive this time. She lowered her head, silently finishing the jade-dew cake in her hand, then took the handkerchief offered by the maid to wipe her hands clean before looking up with a sheepish smile. "Didn't I come back safe and sound?"

Being charming and coquettish was her specialty. Her fair, jade-like face was as clear and beautiful as a lotus. Sima Yu knew her cousin was best at acting spoiled, and in the end, she couldn't bear to scold her further.

"That Ye Second Young Master is like a blockhead," Sima Yu said, shifting her fire to the culprit. "It’s just as well the engagement is broken. How could he ever be worthy of you? Only Xie Second Lady treats him like a treasure. Another day, I’ll send you ten or eight young gentlemen; I guarantee every one of them will be better than Ye Second Young Master."

Gu Yuechan puffed out her cheeks. "Cousin, I just can't swallow this insult."

Originally, the engagement between the Gu family and the Marquis of Changping’s estate was between the eldest daughter, Gu Yueming, and the eldest son, Ye Yan. But who would have thought that Ye Yan would meet the Princess of Minghu and, ignoring his father’s objections, insist on breaking the engagement with Gu Yueming?

The late Emperor’s Noble Consort Zheng was deeply favored at the time and naturally would not allow her niece to suffer such a grievance. The matter grew, the situation reached a stalemate, and the Marquis of Changping’s estate and the Gu residence became the talk of every street and alley in the capital. In the end, it was the Gu family that took the initiative to step back and dissolve the engagement, which finally calmed the matter.

Their engagement had been set while the previous Marquis of Changping was still alive. The current Marquis felt deeply guilty and pleaded for a long time, eventually leading to the new engagement between Gu Yuechan and the Ye family’s second son, Ye Zheng.

Ye Zheng’s mother was the Marquis’s second wife, Lady Xu. When the engagement was made, the Gu family had not yet fallen into decline; there was Noble Consort Zheng in the Inner Court and Grand Tutor Gu in the court. Naturally, she had not objected.

But times had changed, and the Gu family was no longer as glorious as it once was. When Lady Xu saw her now, the warmth of the past was long gone.

If the engagement were broken, people in the capital would surely mock the Gu family for having yet another daughter rejected by the Marquis of Changping’s estate.

Gu Yuechan pulled on her cousin’s sleeve, feeling dejected. "I was thinking that once I married into the Ye family, I would definitely seize control of the household, so that those two bad people who hurt my sister—Ye First Young Master and the Princess of Minghu—would regret it."

Sima Yu couldn't help but roll her eyes. "The Princess of Minghu is my uncle’s daughter; I still call her 'sister,' yet you plot against her right in front of me. With your level of scheming, you’d better save it, lest you get yourself trapped."

"Cousin," Gu Yuechan whimpered, hugging her waist. "But you and I are the closest, aren't we?"

Sima Yu didn't say anything, but the smile on her face betrayed her.

She tapped her cousin’s forehead and laughed, "You, you only know how to use these tricks. When will you ever stop making people worry?"

Gu Yuechan let out a soft sound and said, "Cousin, don't underestimate me. I know many things. Once my father is restored to his post, let’s see if anyone dares to look down on my family again."

Hearing the certainty in her voice, it sounded as if she already had a plan.

Sima Yu made her sit up straight and scrutinized her for a moment, saying skeptically, "Tell me, what good plan do you have? Are you planning to send Ye Second Young Master to Lady Xie’s bed so she can ask her grandfather, Minister He, to arrange a post for your father? Or perhaps ask her sister, Noble Consort Xie, to whisper a few good words about your father in the Sage’s ear?"

Hearing this, Gu Yuechan’s eyes lit up. "Hey, would Xie Second Lady agree to that?"

Sima Yu sighed, holding her forehead. "What do you think? The root of this matter lies with the Sage. If the Sage doesn't loosen his grip, do you see any official in the court who would dare to advise him? The Sage is cold-natured; why would the concubines in the Inner Court risk angering him for the sake of your family’s affairs?"

Gu Yuechan pouted. "Fine, I didn't really intend to do that anyway. Why would I ever beg Xie Second Lady? I’m afraid that as soon as I opened my mouth, she would mock me. I wouldn't do such a foolish thing."

Sima Yu crossed her arms, watching her with a composed look, waiting to see what kind of plan she could come up with.

chapters.title: The Daoist
chapters.content:
Gu Yuechan raised her eyebrows. "Cousin, I met a Daoist today who claimed to be from the Yong'an Temple."

There were likely few people in the capital who did not know of Yong'an Temple, if only because the Sage had once been imprisoned there.

However, that place was not open to casual visitors, so the people of the capital did not know much about what went on inside. They only knew that after the Sage ascended the throne, he had been quite kindly disposed toward the Daoists residing there.

Sima Yu nodded. "And then?"

"I happened to run into him in the woods today. He seemed like a gentle person, so I thought I might ask him to put in a good word for my father." Gu Yuechan looked quite pleased with herself. "Cousin, don't you think this is a good plan?"

Sima Yu was worried she might be getting swindled, but considering that the Lishan hunting grounds were not a place an ordinary Daoist could enter, she gave it some credence. "How do you know he is a Daoist from Yong'an Temple? Did he tell you so himself?"

"I asked him. I saw he was wearing white Daoist robes made of cloud brocade, so I knew he must be a high-ranking Daoist." Gu Yuechan had lived in the inner court often as a child and was very familiar with tribute goods. "Besides, the horse he was riding was a rare Red Qilin horse. If it wasn't a gift from the Sage, where else could he have gotten it? And..."

She lowered her voice. "The attendant following him had a token of the Imperial Guard hanging from his waist."

Seeing that her cousin was not entirely foolish, Sima Yu smiled with relief. "If that Daoist is willing to help, that is naturally a good thing. The people of Yong'an Temple share a unique bond with the Sage. However, if he is unwilling, do not pester him, lest you provoke him."

"I know, Cousin." After saying this, Gu Yuechan reached for a jade dew cake on the plate on the table. She had been talking for so long that she was hungry.

Just as she took a bite, a palace maid reported from outside the room that the Second Young Master Ye had arrived.

"Shall we see him?" Sima Yu asked.

Gu Yuechan pondered for a moment and nodded.

Sima Yu also wanted to see if the Second Young Master Ye realized his mistake, so she said, "Let him in."

Ye Zheng walked in with hurried steps, the worry on his face only fading when he saw the young woman on the couch.

"Liangniang, I am glad you are unharmed."

Gu Yuechan watched him walk straight toward her and said with a huff of feigned anger, "Just stand there and speak."

Ye Zheng hesitated and stopped, knowing she was still angry. He hurriedly explained, "Liangniang, please do not misunderstand. The Second Young Lady Xie is not skilled at riding, and her maid was not by her side. I was merely worried she might get hurt in the woods, so I accompanied her."

"Is that so?" Gu Yuechan raised her delicate eyebrows. "Don't you know that your mother intends to bring you two together? The Xie family is powerful now; how could our Gu family compare? If you wish to break off our engagement, just say so directly. Do you think I would cling to you and refuse to let go?"

"Yuechan, my dear." Hearing her mention breaking off the engagement, Ye Zheng could no longer stand still. He had just taken a step forward when the palace maid blocked his path, leaving him in a dilemma.

"I... how could I ever want to break off our engagement?" Ye Zheng had known she was his fiancée since he was ten. Ever since she returned to the capital, his heart and eyes had been set on marrying her as soon as possible. "Don't worry, no matter what Mother thinks, in my heart..." He lowered his eyes shyly. "In my heart, there is only you."

Gu Yuechan looked at him, half-believing. "Really? Then you must not pay any attention to the Second Young Lady Xie from now on. Can you do that?"

Ye Zheng nodded repeatedly. "I can. Are you not angry anymore, then?"

Gu Yuechan was not so easily appeased. She smiled with a touch of pride. "That depends on how you behave in the future, Second Young Master. It is getting late; you should head back now."

The young lady, with her celestial beauty, smiled brightly in the candlelight. Ye Zheng’s face turned beet red instantly, and even his neck felt hot.

"Yuechan, my dear, please... please rest assured." He lowered his head and hurried out in a panic.

Sima Yu couldn't help but give Gu Yuechan a gesture of admiration. "The Second Young Master Ye is rather thin-skinned. Although he is obedient, will he be able to protect you in the future?"

Gu Yuechan didn't mind. "Do you think I want a husband who controls me? I certainly don't. Besides, he has already been granted an official post and has a bright future ahead of him. Even if the worst happens, I still have you, Cousin."

Sima Yu smiled helplessly, not telling her that as a princess, her own position was but a reflection of the moon in the water. After her father and mother passed away, the respect others showed her was merely superficial.

"But before that," Gu Yuechan clenched her fists and looked at her solemnly, "I must find a way to get my father reinstated."

Sima Yu did not discourage her. "Then I shall wait for your good news."

Gu Yuechan, thinking her cousin truly believed she could succeed, smiled with satisfaction. "Cousin, you are the most discerning. Unlike my elder sister, who is always forbidding me from doing this or that. I am not a child anymore."

She, too, was capable of protecting her family.

"Yes, our Zhaozhao is almost ready to be married; how could you be a child?" Sima Yu teased. "Perhaps by next year, you will be a mother yourself."

"Cousin!" Gu Yuechan drew out the long tail of her voice, a flush of shyness coloring her features. "It won't be that fast. I don't even know how to be a mother yet."

"I don't know about that either," Sima Yu said, tapping her chin with her index finger. "But I suppose it will come naturally. If not, just ask your aunt to give you a couple of nannies to look after things."

Hearing her mention her mother, Gu Yuechan couldn't help but think of the trivial matters at home, and her eyes dimmed. "I really don't want to leave home. My second aunt thinks my mother is hindering the prospects of the men in the Gu family, and even Grandmother..."

She stopped mid-sentence. Her grandmother had always doted on her, and she did not want to speak ill of her.

Sima Yu suddenly understood why her cousin, who was usually simple-minded and only cared for jewelry and fine clothes, had suddenly come up with this idea.

"Tomorrow, when the hunt ends and we return to the capital, I will think of a way for you as well." Sima Yu ran through a list of people in her mind who could speak to the Sage. "Why don't I take you to see my eldest sister first?"

Sima Yu’s eldest sister was the Grand Princess Lehua, born of the same mother as the Sage, the Empress Dowager Fan.

She was gentle with others, and even toward Sima Yu, she never spoke a harsh word.

Hearing her mention the Grand Princess Lehua, Gu Yuechan hesitated. She had met the Grand Princess a few days ago. At first, the Grand Princess had been quite warm, asking about her background, but after hearing her answer, her expression had clearly become much more indifferent.

She was not someone who couldn't read the room.

In the past, when the Empress Dowager Fan was nearly stripped of her title, the Grand Princess Lehua had already been in her prime. Regarding the events of those years, others said it was all because her aunt, Noble Consort Zheng, had bewitched the late Emperor, causing him to ignore the then-Empress Fan and her children, even sending the six-year-old Sage to a Daoist temple.

Although she didn't believe it, it was a fact that her aunt had been favored.

She feared the Grand Princess Lehua felt nothing but disgust for anyone associated with the Zheng family.

"Perhaps, let's forget it," Gu Yuechan shook her head. "You are the Grand Princess's sister, so she treats you with kindness, but she likely won't be the same toward others. I fear I might make things worse."

chapters.title: Offspring
chapters.content:
Sima Yu pondered for a moment. "Then I shall go and test my eldest sister’s attitude. Have your dinner on your own; if there is anything you wish to eat, just instruct Chunfang."

Gu Yuechan was so excited that she hugged her, tilting her face up with a smile. "Cousin, you are truly wonderful. If you ever need my help in the future, just say the word. I would go through fire and water for you."

"I have grown tired of your sweet talk, and besides..." Sima Yu pinched the tip of her nose. "Didn't you say earlier that you wanted me to be your pillar of support? Now you are the one offering to help me; you had better wish me well."

Gu Yuechan gave a soft smile, released her, and waved her hand slightly. "Then hurry along, Cousin. I shall wait for your return."

Princess Lehua resided in the Hanyue Palace. When Sima Yu arrived with her maid Chunli, she was informed that the Sage was inside and the Princess had no time to see her.

Hearing that the Sage had actually come, Sima Yu had no choice but to return.

Unless absolutely necessary, she did not wish to see the Sage. Although this imperial brother, who had lived in a Taoist temple since childhood, did not often fly into a rage, he was by no means a gentle man. Within two years of ascending the throne, he had led troops to personally campaign against the Southern Yi and the barbarian tribes.

In just three years, he had forced them to bow and submit.

Within the imperial court, he had calmly purged the old officials whom their late father had once favored, including her maternal grandfather, the Right Chancellor Zheng.

Sima Yu feared seeing those emotionless eyes of his, as if she were not his sister, but someone insignificant, and her life hung merely upon his whim.

Perhaps the only person in this world who did not fear him was her eldest sister.

Princess Lehua had taken great care of the Sage, so the Sage did indeed listen to a word or two from this sister.

However, it was clear he had not listened this time.

"You did not like the consort Father chose for you, and you did not want the one Mother chose. Fine, I know you have a knot in your heart, but Your Majesty, you are already twenty-five this year. Do you know that there are already those in the court proposing the appointment of an Imperial Crown Brother?" Princess Lehua, Sima Yan, said, her voice trembling with anger. "This time I let you choose for yourself, and you agreed perfectly well, yet you only came today to fob me off. You didn't even meet those young women."

Sima Xin held his tea, listening as she became increasingly agitated, his expression and posture as steady as ever.

Sima Yan pointed at the Taoist robe he wore, her anger burning hotter. "I suspect it was that old Taoist who corrupted you, making you not even keep the matter of offspring in your heart."

"Elder Sister." Sima Xin lifted his eyelids slightly. "The Fifth Brother is also your brother of the same mother. Mother has already mentioned this matter to me, and there is nothing improper about it."

He spoke plainly, but Sima Yan felt a pang in her heart.

The Fifth Brother had grown up by their mother's side since childhood and was her solace when she had no one else to rely on. Sima Yan knew that their mother had always favored the Fifth Brother.

She had told her mother many times that the Sage was not a heartless man, merely one of few words, but people's hearts are not easily changed. Moreover, the Fifth Brother was at the age where he could act spoiled and charming, the most capable of winning people's favor.

Sima Yan’s throat tightened. After a long silence, she sighed. "Qingnu, then what was the point of everything Elder Sister did in the past?"

To help her brother leave that remote, desolate Taoist temple and reclaim the position of Crown Prince, Sima Yan had done so many things against her own conscience that she could no longer count them herself.

Sima Xin rubbed the side of his teacup with his thumb, causing the tea to ripple slightly.

Princess Lehua did not often bring up the past with the Sage, but this time she was truly at her wit's end. The inner court was desolate, and there was not the slightest sign of offspring. Was her brother truly going to live like a reclusive Taoist monk?

"In two months," Sima Xin said calmly.

With these words, Sima Yan felt half her worries vanish. Her tone softened. "Why not stay here for dinner before returning? The Yuanzhang Palace is likely not yet properly prepared."

Sima Xin set down his teacup. "There are still state affairs in the court that have not been handled. Elder Sister need not trouble herself."

Sima Yan knew his temperament and understood that further persuasion was useless, so she did not press him.

...

Returning empty-handed, Sima Yu arrived at the Lingchun Palace and drank a cup of hot tea before saying to her cousin, who was looking at her expectantly, "It was bad timing today; the Sage was there. Let us wait until tomorrow."

"The Sage?" Gu Yuechan’s lips parted slightly. "Why did he come today?"

The autumn hunt had already concluded; what reason did the Sage have to come here suddenly?

That Taoist priest must have come along with the Sage as well.

Gu Yuechan recalled the purpose of this spring hunt and could not help but lower her voice, a trace of teasing appearing in her eyes. "Could it be that the inner court is to have new consorts? Perhaps by next year, the Sage will have offspring of his own."

"You, even daring to joke about the Sage's affairs." Sima Yu waved her hand, dismissing the attending maids, and reminded her, "Be careful not to make matters worse."

Gu Yuechan pursed her lips, looking at her with innocent, glistening eyes.

"Alright," Sima Yu picked up her jade chopsticks. "There is no one else here now."

Gu Yuechan immediately beamed. "I only dare say this with you, Cousin. It is strange, though. Although no one has entered the inner court for many years, when the Sage was the Crown Prince, the late Emperor had already bestowed many noblewomen upon him. Even if the Sage did not like my aunt, why have the other concubines produced nothing?"

She recalled that before her younger brother was born, her grandmother had tirelessly tried to find a concubine for her father. Later, her father stated bluntly that it was a physical ailment of his own, not her mother's fault, and only then did her grandmother stop.

A thought flashed through Gu Yuechan's mind: "Could it be that the Sage himself has a physical ailment that hinders offspring?"

Sima Yu did not deliberately pry into the affairs of the inner court, but she knew there were no favored concubines. However, speaking of this risked the suspicion of prying into the Sage's preferences. Fearing her cousin’s simple nature might lead her to mention this to others, she said, "I do not know. Perhaps the Sage has been away on military campaigns and had no time to spare. Now that the world is at peace, I am sure good news will come from the palace before long."

Gu Yuechan was not entirely convinced. The Sage had married when he was the Crown Prince. The Crown Princess was from the Zheng clan; at the time, the only young woman of suitable age in the Zheng family was her aunt, Zheng Shu. Although it lacked proper ritual, it could not overcome the late Emperor’s firm decision.

This was meant to reconcile the Zheng family with the Crown Prince, but unfortunately, after the late Emperor passed away, the Crown Princess did not successfully become Empress, but was instead titled Consort Xian, which showed the Sage was not satisfied with this marriage.

At that time, the late Emperor's influence still lingered, and countless officials in the court opposed him. The Sage's foundation was not yet stable, yet he did not yield an inch.

Gu Yuechan was only ten years old that year, but she vaguely remembered that her mother and father had looked terrible during that period. Not long after, her grandfather requested to retire, which the Sage granted, and her father was sent away to Qingzhou to serve as the Prefect. Thus, their family avoided a purge in the court.

After this, she realized that the Sage truly disliked the Zheng family.

But the many noblewomen bestowed by the late Emperor to compensate the Crown Prince had nothing to do with the Zheng clan; surely the Sage would not be dissatisfied with them as well.

Gu Yuechan calculated the time: seven years. The concubines in the inner court had not even had a single pregnancy. It was clear the problem lay with the Sage.

A good idea suddenly struck her. She could introduce the physician who had treated her father to the Sage.

However, this matter required someone to act as a go-between. Otherwise, if the Sage were to take offense, her failing would be a small matter, but if it implicated her family, she would be a sinner.

chapters.title: Returning to the Capital
chapters.content:
The next day, the schedule for the return to the capital remained unchanged. Gu Yuechan learned that the Sage had already departed ahead of them, and she had not seen that Daoist priest again along the way. She secretly guessed that the priest had likely arrived with the Sage and had naturally departed with him as well.

That Daoist was indeed highly regarded by the Sage.

Her confidence grew, and she looked forward to returning to the capital with such anticipation that even the people she disliked seemed three parts more tolerable.

Upon seeing Xie Erniang, she even greeted her with a smile, enjoying the hypocritical expression of the girl who clearly disliked her yet had to force a smile in return.

Sima Yu watched her cousin’s mischievous expression and smiled helplessly. She thought to herself that perhaps it was because Ye Erlang had truly listened to her over the past few days and had not spoken a single word to Xie Peiluo, which was why she was in such a good mood upon seeing her.

Upon returning home, Gu Yuechan lifted her skirts and hurried without pause toward the courtyard where her parents resided.

Just as she crossed the threshold, her maid, Qiongyu, gave a light cough. "Young Mistress, watch your posture."

Gu Yuechan hurriedly clasped her hands together and shortened her stride. Only when the hairpins dangling at her temples had settled did she walk slowly toward the main room.

Zheng Ying had already received news of her youngest daughter’s return and was preparing to go see her when she heard a maid outside announce that the Sixth Young Mistress had arrived.

"Mother." Gu Yuechan crossed her hands and performed a graceful bow. "Your daughter pays her respects."

Zheng Ying looked at her daughter’s proper demeanor and felt a sense of relief. Her youngest daughter was beautiful and sweet-tongued, and all the elders in the family doted on her. When they were back at their ancestral home in Yunzhou, she hadn't wanted to constrain her daughter too much, but upon returning to the capital, one had to be cautious in all matters. For the past two months, she had repeatedly instructed her daughter to keep etiquette and decorum in mind, and it seemed she hadn't forgotten them despite her trip to the Lishan hunting grounds.

"Come," Zheng Ying beckoned gently. "Let Mother see, have you lost weight?"

Gu Yuechan’s eyes curved into crescents as she nestled against her mother, speaking in a soft, coquettish tone: "I have lost a little. Riding horses is so tiring. But I had a bountiful harvest this time; I even brought back venison for Father and Mother to enjoy."

Zheng Ying looked her over carefully. She looked plump and rosy, but thinking of how long she had been away from home, she said with a pang of heartache, "Stay here for dinner tonight. I will have your father stop by Xingrongju on his way back to buy the pastries you like, so you won't have to go get them yourself."

The pastries from Xingrongju were famous throughout the capital, but they were notoriously difficult to purchase.

Upon hearing this, Gu Yuechan immediately leaned against her mother’s shoulder and smiled. "I knew it, Mother is the best to me."

However, mentioning her father reminded her of her true objective. "Mother, do you remember the physician who treated Father ten years ago?"

"Treated your father for what ailment?" Zheng Ying looked puzzled. "Ten years is such a long time ago, I’m afraid I don’t recall. Besides, our family mostly engaged doctors from the He'an Hall."

"It’s just..." Gu Yuechan felt a bit embarrassed to speak, so she hinted vaguely, "It’s the physician who treated Father before my younger brother was born. Wasn't it because of that physician that Mother was able to give birth to my brother? Mother, I’ve heard people talk about it."

Zheng Ying’s expression stiffened. How old was her daughter back then? To think she would remember such an old matter. "Why do you ask about this?" She thought of the fact that Ye Erlang had been on this trip as well, and her brow furrowed. "Did Ye Erlang say something?"

Gu Yuechan: "No, he didn't."

"Then why do you suddenly bring up the physician?" Zheng Ying scrutinized her expression. "You are not yet married. If that Ye Erlang dares to do anything improper toward you, you must not agree to it, do you understand?"

Gu Yuechan nodded repeatedly. She knew her mother had misunderstood, but if she told her the truth, she feared she wouldn't even be allowed to leave the house.

Her eyes darted around, and she suddenly thought of someone. "It’s... it’s Elder Sister. She wrote to me saying that Brother-in-law has some health issues, and that’s why I thought of it."

Zheng Ying’s eldest daughter, Gu Yueming—the "Elder Sister" Gu Yuechan referred to—had been married for nine years, but she only had one daughter. This had always been a source of heartache for Zheng Ying.

Hearing this, a subtle sense of relief washed over Zheng Ying. "If that is the case, then it should be taken seriously. But it has been so long that I cannot remember. When I recall it, I will write to your sister."

"No!" Gu Yuechan said urgently. If her mother wrote to her sister, wouldn't the lie be exposed? Seeing her mother’s suspicious expression, she thought quickly. "Elder Sister said this matter must be kept secret. If Mother writes a letter and Brother-in-law sees it, wouldn't it hurt his pride? It would be better to just send a physician directly, saying it is to check on Elder Sister. That way, we can have him check Brother-in-law’s pulse without him knowing."

This made sense, and Zheng Ying nodded to herself. "Very well. You don't need to worry about this anymore. You are an unmarried young lady; how can you keep such matters on your lips?"

Gu Yuechan agreed immediately. Since her mother didn't remember, she would just wait and see.

By the time her sister and mother realized what was happening, she would have already accomplished her goal, and by then, her mother certainly wouldn't blame her.

...

As dusk approached, Gu Mingtu arrived at the veranda carrying the pastries. Before he even entered, the joyful laughter of his wife and daughter reached his ears.

He lifted the corners of his mouth, suppressing the frustration of the setbacks he had faced that day. By the time he stepped into the room, not a trace of sorrow remained on his face.

"Father."

As soon as Gu Yuechan saw his figure, she called out excitedly, "You’re back!"

"Did you have a pleasant time at Lishan?" Gu Mingtu handed the pastry box to his daughter and asked warmly, "Did you suffer any grievances?"

Gu Yuechan took the food box bearing the "Xingrongju" emblem without hesitation and replied casually, "No. With Cousin there, who would dare let me suffer any grievances?"

Their family’s situation was not what it used to be, and they had been away from the capital for many years. He had been worried that his daughter would feel neglected or struggle to adapt, but seeing her still so cheerful and bright, Gu Mingtu finally felt at ease.

Zheng Ying, seeing her like this, worriedly said, "Your cousin and the Sage are not born of the same mother. Although she is a princess, she must still act with caution. If she were to catch the Sage's eye in a bad way, her life would be difficult. You must not use your cousin’s name to cause trouble outside. And another thing, I have often warned you: be more cautious in the capital and do not easily offend people..."

Seeing her mother start to nag again, Gu Yuechan quickly begged for mercy. "Mother, I remember everything. I will never cause trouble. In your eyes, am I really such an unreasonable person?"

"That’s right, my lady," Gu Mingtu chimed in with a smile. "Zhaozhao is the most well-behaved. It’s time for dinner, isn't it? Qingyuan should be finished with his studies as well. Send someone to call him; hasn't he been talking about how much he misses Zhaozhao?"

Zheng Ying looked at her daughter’s nodding head and helplessly stopped. One of them didn't know their own limitations, and the other was blinded by his daughter’s well-behaved appearance.

Forget it, she would take it slowly.

After the family finished dinner, Gu Yuechan carried the Xingrongju pastries back to her own courtyard.

She had eaten too much at dinner and couldn't even touch the pastries, so she had to save them for tomorrow.

She stroked the pastry box with lingering affection. Just as she was about to have Qiongyu put it away, she suddenly remembered that she was going to the Daoist temple tomorrow to find that priest. To show her sincerity, she should bring something.

Gu Yuechan gazed at the eight pastries in the box and fell into deep thought. Should she pick two? No, better make it four; that wouldn't look too shabby.

"Qiongyu, find a peach-wood box, one that can hold four osmanthus cakes." She thought for a moment, then said to Biwen, "Also, bring me my money box, and get a few newly made pouches."

chapters.title: Heading to the Taoist Temple
chapters.content:
“Who is the young mistress planning to give these pastries to?” Qiongyu asked in detail, “A woman or a man?”

Gu Yuechan: “A man.”

Assuming she intended to give them to the second young master of the Ye family, Qiongyu smiled slightly: “Is the young mistress no longer angry with the second young master Ye?”

“What does he have to do with this?” Gu Yuechan carefully selected the pastries intended for the Taoist priest: “I am asking for a favor, so they must appear valuable.”

Asking for a favor?

Qiongyu was puzzled: “Has the young mistress encountered a difficult situation?”

Gu Yuechan looked up, just about to explain clearly, but then she thought better of it. Qiongyu was very rigid; what if she told her mother?

It is said that matters are achieved through secrecy. Her mother was right; she needed to be more cautious.

“I am preparing to go offer incense and pray for the Taoist master to bless our family with smooth sailing in everything,” Gu Yuechan said while taking the money box handed to her by Biwen: “Have the carriage prepared; I will go tomorrow.”

The young mistress was indeed worried because things had not been going well for the family. Going to the Taoist temple to offer incense and clear her mind might be good; perhaps the young mistress’s mood would improve.

Qiongyu did not ask further and turned to find the peachwood box the young mistress had requested.

Gu Yuechan, who was counting her money, raised the corners of her lips slightly, but she became troubled again as she looked at the silver in the box. How much silver should she give that Taoist priest?

If it were too little, she feared he wouldn't take it seriously; if it were too much…

Gu Yuechan pursed her lips. She was reluctant.

Because she had spent money without restraint in her childhood, her mother had begun to control her expenses, giving her only two taels of silver a month. If she gave all her savings to the Taoist priest, she wouldn't even be able to afford a single gold hairpin in the days to come.

But thinking that her father’s affairs were more important, she hardened her heart, placed five hundred-tael banknotes into a dark peony-patterned gold-threaded pouch, and put the remaining smaller banknotes and loose silver into a simple, elegant blue silk pouch.

Biwen, who was serving nearby, saw that the young mistress had taken all the money out of the box and couldn't help but be shocked: “Young mistress, this is what you have saved for a long time. Are you thinking of buying some expensive pearl hairpin again?”

“No,” Gu Yuechan gripped the pouch, her gaze firm: “I am going to offer incense.”

Biwen: “...”

Only today did she realize that her young mistress was so sincere toward the Three Pure Ones that she had emptied her entire fortune.

The next day, after Gu Yuechan paid her respects to her grandmother and parents, she boarded the carriage with Qiongyu and Biwen and ordered the coachman to head to Yongan Temple.

The coachman was stunned.

Seeing him not moving, Gu Yuechan asked: “Do you not know the way?”

“Sixth Young Mistress, it’s not that I don’t know the location of Yongan Temple, it’s just…” The coachman’s rugged brows furrowed: “It is said that Yongan Temple is guarded by the Imperial Guard, and ordinary people cannot enter. Xianglong Temple inside the city and Jingyun Temple outside the city are both extremely efficacious, and ordinary people can enter them. Why doesn’t the Sixth Young Mistress choose another place?”

But Gu Yuechan had made up her mind and refused to change it. Qiongyu tried to persuade her a couple of times, but it was useless.

“Just go; if we truly cannot enter, we will return,” Gu Yuechan said, deliberately putting on a stern face: “Don’t tell me I have to listen to you regarding where I go?”

Seeing her anger, the coachman hurriedly apologized: “It is my loose tongue.”

He did not hesitate any longer, flicked the horsewhip, and the wheels turned, carrying the mistress and her two maids toward the outskirts of the city.

Gu Yuechan checked the items she was bringing for the Taoist priest again. The more she looked, the more anxious she felt. If the Taoist priest was a trusted aide of the Emperor, these things might be insignificant to him. Perhaps she should say more kind words; if the Taoist priest were in a good mood, he might agree to her request.

On the other side, after hearing the coachman’s words, Biwen and Qiongyu both wore hesitant expressions, wondering if they should try to persuade the young mistress.

Although the young mistress was kind to them, her occasionally stubborn nature meant that even the master and mistress could only go along with her; they had even less power to stop her.

“Young mistress…” Qiongyu had only just begun to speak when Gu Yuechan raised a hand to stop her: “You are my maids; just listen to my orders. If you dare to tell my mother…” She hummed: “Then you can go serve by my mother’s side.”

Qiongyu and Biwen now understood even more clearly that what the young mistress was doing was something the mistress would definitely not allow. They were anxious, but they could only bow their heads and agree.

They only hoped the young mistress wouldn't cause any trouble. The mistress had repeatedly warned them that the capital was full of powerful and influential people, and they must not let the young mistress act as recklessly as she did in Yunzhou, lest she invite disaster.

Yongan Temple was located in a forest outside the city. Halfway there, the road was already deserted.

Gu Yuechan lifted the carriage curtain and looked for a long time. This temple was truly built in a remote place. Next time, she should bring more people, lest Qiongyu’s words come true and they encounter villains.

However, although the surroundings of the temple were desolate, the “Yongan Temple” plaque was grand, and there were indeed four soldiers in armor guarding the entrance.

The carriage stopped at a distance without approaching. Qiongyu just took a quiet look and turned to try to persuade the young mistress to think twice.

However, Gu Yuechan had already stood up, ready to get off. Biwen followed closely behind, leaving only the hesitant Qiongyu, who, having no other choice, could only follow her mistress toward the temple gate.

Before the three of them could get close, they were sternly shouted at by a soldier: “Who approaches?”

Gu Yuechan had seen many imperial guards since she was a child; how could she be intimidated? “I am here to offer incense. Please report to your temple master.”

The soldier said coldly: “Incense cannot be offered here. Leave at once.”

“Is that so?” Gu Yuechan looked puzzled: “But when I met that Taoist priest at the Lishan hunting grounds a few days ago, he didn't say that.”

The Lishan hunting grounds were imperial property, and ordinary people were not allowed inside.

The soldier sensed her unusual status and, remembering that the Emperor had just visited Lishan a few days ago, his expression softened slightly. He asked: “I wonder which Taoist priest you mean?”

Gu Yuechan couldn't say; the Taoist priest hadn't mentioned his Taoist name, and she had forgotten to ask.

She said calmly: “The Taoist priest said that when we meet again, he will naturally tell me his Taoist name. However, I remember his attendant was named Yunqi. If you don’t believe me, you can go inside and report that the Sixth Young Mistress of the Gu family has come to thank the Taoist priest for his guidance last time.”

They had just returned from Lishan with the Emperor, and this woman was so beautiful…

The four soldiers whispered to each other, and one turned and walked inside with long strides.

Although the soldier who had spoken coldly did not step aside, after hearing the name of the commander, he dared not be certain of the woman’s relationship with the Emperor.

“Then please wait a moment, young mistress,” he said politely.

Watching the soldier’s attitude soften, Qiongyu couldn't help but speculate: Was the young mistress really here for a serious matter? And she wondered who the Taoist priest the young mistress spoke of actually was.

In less than half an incense stick’s time, the soldier came out and said respectfully: “Young mistress, please enter.”

Gu Yuechan’s clenched fingers slowly relaxed, and she walked in with a steady pace. Just as she crossed the threshold, she heard Qiongyu give a short, urgent cry of “Young mistress.”

She looked back and saw Biwen and Qiongyu being blocked by the soldiers. As she looked at their anxious and worried expressions, she was just about to speak when she heard the soldier say: “Young mistress, please enter alone. They can wait here.”

When Qiongyu heard this, her eyes practically screamed: *Come back quickly.*

This temple was built in a desolate place, and no one knew the character of the people inside. The young mistress was a weak woman; what if something happened?

Gu Yuechan understood what Qiongyu meant, but she only hesitated for two breaths before resolutely leaving them behind and going in alone.

*If you don't enter the tiger's den, how can you catch the tiger's cub?*

She exhaled slowly. She was here to give money, so others naturally wouldn't be plotting against her wealth, and the Taoist priest was a man of the Way; he certainly wouldn't be interested in her beauty.

Gu Yuechan secretly encouraged herself. It was not easy to get in; this trip must yield results.

She must not back down.

chapters.title: Six Hundred Taels
chapters.content:
Gu Yuechan walked up the stone steps. After entering the Sanqing Hall, a young Daoist priest in a cyan robe was already waiting outside. He raised his hand to signal for her to follow him inside.

Exiting through the side door of the main hall and crossing the courtyard, a simple, unadorned compound appeared before her.

Under the lush locust tree, a man in white robes was lounging leisurely on a rocking chair. He did not rise even upon hearing footsteps.

"My Lady, we have arrived," the young Daoist said softly.

Gu Yuechan nodded slightly, her gaze fixed solely on the man in white. The corners of her lips lifted slightly as she called out in a clear voice, "Daoist."

Seeing the man in white move his fingers slightly, the young Daoist lowered his head and retreated silently.

Gu Yuechan did not notice. She lifted her skirt slightly, stepped over the threshold, and said as she walked, "I apologize for the intrusion, Daoist. I only learned today that ordinary people are not permitted to offer incense here."

The man sat up, his voice as indifferent as his gaze: "What is your business with me?"

"Has the Daoist forgotten?" Gu Yuechan walked up to him, holding the peach-wood box, and said with a gentle smile, "I have come to thank you, Daoist."

Sima Xin’s lips curled slightly: "No need."

Gu Yuechan took it as mere politeness and remained enthusiastic: "It is necessary, truly. If not for you, Daoist, I would have likely lost my way in the forest. Had night fallen, I might have encountered wild beasts. You have done me a great service."

Sima Xin said calmly, "There is no need for honeyed words."

Gu Yuechan’s expression faltered. Was she supposed to keep a cold face and say it really wasn't much of a favor?

"Does the Daoist not wish to see me? I even specially brought pastries from Xingrongju for you." As she spoke, she offered the peach-wood box. Seeing him remain unmoved, Gu Yuechan’s eyes dimmed for a moment.

It wasn't like this when they last met.

Could it be that he, too, had encountered some trouble?

"Daoist," Gu Yuechan took the initiative to open the wooden box, and the sweet fragrance of the pastries began to drift out. "Have you encountered something unpleasant?"

Sima Xin raised his eyes, his gaze moving slowly from her vibrant pomegranate-red skirt to the slender, delicate hands resting on the wooden box.

Finally, he looked at her face, as beautiful as peach blossoms.

Her lively, pretty eyes were filled with concern, as if she were truly worried for him.

"Sixth Miss Gu," Sima Xin said slowly, "If you have a request, speak plainly."

If Gu Yuechan had heard him say this at the beginning, she would have poured everything out like beans from a jar. But seeing his current attitude, she felt hesitant to speak.

Yet, if she didn't speak, wouldn't her trip today be for nothing?

Her eyelashes fluttered, and her fingers tightened around the wooden box.

"Daoist, why don't you try this peach blossom pastry first?" Gu Yuechan reached out her arm, and the green gauze shawl embroidered with gold patterns brushed against the back of the man's hand, which was resting on his knee.

Sima Xin remained as steady as a rock: "Place it on the table."

Only then did Gu Yuechan notice a small table beside the rocking chair, on which only a teapot and teacups were placed.

She stepped forward and placed the wooden box on the table, her gaze lingering for a moment on the tea set. How did this porcelain look so much like tribute ware from the palace?

But the Daoist was likely a trusted confidant of the Emperor; it was not surprising that he had tribute items.

After setting down the pastries, Gu Yuechan felt that half of her mission was accomplished, and she felt much more at ease when she spoke again: "Actually, I do have a matter I wish to ask of you."

She glanced at his expression and said, "Regarding what I told you at the hunting grounds last time, do you think there is a chance for my father to return to the imperial court?"

"I have already stated my position on this matter last time; just wait patiently," Sima Xin lowered his eyes. "If there is nothing else..."

Seeing that he intended to see her out, and not knowing if she would be able to enter again next time, she ignored etiquette and hurriedly interrupted him: "I, I have one more thing."

Sima Xin stopped, not rebuking her for her rudeness.

Gu Yuechan steadied her mind and said, "I forgot to ask last time, how should I address you, Daoist?"

She was naturally asking for his Daoist name.

"Qingxuan," he said.

Sima Xin’s Daoist name had been given to him by the old abbot of Yongan Temple. In the past, the fellow disciples who grew up with him in the temple would call him by this name. Later, no one ever called him by his Daoist name again.

"Qingxuan." Gu Yuechan repeated it slowly, looking at him with a smile in her eyes: "Then, Daoist Qingxuan, may I offer a stick of incense here?"

She took a green satin pouch from her sleeve: "My mother always restricts my spending, so I haven't been able to save much money over the years."

Sima Xin glanced at the bulging pouch in her hand, his expression unchanged.

Gu Yuechan knew that this small amount of money would naturally not move him.

"So..." she raised her arm again and took out a crimson peony pouch from her sleeve: "I secretly took out the dowry my mother prepared for me. All of this is for you, Daoist."

She suppressed her heartache and placed both pouches on the table beside him: "Although it is only six hundred taels of silver, it is all the savings I could gather. My grandfather and father were incorruptible officials, and our family assets are meager. Daoist Qingxuan, I am full of sincerity. If it is not enough, I can come every year to add to the temple’s incense money."

A dowry was naturally precious to a young woman.

Sima Xin’s gaze lingered briefly on the crimson pouch. He had not known that the Gu family had fallen to such a state that her dowry was only six hundred taels.

"Daoist Qingxuan." Gu Yuechan’s slender eyebrows drooped as she looked at him pitifully: "I don't ask for my father to hold a high-ranking position; I only wish to know if the Emperor is truly unwilling to restore my father to his original post. If the Emperor truly dislikes my father, then our family need not stay in the capital. We might as well return to Yunzhou early, so as not to end up broken and bleeding in the capital."

The more she spoke, the more aggrieved she felt. She thought of the young ladies who had been warm and polite to her at the Lishan Palace; now, they all followed behind Second Miss Xie. The kinder ones merely looked on coldly, while the snobbish ones made sarcastic, biting remarks.

"I can see that those people look down on our family," Gu Yuechan sobbed with restraint: "I don't want to keep suffering the cold shoulders of others. If the capital really cannot accommodate us, why force ourselves to stay here and lose face?"

Sima Xin’s brow furrowed imperceptibly for a moment.

"Why are you crying?"

Gu Yuechan lowered her head and said stubbornly, "I am not crying; you saw wrong, Daoist."

She was long past the age of fifteen; how could she act in such a crying, rude manner? Wouldn't that make people laugh at her?

Afraid of letting a sob escape, she bit her lip and said no more.

The courtyard fell silent, with only the locust leaves swirling in the west wind, slowly drifting down and making a faint sound on the stone floor.

Gu Yuechan stared at the yellowing leaf that had fallen beside her shoes, thinking to herself: If the Daoist still wouldn't budge, should she mention the matter of the Emperor’s heir? But her mother hadn't yet recalled who that physician was. If she brought it up now and they couldn't find the physician in the end, wouldn't that just annoy him for nothing?

Just as she was hesitating, the man’s deep, cold voice sounded.

"Within half a month, I will send someone to inform you."

Gu Yuechan was stunned for a moment before she realized that the Daoist had agreed. She raised her head in joy: "Is that true?"

Seeing him nod, Gu Yuechan was overjoyed. She clasped her hands together and bowed to him solemnly: "Thank you, Daoist. If this matter can truly be accomplished, I will certainly add much incense money to the temple every year, even if I have to pawn my jewelry and clothes."

The young woman’s red lips parted as she spoke of where her home was and how to find her. Her voice was as clear as an oriole’s, and even though she kept talking, she did not seem annoying.

The late morning sun was intense, making the hibiscus flower at her temple look even more delicate and beautiful.

After a long while, Gu Yuechan felt she had covered everything, when she suddenly remembered one most crucial thing.

"Daoist Qingxuan, you must know a great deal about the Emperor’s past, right?"

Gu Yuechan looked hesitant, and seeing that he did not refute her, she said slowly: "The late Imperial Concubine Zheng was my aunt. So, when you discuss this matter with the Emperor, please be sure to be tactful. If the Daoist is reprimanded by the Emperor because of me, I would feel very guilty."

Sima Xin looked at her calmly and said, "Sixth Miss Gu, you should leave now."

Gu Yuechan pursed her red lips and hesitated: "Then, about my father’s matter..."

"I will not break my word." Sima Xin lowered his eyelashes and ordered: "Yunfeng, take her to offer incense, then see her off."

The young Daoist in cyan from earlier reappeared. His face was gentle, and his every movement was filled with courtesy: "Sixth Miss Gu, please."

Before leaving, Gu Yuechan urged: "Daoist, don't forget to eat the pastries I brought. Perhaps your mood will be a little better."

chapters.title: Kneeling in the Ancestral Hall
chapters.content:
The only female guest had departed, and the Taoist temple returned to its usual tranquility.

A eunuch dressed in a crimson round-collared robe stepped out from the room, his gaze lingering on the low table with a complex expression.

The box containing the pastries was not tightly shut, and the fragrance stole out through the gaps, impossible to ignore.

To think someone would use such trifles to bribe the Saint, and that the Saint had actually accepted them. Could it be to give the Gu family a false sense of hope, only to deal them a heavier blow later?

Just as Xu He was silently ruminating, he saw the Saint suddenly pick up a piece of peach blossom pastry. He was about to remind the Saint that the pastries needed to be inspected before consumption, but before he could speak, the Saint paused, not bringing it to his lips.

Sima Xin examined the peach-shaped pastry in his hand. A moment later, he placed it back into the box and said, "Tell He Lin to come to Hanyuan Hall tomorrow."

He Lin was the Minister of Personnel, responsible for the promotion and transfer of officials.

Xu He hurriedly replied, "Yes, Your Majesty."

Back inside the carriage, Gu Yuechan was fussed over by her two maidservants for a long time, until she puffed out her cheeks in annoyance, causing the two to finally fall silent.

"I’m fine. It’s just a Taoist temple, not a den of tigers and wolves."

Gu Yuechan’s tone was relaxed, having completely forgotten her earlier hesitation. A smug smile tugged at the corners of her lips: "I have always been prudent in my dealings."

If the Taoist priest could bring good news, she wouldn't need to ask her mother about that physician anymore. But if the Saint truly did not intend to grant her father an official post, she would have to trouble the priest again.

By then, she would likely have to use her silks and hairpins to pay for his services.

As for what she told the priest about returning to Yunzhou—that behavior of a stray dog—she would never do such a thing.

If her father could obtain a post outside the capital, he wouldn't have to serve under the Saint’s nose, and he could fulfill his ambitions. That would be ideal.

Once a few years passed and the Saint forgot the past, they could return to the capital.

Gu Yuechan was lost in these pleasant thoughts, not forgetting to sternly warn the few who had accompanied her not to reveal a single word to her father or mother.

The coachman readily agreed, and Biwen and Qiongyu, seeing that no accidents had occurred today, had no desire to stir up trouble. If the Madam found out, she would surely punish the young mistress.

Gu Yuechan had assumed no one would ever know, so she stayed indoors for two days, fearing she might miss news from the priest.

Unexpectedly, before the news arrived, she was punished by her mother to kneel in the ancestral hall.

The prayer mat was coarse and hard; the ancestral hall was cold and damp.

Gu Yuechan knelt there, looking miserably at the generations of Gu ancestors: "It must have been that coachman who tattled. Once I get out, I’ll have Grandmother hire a new one."

"Young Mistress, you should first think about how to appease the Madam," Qiongyu said, kneeling behind her with a sigh. "Otherwise, you’ll have to stay here for three days."

Gu Yuechan was unconcerned: "When Father and Brother return, they will surely plead for me. Mother won't stay angry forever."

Her prediction was correct. When Gu Mingtu returned and learned that his youngest daughter had been punished, his face immediately showed distress. However, he knew his wife also cherished their youngest daughter and would not punish her without cause.

"She is still young. If she has made a mistake, we can teach her slowly. The weather has turned cold these past few days; if she kneels until she falls ill, won't you be the one suffering?"

A flash of heartache crossed Zheng Ying’s face, but she remained firm: "My sister-in-law came to tell me that she actually took two maids to the Yong'an Temple. What kind of place is that? How can she go there so casually? If she were not my daughter, why would I..." She paused, the corners of her eyes turning slightly red. "Why would I worry that the Saint might act against you all?"

How could she not see the hidden dejection on her husband's face every time he returned from being out?

The whole court knew that the Zheng family was a thorn in the Saint's side, and the powerful in the capital avoided them like the plague.

All of this was because of her.

Seeing her sorrow, Gu Mingtu hurriedly stepped forward to hold her shoulders, blaming himself: "It is my fault for making you worry constantly. Once Zhaozhao is married, we will return to Yunzhou for a while. The head of Qingling Academy has invited me many times, and I have no desire for an official career. It would be quite comfortable to be a teacher."

At the mention of their youngest daughter’s marriage, Zheng Ying’s eyes grew even more watery: "I fear Zhaozhao’s marriage will not go smoothly. In a few days, we shall visit the Marquis of Changping’s estate. If they intend to call off the engagement, we might as well end it now."

"But when Brother Ye saw me last time, he spoke of this matter without any intention of breaking the engagement," Gu Mingtu said, puzzled as to why it had come to this. "And Ye Erlang seems quite satisfied with this match."

Ye Erlang had passed the imperial examination before the age of twenty and was a handsome man; Gu Mingtu was quite satisfied with him.

Zheng Ying shook her head: "Madam Xu has only one son, Ye Erlang, and she surely places high hopes on him. When we first returned to the capital, the Marquis of Changping’s estate held a banquet. I saw that Madam Xu treated Zhaozhao with great indifference; it is clear she is not satisfied with this match."

She sighed: "Zhaozhao does not have a virtuous or circumspect temperament. At home, her pride and willfulness don't matter, but if she marries into another family, I fear she will suffer greatly. I have carefully questioned Zhaozhao about Ye Erlang these past few days, and I see that she has no special feelings for him—it is merely a child’s competitive nature."

Gu Mingtu had been busy running about during this time and was unaware of this.

He frowned, also dissatisfied with the conduct of the Marquis of Changping’s estate: "If Brother Ye hadn't pleaded repeatedly, Father and I would never have agreed to this marriage. For such things to happen again and again, I see that Brother Ye is a muddled man."

"How important marriage is to a young woman." Zheng Ying did not wish to dwell on the past, hoping only to do what she could to ensure her daughter’s future happiness: "If you are truly determined to return to Yunzhou, then Zhaozhao’s marriage can be decided there. I would not be at ease if she were left alone in the capital."

Gu Mingtu’s brows were locked tight until Zheng Ying added: "Do not invite trouble, lest Zhaozhao’s reputation be tarnished."

Their family could no longer withstand any more setbacks.

"As you wish, my lady," he said, bowing his head in resignation; otherwise, he would have had a serious talk with that scoundrel Ye An.

After finishing the serious business, Gu Mingtu asked about the Yong'an Temple: "Why did Zhaozhao go to the Yong'an Temple for no reason?"

"She said she went to offer incense." Zheng Ying felt a headache coming on at the thought of her daughter’s willfulness: "She thinks I am easy to fool. Her memory is not poor; how could she forget whose residence the Yong'an Temple once was?"

Gu Mingtu did not know whether he should try to persuade her.

"I have already sent Qingyuan," Zheng Ying said, rubbing her temples with her fingertips: "I have always been too lenient with her; I fear this temperament of hers can no longer be corrected."

Since Qingyuan had gone, the youngest daughter would not suffer, Gu Mingtu thought to himself, and surely by tomorrow, his wife would be unable to bear it herself.

In the ancestral hall, the warmth from the burning red charcoal dispelled the chill around the young woman.

Gu Yuechan knelt on the soft cushion, took a sip of hot tea, and said to the nine-year-old boy sitting opposite her: "Did Mother say when I can go back?"

Since her younger brother had brought charcoal, cushions, tea, and food, she knew she wouldn't be leaving anytime soon.

"Three days," Gu Qingyuan said, holding up three fingers, his young face solemn: "Sister, Mother is truly angry this time. She said that no matter who comes to plead, there will be no room for compromise."

"Hmph." Gu Yuechan puffed out her cheeks: "Mother is so heartless. Go back and tell Mother that I am languishing here, my face is pale, and I am in pain all over..."

"Sister." Gu Qingyuan interrupted her long-winded speech helplessly: "Mother won't be fooled by these things unless I bring them back untouched; only then might she believe you are truly unwell. Shall I go ask Grandmother to plead for you?"

But she had already eaten everything.

And if Grandmother came and started an argument with Mother...

Gu Yuechan conceded: "Forget it, forget it. Remember to bring me some jade dew cakes and chestnut cakes tomorrow, and also some roasted lamb to ward off the cold."

If she could get good news from the Taoist priest, she didn't mind suffering for a few days.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.content:
As the sky grew dim, the sound of footsteps suddenly echoed outside the ancestral hall.

Qiongyu, thinking it was the Madam, hurriedly tidied up the meal the young lady had finished. Although she knew the Madam must be aware that the young master had sent the food, it was still not something that should be done too brazenly.

Gu Yuechan also scrambled to kneel properly. She had just smoothed out her skirt when the visitor appeared at the door.

"Zhaozhao." A silver-haired old lady stepped over the threshold, looking at the delicate young girl kneeling on the cushion with a face full of heartache. "Your mother is too heartless; how could she let you kneel here?"

Gu Yuechan guiltily wiped the corners of her mouth with a handkerchief, turned around, and pulled a radiant smile. "Grandmother, why are you here?"

"Let Grandmother see if you've knelt until you're hurt." The old lady brushed aside the maid supporting her and, with surprising vigor, stepped forward to help her granddaughter up, examining her face closely. "Oh my, your face is all red. Have you caught a chill?"

Liu Momo, who had followed behind, glanced quietly at the charcoal brazier in the corner. The Sixth Young Lady’s rosy complexion was likely from the heat of the charcoal.

Gu Yuechan waved her hands quickly. "No, Grandmother, I am perfectly fine. It was my fault for doing something wrong, which is why Mother made me come here to reflect."

"Fine? The air here is so damp." The old lady ignored the food box, bedding, and charcoal brazier in the hall, pulled her up, and headed straight for the door. "Come with Grandmother; let’s see what your mother dares to say."

Gu Yuechan hesitated for only a moment before following her grandmother out of the ancestral hall.

"Grandmother, who told you?" She linked arms with her grandmother, walking slowly along the corridor. "It wasn't Qingyuan who blabbed, was it?"

The old lady snorted. "That boy Qingyuan is heartless too; knowing you were suffering, he didn't even come to tell me. If your Seventh Sister hadn't let it slip, I probably wouldn't have known until tomorrow. It was just a trip to the Yong'an Temple; you just won't go again next time. What kind of big deal is that to warrant a three-day kneeling punishment in the ancestral hall?"

Gu Yuechan’s seventh sister was named Gu Yueying, a daughter of the second branch’s concubine.

"So it was Seventh Sister." Since returning to the capital, Gu Yuechan had barely spoken to her. Once she knew who had leaked the news, she cast the topic aside and acted spoiled. "Grandmother, that carriage driver in the manor is truly loose-lipped and dishonest. He went around talking about his master's whereabouts. You really must replace him with someone honest, quiet, and capable."

The old lady immediately shifted her focus. "Is that so?"

"Of course. I’m afraid that in a couple of days, everyone inside and outside the manor will know I went to the Yong'an Temple." Gu Yuechan shook her grandmother’s hand, feeling aggrieved. "You must stand up for me."

The old lady doted on her most of all; how could she refuse?

Gu Yuechan followed her grandmother back to the Rong'an Hall and accompanied her for dinner, coaxing the old lady until she was beaming with joy, before finally returning to her own courtyard.

The next day, after paying her respects to her grandmother, she went straight to her parents' residence with a submissive and obedient demeanor.

Zheng Ying pretended to be annoyed for a long while as she let her daughter act spoiled and silly before her expression finally softened. "This time, since your grandmother has spoken, we'll let it be. But you must never go to that Yong'an Temple again. Do you understand?"

Gu Yuechan nodded and asked, "Mother, was it Second Aunt who complained to you?"

Zheng Ying was surprised. "How did you know?"

Gu Yuechan lifted her chin slightly, a look of pure pride on her face. "In these past few years, only Second Aunt has remained in the capital, managing the manor's affairs. In the few months since I returned, I’ve noticed that the servants in the manor always mention Second Aunt; it seems everything must be reported to her. The carriage driver is likely the same. Even though he promised me he wouldn't tell anyone, he was truly loose-lipped. He clearly doesn't hold me, the young lady, in any regard."

Zheng Ying tapped her forehead lightly. "You shouldn't be proud of this. I have already spoken to your Second Aunt about this, telling her she must not spread it further. Otherwise, I fear it won't just be our branch that suffers."
