Gu Yuechan nestled into her mother’s arms and said softly, "Mother, don't worry. Perhaps there will be good news in the manor in a few days."

If Daoist Qingxuan truly didn't want to help her, why would he bother to deceive her?

She only feared that Daoist Qingxuan would think the silver was too little and not put his heart into the task. If she had known, she should have borrowed some silver from her cousin first. Since she wasn't married yet, Mother wouldn't give her her dowry; of those six hundred taels of silver, five hundred had been slipped to her by her elder sister.

"Madam," the maid Shanyu entered the room to report. "The Marquis of Changping’s manor has sent an invitation, requesting everyone in the manor to attend a banquet on the twenty-eighth of the ninth month. This was written personally by Madam Xu to you."

Zheng Ying took the invitation from Shanyu, read it, and passed it to her youngest daughter, instructing Shanyu, "Tell the people from the Marquis of Changping’s manor that we will attend the banquet on time."

Shanyu replied, "Yes, Madam."

"Uncle Ye has been promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat. Mother, this is a good thing," Gu Yuechan said happily, looking at the invitation. "Perhaps in the future, Uncle Ye can put in a good word for Father before the Sage."

Zheng Ying’s smile, however, was faint. After waving the maids away, she spoke slowly: "Zhaozhao, Mother wants to call off your engagement with the Ye family. What do you think?"

Gu Yuechan stared at her mother, dumbfounded. "Why?"

Uncle Ye had been promoted, not demoted; why would Mother bring up breaking the engagement?

"You met Madam Xu after returning to the capital. Do you think she treated you warmly?" Seeing her purse her lips in silence, Zheng Ying knew she understood. "Zhaozhao, their family is powerful now. If you were to suffer grievances in the Marquis's manor, we wouldn't be able to support you. By then, you would be trapped in the inner chambers, sitting face-to-face with a mother-in-law who dislikes you. Under the rules of propriety, you could not defy her. Zhaozhao, could you endure that?"

Gu Yuechan was stunned for a moment before saying, "But wouldn't the Second Young Master help me?"

Zheng Ying gently stroked her daughter’s beautiful face. "Zhaozhao, you are still young; many things are not as simple as you think. How about this: at this banquet, we shall see if this Second Young Master Ye truly has the ability to protect you."

Gu Yuechan didn't understand why both her mother and her cousin were worried that Second Young Master Ye couldn't protect her. She wasn't someone who would let herself be bullied.

Besides, if she suffered grievances under Madam Xu, would Second Young Master Ye really just stand by and do nothing?

Zheng Ying looked at the confusion on her daughter’s face with complex eyes. She hoped that Zhaozhao could live a smooth life without having to rely on schemes, yet she feared that she would suffer even greater hardships because of it.

If their family hadn't fallen from grace, this marriage into the Ye family would indeed have been a good one. But now, it had become a raging fire that could easily burn one's hands.

"Zhaozhao, Mother won't harm you," she said softly. "Think about it carefully. If you have any thoughts, feel free to tell Mother."

Gu Yuechan gave a very slow "Mm."

Her engagement to Second Young Master Ye had been set for ten years. Although the incident at the Lishan hunting grounds last time had made her feel unhappy, she hadn't yet considered breaking the engagement.

Moreover, after the Second Young Master made her angry last time, his attitude in admitting his mistake was good, and he hadn't repeated it.

Mother had her concerns, perhaps because she hadn't spent time with him. Maybe at this banquet, when Mother saw the Second Young Master, she would feel more at ease.

chapters.title: Attending the Banquet
chapters.content:
The Marquis of Changping, Ye An, had been tutored for several years by the late Grand Tutor Gu, and since their families shared a marriage contract, it would be both unreasonable and unfeeling for him to exclude the Gu family from his promotion banquet.

Madam Xu, well-versed in her husband’s upright and rigid nature, harbored no desire to see the Gu family. Nevertheless, she suppressed her distaste and extended a polite invitation to them.

Old Madam Yuan of the Gu family, unwilling to endure the trouble of travel, declined the invitation, sending only a few of the younger generation to join the festivities.

On the twenty-eighth day of the ninth lunar month, the Marquis of Changping’s residence was a riot of flowers and bustling with activity.

Madam Xu sat in the seat of honor, chatting warmly with Madam He, wife of the Marquis of Zhenyuan. "This time, we owe much to Lord He’s recommendation before the Sage. I often hear the Marquis speak of Lord He, praising his tireless dedication and upright character, which have earned him the Sage’s deep trust."

"It is due to the Marquis’s own meritorious service; otherwise, the Sage would not have agreed. My father merely acted according to duty," Madam He replied with a faint smile, refusing to take credit.

She glanced at the young man standing beside Madam Xu and added, "Your second son achieved the rank of *jinshi* at such a young age. His future accomplishments will surely rival the Marquis’s. It is truly enviable—unlike that monkey of mine, who is already in his twenties and still not as steady as my second daughter."

The Marquis of Changping, Ye An, had only two sons. The eldest was born to his late wife, Madam Lin, while the younger was born to his second wife, Madam Xu. Although the Marquis of Yongan favored his eldest son, the boy lacked his father’s talent and only held an official post through hereditary privilege. Fortunately, with the support of the father of the Princess of Minghu, Prince Kang, he had managed to secure a position as a sixth-rank assistant secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

The current Sage placed great importance on the imperial examinations; those who relied on hereditary titles without exceptional achievements would likely never rise to high office.

Thus, it was only after her own son’s name appeared on the Golden List that Madam Xu felt she could finally hold her head high. Though she was a second wife, her son was, after all, the more outstanding one.

The only thing that gave her a headache was the marriage already arranged for her second son.

With the Gu family clearly in decline, marrying a Gu daughter offered her son a hundred harms and no benefits. Her eldest son had been far more calculating, climbing the social ladder by marrying a princess.

It was a pity her second son did not understand how important a good marriage alliance was to his official career.

Now, seeing that the Marquis of Zhenyuan’s household was interested in an alliance, how could Madam Xu let this opportunity slip by?

"I find your second daughter quite delightful," Madam Xu said, her smile growing even warmer. "I often think, if only she were my own daughter."

Xie Peiluo offered a shy smile. "I feel quite close to you as well, Madam."

The few understood each other perfectly, though Ye Zhengxu remained oblivious to their subtext. He stared distractedly toward the courtyard until a maid entered to report that the Gu family had arrived.

A spark of light appeared in Ye Zheng’s eyes. He bowed to Madam Xu and said, "Mother, I shall go to welcome them."

Before Madam Xu could speak, Ye Zheng had already strode out, his very back revealing his eagerness.

Madam Xu forced a smile. "The late master of the Gu family once tutored him for a time. Second Son has always kept that in mind, so he rushed off to pay his respects upon hearing they had arrived."

The marriage contract between the Gu and Ye families was no secret. How could Madam He not know? Had her second daughter not been so infatuated with this young man, she would never have allowed it. Otherwise, how could a man already bound by a contract be worthy of being a son-in-law to the Marquis of Zhenyuan?

It appeared now that this Ye Second Son was satisfied with his engagement. Madam He glanced at her daughter’s expression.

Xie Peiluo’s face remained calm. Sensing her mother’s gaze, she gave a faint smile and said to Madam Xu, "It is only human nature for the Second Young Master to be grateful for the Gu family’s kindness. It is a pity about the Gu family, though—had they not married into the Zheng family, they would not have ended up..." She sighed regretfully and left the rest unsaid.

When the Zheng clan was at its peak, how glorious the Gu family had been.

But once the new Sage ascended the throne, the Zheng family fell, and Grand Tutor Gu passed away, all the past dissipated like smoke.

New emperors bring new ministers.

Madam Xu’s heart tightened. If her second son married the Sixth Miss Gu, would he not be ruining his own future? The Marquis himself might even be implicated by the Gu household.

The Marquis of Zhenyuan’s household was different. Xie Erniang’s father guarded the southwestern fortress, her maternal grandfather served as the Minister of Personnel, and the eldest daughter was a noble consort in the palace.

If her second son could marry her, it would be hard to say who would eventually inherit the title of Marquis.

One family was like the setting sun, the other like the rising sun. There was no need to ponder which to choose for an alliance.

Since her second son refused to break the engagement with the Sixth Miss Gu, she would simply have to make the Gu family retreat in the face of difficulty.

Madam Xu knew what had happened in the past, and she knew the temperament of the Gu family all too well.

Thinking of this, Madam Xu became even more enthusiastic toward them, hinting, "Our eldest son once had a marriage contract with the Gu family, but in the end, he married the Princess of Minghu. It goes to show that whether a marriage succeeds or not depends on the wishes of the children."

Xie Peiluo’s lips curled upward, a flash of determination in her eyes.

That Gu Yuechan only had a pretty face. To think she could marry into the Marquis of Changping’s residence just by acting cute and winning Ye Lang’s favor was truly naive and laughable.

What leverage did she have now to be as arrogant as she was in childhood?

Madam He understood her daughter’s intent. Since she was determined to have this Ye Second Son, she would let her. The family could support her, and an alliance with the Marquis of Changping was, at the very least, a passable match.

Ye Zheng, who had hurried to the front courtyard, spotted the young lady he had been thinking of day and night.

However, the beautiful young lady seemed unhappy; her red lips were pursed, her thick, curled eyelashes drooping, and she stood silently beside her mother.

He smoothed his robes, walked up with a steady gait, and after bowing to pay his respects, his gaze turned impatiently toward Gu Yuechan. "Sixth Miss, what is the matter?"

Gu Yuechan glanced at the woman not far away, who was adorned with high hair and gold hairpins, chatting and laughing with the other ladies. She replied sullenly, "Nothing."

She was simply annoyed at the sight of the Princess of Minghu.

But her mother had warned her: although Prince Kang was not on close terms with the Sage, he was still a member of the royal family. She was not to be as sharp-tongued as she used to be.

If she couldn't say anything, she wouldn't.

She would rather play the mute.

But if she were expected to speak kindly to the woman who had stolen her sister’s marriage, she would rather not have come to the Ye residence at all.

Ye Zheng followed her gaze and saw his eldest sister-in-law entertaining guests, and he suddenly understood.

When they were young, Sister Yuechan would always have a cold face and sharp words whenever she saw the Princess of Minghu. He hadn't expected that years later, she still couldn't stand the woman.

Regarding the dissolution of his eldest brother’s engagement to the eldest Miss Gu, he was actually mostly relieved; otherwise, how could he have his own engagement to Sister Yuechan?

He sighed inwardly, thinking he would just have to mediate their relationship after he and Sister Yuechan were married.

Zheng Ying, fearing her youngest daughter would lose her temper, asked, "Is your mother entertaining guests?"

Ye Zheng replied, "Yes, the wife of the Marquis of Zhenyuan has brought her daughter to the banquet, and my mother is speaking with them."

Gu Yuechan, who had been fiddling with the sachet at her waist, froze. The wife of the Marquis of Zhenyuan—wasn't that Xie Erniang’s mother?

"Xie Erniang is here too?" she asked sharply.

Fearing she would be unhappy, Ye Zheng hurriedly explained, "Yes, but I have not spoken a single word to her."

Gu Yuechan smiled with satisfaction. "It is good that you haven't forgotten."

Zheng Ying listened to their exchange and understood a bit more about the Second Young Master Ye’s intentions. Her previously firm resolve to break the engagement wavered for a moment; perhaps she should wait until after meeting Madam Xu to decide.

"I haven't seen your mother in several months. Would it be convenient for you to show us the way, Second Young Master?"

"Of course." Ye Zheng could not have asked for more.

Sister Yuechan had finished her mourning period. He had already discussed with his mother that their six rites should be put on the agenda. If they could be married next year...

Ye Zheng stared at his fiancée’s fair, delicate profile, a smile flowing from his eyes.

chapters.title: Deliberations
chapters.content:
When Gu Yuechan accompanied her mother to pay respects to Madam Xu, the Marchioness of Zhenyuan and the Second Young Lady Xie had not yet left. When Madam Xu saw her, her smile faded noticeably, and the corners of her lips maintained only a perfunctory curve.

Gu Yuechan felt a slight tightness in her chest. She struggled to maintain her smile and followed her mother in performing a formal bow.

Madam Xu smiled faintly. "Madam Zheng, Sixth Young Lady, please sit and talk; there is no need for such formalities."

After the two sat down, a maid entered the room to serve hot tea.

Gu Yuechan had no heart for tea. She looked at her mother nervously twice. With outsiders present, surely Mother would not bring up the matter of the betrothal immediately.

Zheng Ying knew her youngest daughter was proud. In front of the others, she only spoke casually of mundane, daily matters.

The three ladies in the hall were all from aristocratic families. Regardless of how much they despised one another internally, their expressions remained gentle, revealing no malice.

Gu Yuechan sat properly beside her mother, saying little.

Ye Zheng had a maid bring over pastries. He personally carried the celadon bowl and plate, sat down beside Gu Yuechan, and introduced them eagerly: "Sixth Young Lady, this osmanthus cake is comparable to those from Xingrongju. Taste it and see if you like it. If you think it’s good, I’ll have someone make more for you to take back."

Gu Yuechan glanced at them but did not move her hand. She heard Madam Xu chuckle softly: "Second Young Master, could the Gu family possibly be lacking such trifles? They are not poor relatives here to beg for favors."

Ye Zheng thought he had said the wrong thing and stammered, "That is not what I meant. It’s just that Sixth Young Lady likes the pastries from Xingrongju, so I..."

"Very well, I understand your meaning." Madam Xu interrupted him, seemingly recalling something, and her face showed sympathy: "However, I hear the Gu family’s life is difficult these days. The Marquis also finds it a pity, saying how glorious it was when the eldest son of the Gu family placed first in the imperial examinations. But fate is fickle; having no official position is a minor matter, but one fears someone might whisper in the Sage’s ear, causing him to recall unpleasant past events. In the capital, one must be cautious in all things; one wrong step can lead to total ruin. Madam Zheng, the safety of the whole family is what matters most."

Upon hearing this, Gu Yuechan’s fingers curled.

Could it be so serious?

Would her request for the Daoist priest to speak well of her father before the Sage actually harm her father?

She became restless, not even noticing the deeper meaning behind Madam Xu’s words.

Zheng Ying, however, understood. After her husband returned to the capital, he had visited old friends, and all the news he received was unfavorable. Neither she nor her husband had ever intended to rely on the influence of the Marquis of Changping to re-enter officialdom.

"Indeed," Zheng Ying said with a gentle smile. "My husband also says that the climate in Yunzhou is pleasant and the people are simple. We have found it difficult to adapt to the capital. Once the matters here are concluded, we plan to move the whole family back to Yunzhou."

She looked at her daughter, who was lost in thought, and sighed wistfully: "It is just that Sixth Young Lady has a straightforward temperament, and neither my husband nor I feel at ease leaving her alone in the capital."

When Gu Yuechan heard her mother mention her, she looked up, bewildered. Why was she to be left alone in the capital?

Madam Xu did not know if this was a probe or the truth, so she feigned comfort: "Once the Sixth Young Lady is married, she will naturally be cared for by her husband's family. Madam Zheng need not worry too much."

Ye Zheng also said solemnly: "Please rest assured, I will definitely take good care of the Sixth Young Lady and will not let her suffer the slightest grievance."

Zheng Ying smiled faintly: "Let us discuss that later. Today is a banquet, and I will not speak of things that annoy others. In a few days, I will come to visit you again, Madam."

Madam Xu watched her thoughtfully for a moment. Could the Gu family really be this sensible, requiring no heavy-handed hints from her?

That would be for the best. If they could take the initiative to break off the engagement without hindering her Second Young Master’s future, she would not have to play the villain and risk discord with the Marquis and her son.

The Marchioness of Zhenyuan, sitting opposite Zheng Ying, watched from the sidelines, not interfering in their family affairs.

If the Marquis of Changping’s estate wanted to marry into their family, they should show sincerity and resolve this engagement themselves; there was no need for her to worry about it. However, the Gu family was truly laughable. Unable to make it in the capital, they were slinking back to Yunzhou, yet they still had to put on a facade, blaming the climate of the capital instead.

Because of the words of her mother and Madam Xu, Gu Yuechan was absent-minded throughout the rest of the banquet. She had no energy to deal with those who spoke with hidden barbs, which made her appear much more composed and quiet.

When the banquet ended and they were in the carriage on the way back, Zheng Ying smiled and praised her youngest daughter, then asked how the talk between her husband and the Marquis of Changping had gone.

Gu Mingtu replied: "Zhongzhi asked me what my plans were. I have already made it clear to him that we will return to Yunzhou soon. He did not agree to the idea of reconsidering the marriage, only saying that he would surely take good care of Zhaozhao."

He looked at his youngest daughter’s innocent face and said in a gentle tone: "Zhaozhao, are you reluctant to give up this match?"

"Father, Mother, why must you return to Yunzhou?" Gu Yuechan sat up straight, nervous. "Is it... is it because you fear the Sage will recall old events and it will be detrimental to our family?"

Gu Mingtu’s expression was gentle: "Zhaozhao, this is a matter for your father to consider. If you truly love the Second Young Master Ye, there is still room to discuss this marriage. The Sage is not a narrow-minded person, and we will be fine. It is just that the capital is a place of strife, and it is not suitable for your mother and me to stay here for long."

Gu Yuechan understood his meaning. Her mouth turned down, and her eyes instantly reddened.

"Father, you are still speaking up for the Sage. If he were truly magnanimous, how could you be hitting walls everywhere?" She blinked hard to force back the tears. "If the Marchioness really likes the Second Young Lady Xie, then let her be the daughter-in-law of the Ye family. I don’t care for it at all! There are plenty of good men in Yunzhou; is your daughter really lacking people who like her?"

Gu Mingtu sighed: "Zhaozhao, do not act on impulse. You are still young. The matters of the imperial court are intricate and complex. The Sage is the master of Great Jin and holds the power of life and death. Those beneath him fear him and naturally dare not risk their own safety. This has nothing to do with how the Sage thinks."

Gu Yuechan huffed: "They are all sycophants; the world is truly cold and fickle."

The young boy sitting opposite her nodded in agreement: "Sister is right."

Gu Mingtu straightened his face: "Qingyuan, do not interrupt."

Gu Qingyuan’s chubby cheeks puffed out, as if he were unconvinced, but he did not retort.

Gu Yuechan: "In any case, wherever you go, I go."

She no longer cared about the issue of face. She thought that her father must be saying this so she wouldn't worry; otherwise, why would they return to Yunzhou?

Her grandfather had said that her father had studied hard since he was young, placing first in the imperial examinations at eighteen. He was highly regarded by the late Emperor, and even her maternal grandfather, who was already a Secretariat Drafter at the time, was willing to betroth his eldest legitimate daughter to him.

The pride on her grandfather’s face at that time had not yet faded from her memory.

Returning to Yunzhou meant her father was giving up everything he had in the past.

She thought it must be because her father realized the danger in the capital; otherwise, how could he have made such a decision?

Gu Mingtu looked at Zheng Ying with hesitation: "What does Madam think?"

"Since Zhaozhao agrees, then let it be so." Zheng Ying pressed her temples to soothe the throbbing ache. "Breaking off the engagement should go smoothly. After we return, I will go and speak with Mother."

Gu Mingtu frowned: "Returning to Yunzhou was my decision; I should be the one to speak to Mother. If you go, it will only be harder to explain."

Zheng Ying nodded, not refusing her husband’s kindness.

If that Second Young Master Ye had any discernment, she would not have found it so easy to decide on breaking the engagement.

He couldn't even hear the subtext in his own mother’s words, only foolishly echoing and explaining. How could she dare to let Zhaozhao marry into such a family?

chapters.title: News
chapters.content:
Since her father had already resolved to return to Yunzhou, she would go to Yongan Temple again tomorrow, and upon her return, she would tell him everything.

Her mother had already punished her once; given that she had taken the initiative to admit her fault, surely she wouldn't be made to kneel in the ancestral hall again.

She hoped Daoist Qingxuan had not yet mentioned her father to the Sage.

But eight days had already passed of the half-month deadline. If the Daoist had already spoken, and the result was the Sage’s wrath, what would they do then?

Amidst her anxiety, the carriage passed through the long street, turned into Xingping Ward, and stopped in front of the Gu residence.

Gu Yuechan was full of worries. She waited until everyone else had exited the carriage before stepping out slowly.

Just as she placed her hand on Qiongyu’s arm and before her foot had touched the footstool, a clear, resonant shout came from afar, startling her so much she nearly missed her step.

Qiongyu was quick-witted and caught her: "Young Mistress, be careful."

"Mm." Gu Yuechan responded absentmindedly, stepped onto the footstool, and alighted from the carriage, her gaze fixed firmly on the young man not far away.

She did not recognize him, but the Daoist robe he wore was very familiar.

Everyone at Yongan Temple, except for Daoist Qingxuan, wore this type of green Daoist robe.

Gu Yuechan’s heart began to beat rapidly.

Did Daoist Qingxuan send him?

The people in front of the carriage also looked toward the young man in unison; his loud shout of "Young Mistress Gu the Sixth" was truly impossible to ignore.

Under the gaze of the crowd, the man in the green robe stepped forward composedly. After offering a polite bow, he said, "My senior brother asked me to come and inform you that the matter you requested has been accomplished. Please rest assured and remain in the capital."

For a moment, Gu Yuechan did not know what expression to wear.

This sentence meant that her father’s official position was secured. If she had heard this earlier, she would have been overjoyed.

But now... was this a blessing or a curse?

She furrowed her brows, but thinking that someone had helped her as promised, how could she look so miserable? She quickly put on a smile and returned the bow: "Thank you, Daoist."

The green-robed Daoist smiled and nodded. Having delivered the message, it was time for him to return and report.

Just as he was about to turn and leave, he heard the young lady ask softly: "Daoist, I wonder if Daoist Qingxuan will be at the temple tomorrow? I would like to thank him in person."

This was not an easy question to answer. The Sage only occasionally visited the temple to clear his mind; whether he would be there tomorrow depended entirely on the Sage’s mood.

The green-robed Daoist’s expression remained unchanged as he replied gently: "My senior brother is not often at the temple. I will convey your sentiments to him."

Gu Yuechan thought to herself that perhaps Daoist Qingxuan was constantly by the Sage’s side, which was why his whereabouts were uncertain.

"I see, then." She pursed her lips in disappointment: "Then please thank Daoist Qingxuan on my behalf. If I have the chance to see him another day, I will thank him in person."

The green-robed Daoist said: "Very well."

After he left, Zheng Ying, who had been watching for a long time, spoke coldly: "Zhaozhao, who is this person?"

Gu Yuechan carefully glanced at her mother’s face, which was as dark as ink.

She took two steps forward like a tortoise and whispered: "Mother, let’s go inside and talk."

The carriage of her second uncle’s family was not far behind them. They had just stepped down and were watching them as if they were watching a play.

She did not want to lose face in public.

"Sister-in-law, what is going on?"

Lü Yanfang’s gaze swept across Gu Yuechan’s face: "Could it be that the Sixth Young Mistress has caused trouble again? And who was that man just now? Sister-in-law, if something major has happened, you must not hide it from Mingchang and me."

Zheng Ying had already recalled that her youngest daughter had been to Yongan Temple, and since the man was wearing a Daoist robe, he was likely connected to the temple.

She gave her guilty-looking daughter a light glare, then turned and put on a smile: "We are all family; if something truly major had happened, how could I hide it from you? It is just that she was playful and left the residence without telling me. If you are worried, Second Sister-in-law, I will explain it to you in detail when we go to pay our respects to Mother tomorrow."

Lü Yanfang’s mouth twitched. Everyone knew the old lady doted on the Sixth Young Mistress the most. If they went to the old lady, even the biggest matter would likely be lightly brushed aside.

A few days ago, that coachman had merely been doing his duty by reporting the movements of the household to her, yet the Sixth Young Mistress had accused him of being meddlesome, and in the blink of an eye, the old lady had sent him away.

Even the marriage into the Marquis of Changping’s residence had been decided for the Sixth Young Mistress without any consultation, even though her own daughter, the Fifth Young Mistress, was clearly a better match in age for the Second Young Master Ye.

They were all her granddaughters, yet any good thing was reserved for the Sixth Young Mistress to enjoy.

Back when the Zheng family was powerful, she had to suppress her resentment, but things were different now. The Zheng family had fallen; what standing did the Sixth Young Mistress have to marry into a Marquis’s residence?

It was a pity her Fifth daughter was already married, otherwise, she would have fought for this match herself.

"Sister-in-law, what are you saying? Why would I be worried?" Lü Yanfang feigned a smile: "The Sixth Young Mistress has been free-spirited since she was a child. If this were nine years ago, I wouldn't say anything, but now..."

She sighed twice: "Sister-in-law, don't blame me for being blunt, but if the Sixth Young Mistress doesn't change her ways, she will suffer when she marries into the Marquis’s residence. You must be firm, sister-in-law; don't be as lenient as you were last time."

Her mother hadn't even scolded her yet, but her second aunt, not knowing the full story, had already decided she was at fault and brought up the past.

Gu Yuechan looked up indignantly, wanting to speak, but she heard her mother cough lightly, a strong warning.

The guilt that had been briefly suppressed by anger regained the upper hand, and she lowered her head again, looking apologetic.

Zheng Ying: "I have noted your words, sister-in-law. However, this is not the place for such talk. If you have any more unpleasant things to say, it would be better to wait until we are back in the residence with the doors closed."

What did she mean by "unpleasant things"?

Lü Yanfang’s expression stiffened. Truly ungrateful.

Zheng Ying had no intention of entangling with her further. After saying this, she led her people into the residence and back to their courtyard.

Once inside the main room of Jinxiu Courtyard, Zheng Ying dismissed the maids and closed the door.

Gu Yuechan stood in the hall with her eyes downcast, watching the light on the floor dim, and nervously twisted her fingers.

"Speak," Zheng Ying said, standing before her with a cold face: "What exactly did you do when you went to Yongan Temple last time?"

Gu Yuechan raised her peach-blossom-like face and smiled ingratiatingly: "Mother, why don't you sit down and have some tea? I will tell you everything slowly."

Zheng Ying did not speak, only looking at her expressionlessly.

A moment later, Gu Yuechan gave in and told her everything she had done at Yongan Temple, including how she had met that Daoist.

"The words that Daoist sent someone to tell me today must mean that Father can return to the imperial court." Gu Yuechan looked up, pitifully: "Mother, did I do something wrong?"

Zheng Ying’s eyes widened in shock. Who at Yongan Temple could possibly influence the Sage’s thoughts?

If that person was not lying, how could someone so trusted by the Sage be easily swayed by a few hundred taels of silver?

She looked at her daughter’s beautiful face, a wave of panic rising in her heart: "Did he get close to you?"

Gu Yuechan didn't understand. She blinked blankly: "Close?"

Seeing that her expression was not feigned, Zheng Ying breathed a sigh of relief: "A Daoist is, after all, a man. How could you be alone with him? If he had ill intentions toward you, it would be too late to regret it."

Gu Yuechan muttered: "The Daoist is a man of cultivation; why would he covet beauty?"

Besides, he looked full of integrity, not at all like those men who fawned over her.

When she was at the temple, he only wanted her to leave as quickly as possible.

But there was no need to tell her mother that; she only complained silently to herself.

"Status and character are not always in alignment." Fearing that her daughter would be reckless and overly trusting in the future, Zheng Ying warned her carefully: "You can know a person’s face but not their heart. In the future, when dealing with others, you must ensure your own safety. Do you understand?"

Gu Yuechan nodded earnestly.

Seeing that she had taken it to heart, Zheng Ying turned to her husband: "What do you think of this?"

Gu Mingtu was thinking silently. He had been back in the capital for half a year and had heard of many things that had happened in recent years, but he had no clue about the person his daughter mentioned.

He had been away from the capital for too long.

"The Sage’s temperament..." He paused slightly: "His decisions are not easily swayed by others."

Zheng Ying: "Do you think that Daoist is a fraud?"

Gu Mingtu could not draw a conclusion: "Perhaps that Daoist merely voiced the Sage’s own thoughts."

That would mean the Sage had likely never issued an order forbidding the Gu family from returning to officialdom.

But at this moment, no one could be certain of the Sage’s mind.

chapters.title: Reporting Back
chapters.content:
Gu Yuechan spoke weakly: "So, are we still going back to Yunzhou?"

She had originally thought that if she could see the Daoist priest tomorrow, she could ask him what the Sage really thought of their family, and whether it was as her father feared.

Unfortunately, the Daoist priest was hard to see.

Zheng Ying and Gu Mingtu exchanged glances, neither speaking.

Gu Mingchan could not decipher their silent communication and assumed they needed to deliberate.

If not now, when? Perhaps by tomorrow, Mother would have cooled off.

She gestured to her younger brother. Gu Qingyuan caught the hint and said in a clear voice, "Father, Mother, since things have changed and there is no result for the time being, why don't my sister and I head back first?"

After a brief silence, Zheng Ying nodded in agreement.

Gu Yuechan secretly gave him a thumbs-up; her younger brother was as reliable as ever.

Stepping out of Jinxiu Courtyard, she felt as if she had been granted amnesty, her entire body feeling much lighter. Yet, until the matter was settled, she feared she would worry every single day.

She couldn't help but sigh: "Little Brother, do you think Father still wants to be an official?"

Gu Qingyuan replied: "I don't know. Father hasn't said."

Studying for over a decade, placing on the Imperial Examination, and gaining great fame.

Serving as an official in the court for twenty years, with remarkable political achievements.

Did Gu Mingtu really not want to continue being an official?

Zheng Ying knew he did.

He was the man who shared her pillow; how could his thoughts be hidden from her?

In the quiet room, Gu Mingtu spoke first: "Tomorrow, I will go find Brother Ye to inquire whether there is indeed a Daoist priest named Qingxuan by the Sage's side."

Zheng Ying nodded indifferently. After a long while, she said: "If such a person truly exists, ask what kind of person he is. I am still quite uneasy about Zhaozhao."

"Mm." Gu Mingtu rested his hand lightly on her shoulder, soothing her: "Don't worry too much. Judging by that person's reply today, that Daoist priest likely has no ulterior motives toward Zhaozhao; otherwise, he would have lured her to seek him out long ago. Perhaps he was just soft-hearted for a moment and thus granted her request."

Zheng Ying let out a slow breath: "I hope so."

Calming her mind slightly, she looked up at her husband: "If the Sage truly does not intend to make things difficult for you, then there is no need to return to Yunzhou."

Seeing the surprise in his eyes, as if he wanted to say something, the corners of Zheng Ying's lips curved slightly: "Mingtu, you don't need to say anything about not wanting to be an official anymore."

They had been husband and wife for over twenty years; there was no need for many words to understand each other's meaning.

Gu Mingtu chuckled: "Nothing can be hidden from you."

He did not want her to blame herself or worry, and she was concerned that staying in the capital for too long would be disadvantageous to him. Returning to Yunzhou had become the best choice.

However, if the Sage no longer held a grudge against the Gu family, then staying in the capital was not necessarily out of the question.

But who could truly know what the Sage was thinking?

Sima Yan had entered the palace today to speak with the Sage about the princess's marriage.

The Empress Dowager did not care for offspring born to other concubines, and the Sage had not yet appointed an Empress. If a princess's birth mother were still alive, she could at least go before the Sage to request an imperial decree for marriage. But if the mother had passed away and no one brought up the marriage, it would be delayed indefinitely.

She had not expected to run into Yun Tan, dressed in Daoist robes, coming to the Yuanzhang Hall to report matters. The Sage had no intention of hiding anything and told him to speak plainly.

Listening to Yun Tan's words, Sima Yan grew increasingly suspicious.

She knew this Sixth Miss of the Gu family. When Consort Zheng was still alive, the Sixth Miss often frequented the palace to keep Ningxi company.

A girl carved from jade, she wore a smile whenever she saw anyone; few in the palace did not like her.

As she grew up, her beauty only increased. When Sima Yan first saw her, she had considered introducing her to the Sage, but after hearing of her family background, that thought faded. Later, learning she was already betrothed, the idea was cast to the back of her mind entirely.

But how could the Sage know the Sixth Miss of the Gu family?

"Sage, the Sixth Miss of the Gu family wanted to thank you in person, but I did not know when you would be visiting the Yong'an Temple, so I told her that you are not often at the temple," Yun Tan said, bowing. "Would the Sage like to see her?"

Sima Xin sat before the imperial desk, seemingly in thought.

"Sage," Sima Yan couldn't help but probe, "I know this Sixth Miss Gu. Last time she accompanied Ningxi to Mount Li, I saw that her beauty was fresh and bright, surpassing many noble ladies in the capital. I even thought of playing matchmaker, but unfortunately, this young lady is already betrothed."

The hall fell silent.

After a few breaths, Sima Xin lifted his eyelids slightly: "To which family is she betrothed?"

Sima Yan carefully observed his expression. There was no displeasure, but the Sage was a man who did not show his emotions; for him to ask even a single question was unusual.

She smiled lightly: "The second son of the Marquis of Changping's estate. The Sage might have some impression of him; he passed the spring examinations this year and is quite talented. The two are a talented pair, well-matched."

Sima Xin's expression remained calm. He rubbed his thumb against his fingers, and after a moment, said slowly: "Indeed."

This remark surprised Sima Yan. Could it be that the Sage had no other intentions toward the Sixth Miss Gu?

"What brings you here today, Elder Sister?"

Sima Yan only then remembered her main purpose. Pushing her doubts to the back of her mind, she said: "Ningxi has turned seventeen; it is time to choose a consort for her. Does the Sage have any candidates in mind?"

Sima Xin: "No."

Sima Yan had expected this and said directly: "Then does the Sage have someone to handle this matter? The Empress Dowager is at an age to enjoy her twilight years; she likely does not wish to exert herself."

"I shall trouble you with this, Elder Sister," Sima Xin said.

Sima Yan had exactly that intention. Hearing this, she nodded: "Then once the candidate for the consort is decided, I will present it to the Sage for approval."

After discussing Ningxi's marriage, she couldn't help but recall that Ningxi had come to see her a few days ago, hoping she would put in a good word for her uncle before the Sage. At the time, she had politely refused.

She would not displease her own brother for the sake of an outsider.

But at this moment, she suddenly remembered that the Sixth Miss Gu's father was Ningxi's uncle. Just now, Yun Tan only said the Sixth Miss Gu asked him to convey her thanks. What favor had the Sage done for her?

If she asked now, the Sage might answer, but he would likely not reveal a shred of his true thoughts. However, the matter of offspring could not be delayed any longer.

"Sage, last time you said you would consider the matter of offspring in two months. I wonder when you plan to fill the inner court?"

Sima Xin's expression was indifferent: "Elder Sister, I still have official business to attend to. Let us discuss this another day."

It was like this again.

Sima Yan was instantly disappointed. This was likely another one of his stalling tactics. She had brought it up many times over the past two years; when had he not brushed it aside?

Last time, he had finally relented, but not even a month had passed, and they were back to square one.

If he were not the Sage, as his sister, she would truly want to get to the bottom of it and ask him what he was really thinking.

Sima Yan closed her eyes, rose to bow, and left the great hall without saying another word.

chapters.title: Different
chapters.content:
Yun Tan had been waiting for the Sage’s reply, but until the Grand Princess departed, the Sage did not utter a single word.

He waited quietly for a long time, then could not help but cup his hands and ask, "Sage, do you wish to see the Sixth Miss Gu? If she comes to the temple to seek you again, how should I handle it?"

Sima Xin did not look up and said, "Give her six hundred taels and tell her not to come again."

That meant he did not want to see her.

He did not understand why money should be given to her, but since the Sage had ordered it, he would simply comply.

"Understood. I shall take my leave."

He had just turned and taken two steps when he heard the Emperor’s voice again.

"The wording—do not be too harsh."

Yun Tan hurriedly stopped, turned back to face the Sage, and replied, "I understand."

Walking out of the main hall, a faint smile leaked onto his gentle face. It seemed the Sage was indeed treating this Sixth Miss Gu differently. If she were not already betrothed, perhaps there would be a new consort in the palace.

He wondered when the Sage had developed such thoughts. Hadn't Yun Feng said the Sage had only met the Sixth Miss Gu twice?

As he walked down the jade steps outside the hall, pondering the reason for the Sage’s unique treatment of the Sixth Miss Gu, a hand suddenly blocked his path.

Yun Tan frowned and looked at the person obstructing him; it was a maidservant from the side of Grand Princess Lehua.

The maid withdrew her hand, bowed, and said, "Lord Yun, the Grand Princess requests your presence."

Yun Tan sighed inwardly; being summoned at this moment was surely about the Sage’s affairs.

He smiled helplessly and said, "Please lead the way."

Outside the Ding'an Gate, a carved nanmu carriage drove out from the palace gate.

The air inside the carriage was pleasantly fragrant. A maid knelt to the side, offering hot tea with slender hands.

Yun Tan took the teacup and said, "Thank you, Grand Princess."

The elegant woman in the seat of honor had a gentle expression: "Lord Yun, there is no need for such formality. The Sage trusts and values you; there are some things even I am not privy to, and I fear I shall have to rely on you in the future."

Yun Tan’s heart tightened, and he felt the teacup in his hand suddenly become quite scalding.

"I am merely helping the Sage with trivial matters. How could that compare to the blood ties between you and the Sage?"

Sima Yan’s gaze turned slightly cold: "Is that so? The Sage sent you to pass a message to the Sixth Miss Gu, yet he still refuses to fill the inner court. What do you think is the reason?"

If the Sage had intentions toward the Sixth Miss Gu, he could simply have her brought into the palace; who would dare snatch someone from the Sage?

Yun Tan said, "The Sage’s thoughts have indeed never been shared with me. The Sixth Miss Gu only went to the Taoist temple to seek an audience with the Sage once, and she does not even know the Sage’s true identity. Why the Sage granted the Sixth Miss Gu’s request, I dare not speculate."

Sima Yan stared at him quietly for a long time before letting out a low sigh.

"Yun Tan, you grew up accompanying the Sage. He is the master of Great Jin, no longer a Taoist at Yong'an Temple. You should also offer counsel regarding the matter of heirs, whether for the sake of the Sage or for the stability of Great Jin."

The Sage had experienced very little familial affection since childhood; only Grand Princess Lehua had shown him any genuine sincerity. When Yun Tan saw her in his youth, he never understood why this sister always shed tears whenever she visited the Sage.

As he grew older and wiser, he realized that the Sage was different from them—he was not an orphan without a home, but someone abandoned by his own parents.

Yun Tan lowered his head and eyes, saying, "I will do my best."

The carriage stopped for a moment, then continued on its way.

The maid tidied up the tea set used by Lord Yun. Seeing the Grand Princess with her eyes closed, lost in thought, she waited quietly to the side, not daring to disturb her.

A moment later, Sima Yan opened her eyes, her gaze filled with resolve: "At the polo match in ten days, add the Sixth Miss Gu to the list. You go and invite her personally."

The maid replied respectfully, "Understood."

Sima Yan pressed her temples and whispered, "If the Sage truly treats her differently, then..."

She did not finish her sentence. The maid sat quietly, thinking to herself that if the Sage’s treatment of the Sixth Miss Gu was truly extraordinary, then this Sixth Miss Gu’s marriage would likely be annulled.

The sun gradually dipped westward, the sunset glow staining the eaves.

Gu Yuechan sat at her desk, chin in hand, staring blankly at the yellowing ginkgo tree outside the window.

"Miss, it is almost nightfall, and the wind is quite strong. Be careful not to catch a chill." Qiongyu placed a bowl of pear soup by her side and said softly, "Shall I close the window for you?"

Gu Yuechan nodded and let Qiongyu close the window. She picked up the warm porcelain bowl, looking at the pear soup she usually loved, but it no longer seemed as sweet.

"Qiongyu, what do you think the capital is like compared to Yunzhou?"

"The capital is prosperous, while Yunzhou is leisurely. It depends on what kind of life you prefer, Miss." Qiongyu closed the window and looked at her with a smile: "Are you missing Yunzhou?"

Gu Yuechan hadn't really thought about it. The capital was far more prosperous than Yunzhou; even the styles of jewelry and clothing were more magnificent. Besides, her cousin was also in the capital.

But the capital also had its downsides.

It made people feel less happy.

Burdened with thoughts, Gu Yuechan did not sleep well. Her dreams were chaotic, and she felt listless upon waking. When she went to the Rong'an Hall to keep her grandmother company, her voice was hoarse with fatigue.

Old Madam Yuan touched her cheek with concern: "What is the matter? Are you ill?"

"No, Grandmother, don't worry." Gu Yuechan’s eyes curved slightly: "I just had a nightmare and didn't sleep well."

"Then you should have slept longer; you could have just sent your maid to let me know. Why bother coming over? You should go back and rest early." Old Madam Yuan turned to the side and instructed Nanny Liu: "Have the kitchen boil a bowl of calming soup and send it to the Sixth Miss's courtyard."

Just as Nanny Liu acknowledged the order, a light laugh sounded in the room, carrying a subtle mockery.

"Mother, if the Sixth Miss cannot sleep well, I fear a bowl of calming soup will be useless." Lü Yanfang met Old Madam Yuan’s puzzled gaze and said languidly, "It treats the symptoms but not the root cause. Speaking of which, I didn't sleep well yesterday either because of the Sixth Miss's affairs."

Gu Yuechan had been sitting lazily beside her grandmother, but upon hearing these words, her back slowly straightened.

"What do you mean by that?" Old Madam Yuan asked.

Lü Yanfang sighed leisurely: "It’s about that business at Yong'an Temple last time. This time, a Taoist actually came to the door; who knows what he said to the Sixth Miss. Yong'an Temple is the Sage’s former residence. Your mother’s status is awkward, and as her daughter, you should avoid drawing attention to yourself. How could you go there voluntarily? Isn't this inviting disaster upon our Gu family?"

Although she hadn't heard clearly what the two had said yesterday, judging by the expressions of the eldest branch, it didn't seem like anything good.

"Second Aunt." Gu Yuechan sat up straight, her lips pressed into a thin line: "By saying that, do you mean you think the Sage is holding a grudge against my mother? When my grandfather was alive, he praised the Sage for being fair and broad-minded. My mother has never meddled in court affairs, so why would the Sage punish the Gu family because of her? Are you criticizing the Sage? If outsiders heard what you just said, Second Aunt, I fear that would truly be what invites disaster upon our family."

She was truly spouting nonsense with her eyes wide open. Did she really think she was deaf to the world outside?

And this was hardly the way to speak to an elder.

Lü Yanfang’s face stiffened, but she couldn't refute it; she couldn't very well speak ill of the Sage. "Sixth Miss, I was only worried..."

"Enough." Old Madam Yuan frowned and interrupted: "It is a pity that you have lived in the capital for so many years and yet still speak with such lack of restraint."

It wasn't just today or yesterday that the Old Madam had been biased. They all knew full well why the father-in-law had retired.

Lü Yanfang dared to be angry but dared not speak, saying sullenly, "This daughter-in-law knows her mistake."

chapters.title: Settled
chapters.content:
Old Madam Yuan could easily see through the thoughts of her second daughter-in-law. The Gu family was already in a precarious state, yet she was still looking for ways to make things difficult for her own kin.

"Your eldest sister-in-law has been back in the capital for some time now. You should return the household management tokens and ledgers to her as soon as possible."

Lü Yanfang could not sit still for a moment longer. "Mother, Eldest Sister-in-law has only just returned to the capital, and Eldest Brother’s official position has yet to be finalized. If he cannot remain in the capital, all this back-and-forth will only cause chaos within the manor."

Old Madam Yuan’s expression wavered.

Lü Yanfang pressed her advantage: "Besides, Seventh Daughter is currently learning household management from me. She is quite clumsy, and I would hate for her to disturb Eldest Sister-in-law."

"Speaking of Seventh Daughter, you should also put more heart into her marriage prospects." Old Madam Yuan pondered for a moment, then spoke again, dropping the previous subject: "If there is a suitable family, keep looking. Once Sixth Daughter is married, it will be the perfect time to arrange Seventh Daughter’s marriage."

Gu Yuechan let out a secret huff. When it came down to it, she was simply reluctant to give up the power of managing the household.

Her mother was the true mistress of the clan. Had her father’s situation not been so uncertain, she would have certainly argued the point right then and there.

"I also want to find a good family for Seventh Daughter, but her circumstances are lacking compared to Sixth Daughter, who has had such a well-settled match for a long time." Lü Yanfang glanced at the young woman sitting beside her, who was as inconspicuous as a ghost. "Her appearance and demeanor are not outstanding either. Look, she has been sitting here for so long without saying a single word. I fear she will have to rely on Sixth Daughter to help pull strings in the future."

Gu Yuechan turned the jade bracelet on her wrist and said nothing.

She didn't even know if her own marriage would come to fruition; how could she worry about anyone else’s?

Old Madam Yuan, however, smiled happily: "The second son of the Marquis of Changping is much better than his elder brother."

"Indeed," Lü Yanfang agreed, following her lead. "When we attended the banquet at the Marquis of Changping’s manor last time, the second son was very attentive to Sixth Daughter. It’s just that..."

Old Madam Yuan asked, "Just what?"

Lü Yanfang replied, "It’s just that the Marchioness’s attitude was a bit cold. Mother, Sixth Daughter has been back for three months, and the Marquis’s manor has yet to send anyone to discuss the wedding date. My heart is truly worried. If the marriage were to change, where else could Sixth Daughter find such a good match?"

She added with a tone of feigned concern: "Sixth Daughter, you should also be more attentive to the Marchioness. When you need to bow your head, you must do so. Don't be like Second Daughter, who ended up with a broken engagement and caused such a huge scandal. Our family cannot afford to lose face like that again."

Gu Yuechan raised her eyes, not even bothering to feign a smile: "My elder sister’s situation was due to Eldest Young Master Ye’s lack of integrity. Why does it sound like Second Aunt is implying it was my sister’s fault?"

Lü Yanfang was about to retort, but Old Madam Yuan stopped her with a stern voice: "Enough. You have no decorum as an elder. Go back; let me have some peace and quiet."

"Zhaozhao," Old Madam Yuan turned to her granddaughter, her tone much gentler. "You go back as well. Drink your calming soup before you sleep. As for your marriage, Grandmother will handle it for you."

Gu Yuechan opened her mouth to speak but hesitated. After a moment of thought, she decided not to tell her grandmother that her mother was considering calling off the engagement.

"Granddaughter understands." She stood up, bowed, and took her leave.

Lü Yanfang took Gu Seventh Daughter and left as well. With the people gone, Rong'an Hall fell into a profound silence.

Old Madam Yuan sat quietly in her armchair for a long time before saying, "Mama Liu, do you think there will be any changes to this marriage with the Marquis of Changping’s manor?"

Mama Liu, knowing the Old Madam was worried about the Sixth Young Lady, chose her words carefully: "The second young master of the Ye family has been obedient to the Sixth Young Lady since they were children; how could he bear to break the engagement? Could the Marchioness really force a broken engagement against the second young master’s wishes? And you watched the Marquis of Changping grow up—you know his character, do you not?"

When the Second Daughter’s marriage had fallen through, it was because the Ye family’s eldest son and the Princess of Minghu had disregarded propriety and engaged in illicit relations before marriage. The Gu family had refused to let the Second Daughter marry a heartless and unfaithful man, and it was the head of the family who had proposed breaking the engagement. Otherwise, even if the eldest Ye son had caused a city-wide scandal, he would have been powerless to do anything.

"That is the logic of it," Old Madam Yuan sighed, her expression not softening at Mama Liu’s words. "But even so, Zhaozhao will inevitably suffer grievances."

How could marrying into another family ever be as comfortable as one’s own home? But given the Sixth Young Lady’s temperament, she likely would not be one to suffer in silence.

"If it were the Seventh Young Lady, I would certainly have nothing to say," Mama Liu smiled. "But the Sixth Young Lady will likely not endure it."

Old Madam Yuan thought of how she had spoken to Lü earlier and couldn't help but shake her head: "She... she is just like her aunt when she was young... Never mind, let’s not talk about it. When the Sixth Daughter’s mother comes tomorrow, I will ask her what the Marquis of Changping’s manor is truly planning."

Back in her courtyard, Gu Yuechan could not sleep even after drinking her calming soup.

She was only growing angrier the more she thought about it.

If even her Second Aunt thought this way, then outsiders would surely think so even more.

Why was it that the Gu family’s daughters were the ones at fault? If the engagement were broken, her elder sister would be gossiped about all over again.

She tossed and turned in agitation. It was clearly Eldest Young Master Ye who was shameless, depraved, and fickle.

If she could stay in the capital, she would not break this engagement. It was just a Marchioness who didn't like her—was she really going to be afraid of that?

Qiongyu stepped into the room quietly. Seeing the peach-blossom gauze curtains swaying, she knew her mistress was still awake. Thinking of the news that had just come from the Madam’s quarters, her voice was filled with joy: "Mistress, the Marquis of Changping just visited. He said the head of the family’s official position has been finalized, and in about two days, an envoy will arrive to deliver the imperial decree."

The gauze curtains were suddenly pulled open from the inside. Gu Yuechan poked her head out, looking at her nervously: "Truly? Did he say what the position was?"

"That, this servant does not know," Qiongyu stepped forward to pull back the curtains. "If you cannot sleep, Mistress, would you like to go for a walk?"

Gu Yuechan rose decisively, stepped into her shoes, and said eagerly: "Let’s go. I am going to find Mother."

Just as she led Qiongyu to the entrance of Jinxiu Courtyard, she ran into Hanyu, who was coming out.

Hanyu bowed and smiled: "Sixth Young Lady, you have come at the perfect time. The Madam just received good news and was about to send word for you to come over at lunchtime."

Gu Yuechan asked anxiously: "Is it about Father being granted an official post?"

"It is," Hanyu said, not waiting for her to ask for the specific title. "The decree appointing the Master as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue has already been sent to the Secretariat. It is only waiting for the imperial edict to be drafted and presented to the Sage for approval. The Madam ordered me to inform the Old Madam. Please, Mistress, go on in."

Before her father had resigned to observe the mourning period, he had been the Prefect of Qingzhou, a fourth-rank official. The Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue was also a fourth-rank position. As far as she knew, for a local official to be transferred back to the capital with his rank unchanged was already considered a promotion.

Gu Yuechan was overjoyed. It seemed the Sage was indeed benevolent.

Then her father and mother would no longer need to worry.

She lifted her skirts and walked happily into the courtyard.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.content:
Zheng Ying was busy instructing servants to prepare food and wine to entertain guests when her youngest daughter’s figure suddenly appeared outside the door, and in the blink of an eye, she had thrown herself into her arms.

"Mother." Gu Yuechan held her mother’s arm, her smile incredibly bright. "Father is being reinstated smoothly, which shows the Sage does not hold a grudge. Mother, you can rest easy from now on; everything will be just as it was before."

She did not specify what the Sage might have held a grudge about, but Zheng Ying knew exactly what she meant without needing to dwell on it.

Zheng Ying suddenly reached out to stroke her youngest daughter’s hair. She wanted to say that there was no need for her to risk scheming for family matters, but looking at her innocent and radiant smile, she only let out a soft laugh.

"Zhaozhao has grown up."

She had wanted to keep her daughter under her wings, shielding her from the wind and rain, but a fledgling bird must eventually fly high.

Now, it had come to the point where her daughter was worrying for her mother.

Zheng Ying’s eyes turned slightly red as she pulled her daughter into an embrace. "Yes, Mother is at ease now. This is all thanks to Zhaozhao."

Gu Yuechan nestled against her mother, her expression full of joy.

"Once Father receives the imperial decree, our family should host a grand banquet to let those people know that they all guessed the Sage’s intentions wrong."

If the official appointment were finalized, the Gu family would naturally host a banquet, but before that, they still needed to prioritize caution.

"There is no rush for a banquet," Zheng Ying said. "Although your Uncle Ye said this matter is all but certain, we should keep a low profile until it is finalized to avoid any sudden trouble."

Gu Yuechan nodded repeatedly. "I understand, Mother."

Since returning from Lishan, she had only been out twice: once to visit a Daoist priest at the temple, and once to attend a banquet at the Marquis of Changping’s residence.

She hadn't visited her cousin in several days.

Once this matter was over, she would definitely invite her cousin to the East Market to see if there were any new styles of clothing or jewelry.

Wait, she seemed to be out of money.

Thinking of this, she felt like crying. She was a pauper; even if she saw something she liked, she couldn't afford it.

If she asked her mother for money now, her mother would probably agree.

Just as she was about to speak, Hanyu, who had left not long ago, suddenly appeared at the door, hurrying into the room to present an invitation. "Madam, Young Lady, an invitation from Princess Lehua."

Princess Lehua had never had any dealings with their family; why would she send an invitation?

Zheng Ying took the invitation, puzzled. After quickly reading the contents, she shifted her gaze to her daughter, who was blinking at her. "Zhaozhao, did the Princess speak to you when we went to the Lishan hunting grounds last time?"

Gu Yuechan replied, "We exchanged a few words, but the Princess was not very warm toward me."

That was strange.

Zheng Ying read the invitation again. Why was it addressed only to Zhaozhao?

Gu Yuechan curiously stretched her head over, leaning against her mother to look at the invitation.

"The Princess is inviting me to play polo?" Gu Yuechan was first confused, then smiled happily. "Could it be that the Princess also knows that I am quite skilled at it?"

Zheng Ying gave her daughter a helpless look, closed the invitation, and asked Hanyu, "Has the person who delivered the invitation left?"

Hanyu replied, "They should still be in the Rong'an Hall. Cuiping said that after you have looked at it, Madam, please give a definite answer: will you go? If not, we should have the Sixth Young Lady feign illness, and the Old Madam will find a way to decline."

"Why wouldn't I go?" Gu Yuechan’s worries vanished, and she looked quite proud. "I have never feared anyone when it comes to polo."

Zheng Ying pondered for a moment and felt that going would be fine. Princess Lehua was known for her gentle temperament; if Zhaozhao refused, it would be even harder for her to establish herself in the capital in the future.

Moreover, she should try to trust that her daughter had the ability to handle difficult situations.

"Since it is an invitation from the Princess, how can we refuse? Hanyu, accompany me to the Rong'an Hall." Zheng Ying placed the invitation into her daughter’s palm and gently instructed, "Your Uncle Ye will be staying for lunch today, and the whole family will be present. Go back to your room first; I will have someone call you later."

Gu Yuechan nodded with a smile. "I understand, Mother."

In the Rong'an Hall, Old Madam Yuan was speaking with the woman who had delivered the invitation. Their conversation revolved around the scenery of Yunzhou, without mentioning the Sixth Young Lady once.

The woman wore a faint smile and did not urge them.

It was not until Zheng Ying entered the room that the woman stood up to greet her and asked politely, "The Princess is still waiting for an answer. Is the Sixth Young Lady feeling unwell?"

Zheng Ying said warmly, "She just caught a slight cold from the wind; she will be fully recovered in a couple of days."

The woman smiled. "This polo match is being held by the Princess specifically to help Princess Ningxi choose a consort. The Sixth Young Lady is Princess Ningxi’s cousin, so she can perhaps offer some advice. Since the Sixth Young Lady is well, we shall look forward to her presence."

These words made everyone in the room breathe a sigh of relief. So that was it.

Zheng Ying remained composed. "The Princess is truly thoughtful."

"Then I shall not disturb your residence any longer." The woman bowed with joined hands. "Farewell."

Old Madam Yuan hurriedly instructed Nanny Liu to see her out; one had to treat the Princess’s lady-in-waiting with proper courtesy.

After the woman left, Zheng Ying stepped forward and informed Old Madam Yuan about the Marquis of Changping’s visit. Old Madam Yuan was startled, thinking that something had gone wrong with the Sixth Young Lady’s marriage.

When Zheng Ying explained the purpose of the Marquis’s visit, Old Madam Yuan was stunned.

Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue—that was a fourth-rank capital official.

"Mother, it is currently just a draft decree. Whether it can be finalized depends on whether an envoy comes to the house in the next few days," Zheng Ying said, her voice softening as she saw her mother-in-law still in a daze. "But it is a good sign regardless."

After a long while, Old Madam Yuan closed her eyes, her aged voice echoing in the quiet room.

"Heaven bless the Gu family."

At last, the ancestral legacy would not be lost on her watch.

At lunch, Old Madam Yuan drank two cups of wine, a rare occurrence. Seeing his mother’s demeanor, Gu Mingtu felt a surge of emotion.

At the table, the Marquis of Changping, Ye An, was also happy for him and kept offering toasts. "I’ll pretend I never heard what you said to me last time. In a while, I’ll have Lady Xu prepare the betrothal gifts. Both the Sixth Young Lady and my second son are grown; it is time to set the wedding date."

Gu Mingtu smiled without giving a direct answer.

He still had to discuss the marriage with his wife, and ultimately, his daughter’s consent was required.

Ye An took his silence for agreement and said to Old Madam Yuan, "Old Madam, rest assured. I have watched the Sixth Young Lady grow up since she was a child. In my heart, she is no different from my own daughter. Once she marries into our family, it will be just like being in her own home. Whenever you miss her, you are welcome to stay at our residence at any time. Of course, letting the second son come back to live with the Sixth Young Lady is also fine."

These words truly touched Old Madam Yuan’s heart. She said happily, "Don't go back on your word. Don't say later that our Gu family is just raising a son-in-law."

Ye An waved his hand. "I will never go back on my word."

Gu Yuechan felt happy hearing this as well. She would be able to visit her grandmother and parents often. It didn't matter if Lady Xu didn't like her; she could often return to her maiden home and bring the second son with her.

She secretly tugged at her mother’s sleeve, showing an expectant expression.

Zheng Ying saw her daughter’s thoughts and patted her hand reassuringly. Since they were staying in the capital, this marriage could no longer be handled as they had previously planned.

Relationships in the capital were complex, and it would not be easy for Zhaozhao to find another good match.

chapters.title: The Appointment
chapters.content:
Inside the Princess’s residence, Cheng Wu reported the results of her trip to the Eldest Princess.

"When this servant arrived, the Old Madam of the Gu family did not agree immediately. She said that the Sixth Miss has been feeling unwell lately and that she must send someone to check on her recovery, so as not to let her attend while ill and dampen your spirits."

Sima Yan chuckled, "They are quite vigilant indeed."

Cheng Wu said, "Therefore, I clarified the purpose of this polo match and explained that we invited the Sixth Miss because she is a cousin of the Eldest Princess Ningxi. Only then did they let down their guard."

Sima Yan pondered for a moment and said, "It seems the Gu family dotes on this Sixth Miss quite a bit."

If the Emperor truly had designs on the Sixth Miss Gu, using benefits to lure her would likely not make her willingly approach him.

"Furthermore, the Marquis of Changping went to the Gu residence today, though I do not know for what purpose," Cheng Wu continued. "The Sixth Miss has finished her mourning period and has turned sixteen. If the two families intend to marry as soon as possible..."

Sima Yan said nonchalantly, "It matters not. They are not a family of low standing; even if they are in a hurry, they will not marry within the year."

Cheng Wu said no more, knowing that the Eldest Princess had her own calculations.

Meanwhile, inside the Marquis of Changping’s residence, Lady Xu’s pupils widened slightly upon hearing the Marquis's words: "Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue? But wasn't it said before that the Emperor was dissatisfied with the Gu family..."

"The Emperor's mind is not something we can fathom," Ye An said, sitting in a yellow pear-wood armchair with a pleased expression. "You go to the Gu residence tomorrow and settle the matter between the Sixth Miss and the Second Young Master as soon as possible. The Second Young Master is no longer young; it is not good to keep dragging this out. As for the betrothal gifts for the Gu family, we already said they would be comparable to the Eldest Young Master’s. They should be just about ready, shouldn't they?"

The Eldest Young Master was the heir to the Marquisate, and the Lady of Minghu was a member of the imperial clan; the betrothal gifts were naturally supposed to be much higher. If these gifts were not going to the Gu family, Lady Xu would have been very satisfied.

But with the person being wrong, Lady Xu felt extremely uncomfortable.

She had previously used the excuse that the betrothal gifts were not yet fully prepared to delay things once, and it would be difficult to use the same excuse again.

"Naturally," Lady Xu said with a stiff smile. "It is just that this matter has not yet been finalized, and I fear the Gu family will not be able to handle the wedding with full attention. Shall we wait a few more days?"

Ye An frowned in dissatisfaction, his gaze probing as he looked at her: "Are you dissatisfied with this marriage? I asked for your opinion when the engagement was set years ago, and you agreed to it yourself. Why do you keep delaying it now?"

If the Marquis knew she wanted the Second Young Master to marry a daughter of the Xie family, she feared she would no longer be able to interfere in this marriage.

Lady Xu hurriedly explained, "It is just that when Madam Zheng came last time, she mentioned wanting to return to Yunzhou. I was afraid that if we went to discuss it before the Gu family had settled down, it would be hard to reach a conclusion. It would be better to wait until the imperial edict is issued; once they have that reassurance, the wedding can proceed more smoothly."

There was some truth to these words.

Ye An nodded: "Very well. It is only a matter of four or five days; you prepare in the meantime."

Lady Xu agreed softly.

If not for the option of the Xie family, she could barely be satisfied with this marriage now that the Gu family was re-entering officialdom. But with a comparison, how could she be willing to give up the great tree that was the Xie family?

The imperial edict had not yet been issued, and who knew what the outcome would be? If the Emperor suppressed the appointment decree, or if officials at court submitted memorials in opposition, what reason would the Gu family have to stay in the capital?

She instructed the servant who attended to the Marquis to report immediately if there was any news from the court.

Because of this, Lady Xu was in a terrible mood for two consecutive days, but she could not show it in front of others. Under the suppression, her complexion grew noticeably duller.

The trusted nanny who served her knew her thoughts. When the night was quiet and no one was around, she whispered, "Madam, why do you worry? Even if the Marquis and the Second Young Master would not agree to break the engagement, there is still the Gu family. Have you forgotten how the Heir broke his engagement back then?"

Lady Xu certainly remembered, but this matter damaged one's reputation, and she was unwilling to use such tactics unless absolutely necessary.

She hesitated: "The Second Young Master has just entered officialdom. If it causes a big scene, I worry he will be impeached by the censors."

"For a man, it is nothing more than a romantic affair. Back then, the Heir only suffered some minor physical injuries." Seeing that she still had concerns, the nanny lowered her voice: "However, this servant has another way. If the person with the tarnished reputation is the Sixth Miss Gu, then you, Madam, will have a legitimate reason to break the engagement."

Lady Xu’s eyes flashed. In this way, it would neither damage the Second Young Master’s reputation nor allow him to hold onto hope.

It was indeed a good plan.

Three days later, amidst the secret anticipation and anxiety of the Gu family, an envoy knocked on the gates of the Gu residence, carrying the Emperor’s appointment decree.

Gu Mingtu took the decree, his fingers trembling slightly.

He recalled his father’s worries before he passed away—how difficult it was for an official who lacked the Emperor's favor to return to office after a period of mourning. Having been back in the capital for half a year, he had already prepared himself to pin the family’s prosperity on the next generation.

Who could have expected that he would receive an imperial decree?

At this moment, he was exceptionally grateful for the Emperor’s great grace and secretly vowed to serve the imperial court with all his might.

Seeing her father standing still, Gu Yuechan asked in confusion, "Mother, what is wrong with Father?"

"He is probably just too happy," Zheng Ying smiled. "It is fine, he will be back to normal in a couple of days."

Rarely seeing her father so composed, Gu Yuechan pursed her lips and smiled, leaning toward her mother to whisper, "Father looks so silly."

Zheng Ying patted her daughter’s shoulder, also lowering her voice: "Don't let your father hear you; he cares about his face."

Gu Yuechan nodded with a smile.

After giving the envoy a tip and politely seeing him out, Old Madam Yuan turned back, glowing with energy. Seeing her son’s eyes reddening—looking even less composed than when he first entered officialdom—she couldn't help but click her tongue in disdain: "Look at you, over forty years old and not as steady as Zhaozhao."

Gu Mingtu felt ashamed and bowed: "Mother, please forgive me. It is just this once."

"Enough, go back inside." Old Madam Yuan stepped forward and took Gu Yuechan’s hand: "This time, we owe it all to Zhaozhao. Last time, you were so heartless as to make her kneel in the ancestral hall. If she hadn't asked someone to put in a good word before the Emperor, would the Emperor have even remembered you?"

These words made Gu Yuechan feel a bit embarrassed: "Grandmother, actually, it is not entirely this granddaughter's credit. Father has been an official for many years; if the Emperor were not satisfied with Father, why would he appoint him as the Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue?"

Old Madam Yuan smiled and glanced at her son: "Look, how filial Zhaozhao is, even knowing how to speak up for her father."

Gu Mingtu held the decree, the smile in his eyes deepening: "Indeed, Zhaozhao has always been sensible and well-behaved."

Lü Yanfang, who had been watching from the side, rolled her eyes in secret. If the Sixth Miss was a sensible and well-behaved woman, then there were no spoiled or willful young ladies in the entire capital.

Since her brother-in-law had been appointed as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, she feared that her mother-in-law would soon order the management of the household to be returned to her sister-in-law.

She glanced at her husband with dissatisfaction; if he could be more capable, would the first branch have been allowed to hold such power for so many years?

Gu Mingchang did not notice her gaze and was still smiling as he offered congratulations: "It is truly a turn for the better. Brother, I am truly happy for you. When the Eldest Young Master returns, I will have to ask you for some guidance."

"We are family, no need for such formalities." As the head of the Gu family, with the family’s future tied to him, mentoring the younger generation was his duty.

The Eldest Young Master of the Gu family was the eldest son of the second branch, and only then did Lü Yanfang realize that their family would still have to rely on the first branch in the future.

She hurriedly put on an exaggerated smile: "Then shouldn't our family host a banquet? Sister-in-law, I am quite unfamiliar with these matters; it is still best for you to handle it. I will personally deliver the tally and the account books to Jinxiu Courtyard in a while."

Gu Yuechan recalled the look on her second aunt's face just a few days ago, and seeing her attitude now, she found it quite ironic.

However, she felt she was no longer a girl who hadn't seen the world, so she only curled her lips slightly and said nothing biting.

Zheng Ying did not decline politely either. She hadn't bothered to argue before only because she felt they were highly likely to return to Yunzhou.

chapters.title: Amusement
chapters.content:
The once-deserted Gu residence gradually began to bustle with activity from that day on.

The former students of Grand Tutor Gu arrived one after another to request an audience, and Gu Mingtu did not turn them away.

While Gu Yuechan was writing invitations in her mother’s room, she looked at the names on the list and grumbled with dissatisfaction, "Why does Father still have to associate with those ungrateful people?"

"Seeking advantages and avoiding harm is an instinct. They have their own families and friends, so naturally, they won't easily put themselves in danger. There are no perfect people in this world; if you demand too much, you will easily find yourself isolated and helpless," Zheng Ying explained patiently. "Zhaozhao, being too rigid makes one prone to breaking. In the imperial court, enemies and friends are not absolute. In the future, when you are the one in charge, you cannot associate with people based solely on your likes and dislikes. Do you understand?"

Gu Yuechan understood, but she felt it was truly unbearable. She said deliberately, "I don't want to understand. I only know that I will be good to those who are good to me, and I will ignore those who don't like me."

No one knows a daughter better than her mother; how could Zheng Ying not see through her thoughts?

Zhaozhao had never managed a household before, so there was no need to rush. She would explain it to her in detail when she encountered such situations in the future.

The date for the banquet was set for the ninth day of the tenth month, exactly one day after the polo match.

Gu Yuechan had originally wanted to go to the Princess's residence to spend a few days with her cousin and ask what kind of man she actually liked, so she could carefully select one for her. However, Zheng Ying intended to test whether she had forgotten the etiquette for hosting guests, so she kept her by her side for several days.
