It wasn't until the day before the polo match that Gu Yuechan regained her freedom.

Taking Qiongyu and Biwen, along with the twenty taels of silver her mother had given her, she felt like a bird released from a cage and went off to find her cousin for some fun.

The East Market of the capital.

This place was crowded with shops and gathered rare treasures from all over the Great Jin; it was the most frequent place for high-ranking officials and nobles to seek entertainment.

Most of the rouge and hairpins Gu Yuechan used were purchased here.

However, she hadn't come out today with the intention of buying rouge or hairpins. She had to save half of these twenty taels to give to the Daoist priest the next time she had the chance to see him.

He had done her such a great favor that she must keep her promise to bring him silver every year.

Inside the Jingwen Pavilion, after Sima Yu finished listening to her cousin, she asked, "So, you only have twenty taels of silver on you in total now?"

Gu Yuechan replied dejectedly, "Cousin, it's ten taels."

Sima Yu: "…Did Aunt not reimburse you for those six hundred taels?"

Gu Yuechan shook her head. "Mother said she added it to my dowry list." She rested her chin on her hand and sighed. "Mother said that in the officialdom, my behavior is called bribery. Perhaps Mother is afraid that I will do something like using silver to bribe people again, and she also said that my elder sister is not allowed to subsidize me privately in the future."

Sima Yu nodded in agreement. "Aunt’s concerns are not without reason. I thought you would at least inform me; I didn't expect you to go to the Yong'an Temple with just a maid and a carriage driver. Fortunately, that Daoist priest had no malicious intent."

"Cousin, I know I was wrong." Gu Yuechan looked at her pleadingly. "Mother has already punished me."

The matter had passed, and there was no use dwelling on it.

"I remember the Daoist priests at Yong'an Temple are all of the 'Yun' generation," Sima Yu pondered for a moment. "I have never heard of a 'Qing' generation."

"My father said he asked Uncle Ye, and indeed, he has never heard of a Daoist priest named Qingxuan," Gu Yuechan speculated. "Perhaps he used a fake name because he was afraid of damaging his reputation. Regardless, he helped me, so I will just pretend I don't know."

She suddenly thought of the polo match tomorrow and whispered teasingly, "Cousin, what kind of gentleman do you actually like? Have you set your sights on anyone? I..."

"Master Dou, are you going to play polo tomorrow as well?"

A hearty male voice suddenly rang out from outside the door. Gu Yuechan stopped speaking and looked toward the closed door.

"Master Xu, I am indeed going tomorrow." The other person's voice was gentler; he must be the one addressed as Master Dou.

"If it weren't for the fact that Princess Lehua's invitation is hard to decline, I would never want to go," Master Xu scoffed. "What if I were actually chosen by Princess Ningxi? That would be a disaster."

"Watch your words."

"You are still as cautious as ever. Let's go, come with me to the private room I booked to drink? It's on the second floor. I even invited a lady from the Yunxiang Pavilion to sing today. Master Qin the Third and Master Fan the Second are there too. We were just saying that we must keep a low profile tomorrow; if we stand out too much, it will be a big trouble."

Gu Yuechan no longer cared how the other person replied. She stood up abruptly. This so-called Master Xu had such high airs; she wanted to see what kind of person he was to have such a big mouth and dare to look down on her cousin.

"Sit down." Sima Yu pulled her sleeve. "What are you getting so worked up about?"

Gu Yuechan pointed a finger. "I'm going to see what that piece of trash outside looks like."

"And then what?" Sima Yu said calmly. "Do you intend to beat him up?"

Gu Yuechan thought to herself, why not? She could have someone put a sack over his head so he wouldn't know who did it.

"What he said is the truth," Sima Yu looked at her helplessly. "Do you think everyone is fighting to be a Prince Consort?"

She was not close to the Emperor, and being her Prince Consort would only mean ruining one's official career in vain while being bound by rules. Naturally, the gentlemen from noble families would want to avoid it.

After this short delay, the conversation outside had vanished; the two gentlemen must have gone off together to drink.

Gu Yuechan sat back down in defeat and muttered, "Anyway, in my heart, only those who are unworthy of my cousin exist."

"Alright, I'm not even upset." Sima Yu chuckled when she saw her pouting. "Don't you like the hairpins from Fuyu Pavilion? I'll pay today, you can pick whatever you want, how about that?"

Gu Yuechan: "I don't want to."

Clearly, that man had belittled her cousin, but not only was her cousin not angry, she was even trying to comfort her.

Her cousin was such a good person; those men were the ones unworthy of her. She had noted those gentlemen down. She would find a chance to recognize their faces later, and tomorrow she would let them know that their worries were truly unnecessary—her cousin wouldn't look twice at them.

"Then don't go back on your word," Sima Yu laughed. "Your ten taels of silver won't be enough to buy the gold and jade hairpins there."

Gu Yuechan hesitated for a moment, then refused with great integrity.

"Cousin, you should at least know who they are. Even if you don't want to make things difficult for them, you can at least avoid picking them." She blinked and looked at her expectantly. "Don't you think so?"

Sima Yu felt a slight warmth in her heart. "Then what do you want to do?"

Gu Yuechan leaned close to her and whispered her plan.

A moment later, Sima Yu nodded. "Only look at their faces; don't do anything else."

Gu Yuechan: "Don't worry, Cousin, I know my limits."

chapters.title: Why
chapters.content:
The next day, the sky was clear and the clouds were soft.

The sport of polo was immensely popular in the Great Jin, and there were countless polo fields within the capital, but the most spacious and luxurious one was located right beside the Imperial City.

On a raised platform over a zhang high, maidservants wove between the various seating areas, topping up tea and wine for the guests.

Gu Yuechan followed behind Sima Yu and took her seat under the guidance of a maid.

She glanced at the main seat nearby, which was still vacant, and whispered, "Cousin, do you think the maid might have gotten my seat wrong?"

Having assisted her mother with the preparations for a banquet the day after next, she was well-versed in the rules of seating arrangements. Given her current status, she shouldn't really be sitting right next to her cousin.

"I shouldn't think so," Sima Yu said with a smile. "Perhaps Eldest Sister arranged it specifically. Didn't she say you were invited to help me keep an eye out? How could you help me choose if you aren't sitting by my side?"

Hearing this, Gu Yuechan felt it made some sense. Princess Lehua was truly thoughtful.

Since it was about choosing a husband for her cousin, she was reminded of the man who had spoken so arrogantly the day before. The private rooms on the second floor of Jingxiu Pavilion were limited, and since they had hired musicians, it wouldn't be hard to find them. They only needed to have someone keep watch on when they left their room, and then they could go out themselves to get a clear look at those men.

Her gaze swept across half the area, suddenly fixing on one spot, a cold sneer appearing on her lips.

That Master Xu, dressed in a sky-blue round-collared robe, was leaning against the railing, chatting and laughing with the gentlemen beside him.

He looked so ordinary, yet he had the audacity to say he was afraid her cousin might take a fancy to him. He must have covered all the bronze mirrors in his home with thick cloth, unable to see his own reflection at all.

"Hey, the young lady next to Princess Ningxi keeps looking over here," the Third Young Master Qin whispered to Xu Yi. "I wonder whose daughter she is."

Gu Yuechan had not been back in the capital for long, so not many people knew her. But because she had arrived with Princess Ningxi and was so stunningly beautiful, any gentleman who noticed her couldn't help but take a few extra looks, and Third Young Master Qin was no exception.

He hadn't expected her to look in their direction, but why was she looking at Xu Yi? Did they know each other?

Hearing his words, Xu Yi turned his head to look. When he met the young lady's gaze, he was stunned for a moment. Her eyes were like clear water, and her beauty was as bright as the midday sun.

How had he never seen such a beautiful woman before?

Unfortunately, the young lady seemed to be shy; seeing him look over, she hurriedly lowered her head to drink her tea.

Xu Yi couldn't help but feel secretly pleased. She must have heard of his talent, he thought. He just didn't know whose daughter she was; since she could sit beside the Princess, her family background was likely not low.

If she were of a virtuous temperament, it wouldn't be impossible to give her a chance...

"Princess Lehua has arrived."

The announcement suddenly rang out, interrupting Xu Yi's thoughts. Everyone present hurriedly bowed in greeting.

Gu Yuechan also set down her teacup and rose to bow. As a gentle "Rise" was spoken, a gold-embroidered dress brushed past her side, pausing for a heartbeat—or perhaps that was just her imagination.

"Everyone, be seated. No need for such formalities." Sima Yan sat in the main seat and glanced at her younger sister. "Ningxi, you have always been good at polo. Why don't you lead a team and choose your players to go down to the field?"

Sima Yu looked troubled. "Eldest Sister, it is easy for me to play, but if I choose the players and happen to pick someone who isn't good at polo, winning or losing is a small matter, but if they were to get injured..."

"Then choose a few you know well. If there aren't enough people, I will add some," Sima Yan said.

Only then did Sima Yu seem to breathe a sigh of relief. "Then I am reassured. Let Gu Liuniang accompany me, and I will trouble Eldest Sister to choose the others."

Choosing only one, and a woman at that.

Sima Yan’s brows twitched slightly. Was Ningxi lacking a candidate she favored, or was she being overly cautious?

She calmly glanced at the Gu Liuniang whom Ningxi had mentioned. Unlike the bright and agile nomadic-style clothing she had worn at the hunting grounds last time, today she was dressed in a sky-blue cross-collared jacket and skirt, appearing much more composed.

That face, however, was as eye-catching as ever.

She shifted her gaze to Sima Yu and said gently, "Since you are unfamiliar with them, I will temporarily choose a few for you. See how they play; if you think they are good, you can invite them to play together again next time."

Sima Yu smiled. "Thank you, Eldest Sister."

Sima Yan took her younger sister's marriage prospects quite seriously; she had personally selected the guest list, and picking players now was easy for her.

She mentioned a few names unhurriedly, including both men and women. As she spoke, those she named all stood up to accept the order.

"Your Highness," Cheng Wu reminded her in a measured tone, "you have chosen seven people; that is one too many."

Sima Yan frowned slightly, as if pondering who to leave behind. Finally, her gaze fell upon the woman who seemed to be in a daze. "Gu Liuniang, Ningxi is familiar with you. Why don't you stay here and watch with me instead?"

Gu Yuechan had been thinking about how none of the Xu family seemed to be among those Princess Lehua had mentioned. Hearing the Princess address her suddenly, she couldn't help but be startled.

"That works too." Seeing her cousin dazed and fearing she might displease the Eldest Princess, Sima Yu hurriedly accepted on her behalf and gave her arm a nudge. "Then, Cousin, you can wait until the next round."

Gu Yuechan realized what was happening and replied, "Yes, Your Highness."

The eight people were divided into two groups and went down to the field. Before long, several graceful figures appeared on the polo field.

Gu Yuechan watched the people galloping on horseback intently, but none of them seemed particularly outstanding in their bearing.

"Young Lady Gu."

Gu Yuechan looked up at the woman who had appeared beside her seat at some point.

"This is lychee wine," Cheng Wu said, holding a jade wine ewer and filling the empty cup on her table. "It is sweet and does not intoxicate. Please, have a taste."

Gu Yuechan rarely drank, but since this was the Princess's maid, it must have been the Princess's order. Although she didn't know why the Princess was being so close to her, her cousin's marriage depended entirely on Princess Lehua...

A wine that didn't intoxicate—a little bit should be fine.

She smiled softly. "Thank you."

She then picked up the cup, pulled back her sleeve, and drank the wine. It was indeed as the woman had said: sweet, and she felt no sign of intoxication.

Seeing her posture was elegant and proper, Sima Yan was pleased and said kindly, "Young Lady Gu, come and sit beside me."

Gu Yuechan could hardly refuse. Cheng Wu hurriedly had a chair placed next to the main seat. After Gu Yuechan sat down, she filled her cup again.

Sitting beside someone she wasn't familiar with, Gu Yuechan felt a rare trace of nervousness. Subconsciously, she picked up her cup and slowly finished it.

Sima Yan watched the polo field for a moment and said gently, "Young Lady Gu, do you think anyone on the field plays polo well?"

Her makeup was magnificent, yet her expression was gentle and kind, making it difficult for anyone to be on guard.

Gu Yuechan’s eyelashes fluttered. She bit her lip sluggishly and said, "No, none of them are as good as me."

Cheng Wu, standing beside Princess Lehua, raised her eyebrows imperceptibly. This Young Lady Gu was certainly blunt.

Sima Yan also looked over, noticing that the girl's jade-white face was gradually flushing with a soft, rouge-like red, as if she were drunk.

Was this Gu Liuniang’s tolerance for alcohol really so poor?

She looked thoughtful, then suddenly said softly, "I heard your father was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue. Have you gone to thank that Daoist priest?"

Gu Yuechan shook her head. "Not yet."

"Why not?"

"It... it was that Daoist priest who brought the message who said..." Gu Yuechan furrowed her brows, her brain, soaked in wine, briefly returning to clarity.

The person asking her was Princess Lehua.

Why would Princess Lehua know about her going to find the Daoist priest?

chapters.title: Wanting to Win
chapters.content:
"Don't be afraid." Sima Yan noticed her nervousness and said in a gentle tone, "It is not easy to get a few words out of him. I am simply curious, how did Mistress Gu manage to persuade him?"

Gu Yuechan bit her lip lightly, struggling to weigh how she should answer.

She couldn't say it was six hundred taels. Although that wasn't a large sum of money, it didn't sound good; it would make the Daoist priest seem like a greedy person.

"The Daoist priest is kind-hearted. He happened to hear of my worries, felt pity, and offered a few words of comfort. Later, I gifted him a box of pastries, and he agreed to put in a word for me before the Saint."

She gave a soft smile. "The Daoist priest is a good man."

Kind-hearted, pity...

Sima Yan’s gaze grew even warmer as she looked at her. Even when her younger brother was a child, he wouldn't have been swayed by a box of pastries.

"So that is how it was," she said warmly. "Is the lychee wine good? If you like it, I shall have someone bring some back for you to enjoy."

Gu Yuechan breathed a sigh of relief, and the slight tipsiness she felt began to dissipate.

"It is delicious. Thank you, Your Highness."

Although their conversation was quiet, their friendly and laughing demeanor was seen by everyone on the high platform.

Xu Yi asked the young Master Qin beside him in a low voice, "The Gu family—could it be that family?"

"The Gu family that has ties to Princess Ningxi, which other one could it be?" Young Master Qin lowered his voice. "Isn't it the family of the newly appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue?"

Xu Yi sighed, "What a pity for this Mistress Gu."

Such a delicate and beautiful young lady, yet she came from the Gu family. Although the Saint did not seem to loathe the Gu family as they had speculated, and the Princess was currently being very kind to Mistress Gu, if in a few years the Saint recalled old grievances and felt displeased, the downfall of the Gu family would be nothing more than a passing thought for the Saint.

To form a marriage alliance with them was still too risky.

Young Master Qin saw through his thoughts and scoffed, "Don't pity her. This Mistress Gu is already betrothed to the second young master of the Changping Marquis's estate."

The second young master of the Ye family had some reputation in the capital. Born into a Marquis's estate, he had also passed the imperial examinations at a young age and was gentle and polite to others. Xu Yi's father had even envied the Marquis of Changping, saying he had a worthy successor.

Xu Yi didn't think he was any worse than the second young master of the Ye family; the man just had better luck and happened to guess the exam questions correctly.

But if he were to say the Ye family's second young master was worse than him, he couldn't bring himself to say it.

Xu Yi looked embarrassed and lowered his head to drink.

On the polo field, the match between the Blue and Red teams was nearing its end.

The Red team, where Princess Ningxi was, was trailing behind. Seeing that the Blue team only needed one more goal to win, Gu Yuechan could no longer sit still.

Hindered by the fact that the person beside her was Princess Lehua, whom she didn't know well, she didn't suggest that the two people dragging her cousin down should leave the field.

Sima Yan, however, noticed her anxiety and asked with a smile, "You don't want Ningxi to lose?"

Gu Yuechan hesitated for a moment and nodded. "Two people on the Blue team are extremely skilled at polo."

No sooner had she finished speaking than a man on the Blue team successfully hooked the red wooden ball, swung his mallet, and passed the ball to a woman near the goal. Unsurprisingly, the Blue team scored another goal.

The outcome was decided.

"It seems there is nothing to be done about this match." Sima Yan knew she likely wanted to play, so she said in a warm tone, "Mistress Gu, you shall play in the next match. I would also like to see how well you play polo."

Upon learning she could play, Gu Yuechan was happy at first, but then she suddenly remembered what she had said after drinking and felt a wave of pressure.

Even if she truly felt those people didn't play as well as she did, how could she have said it out loud?

It would have been fine in front of her father and mother, but saying it in front of the Princess made it seem like she was incredibly arrogant.

It turned out her mother was right not to let her drink.

With an embarrassed expression, she lowered her head and said, "I will do my best."

On the polo field.

The Lady Liu who had just lost the ball said apologetically, "I am not very good at polo, not as good as Lady Zhao on the other side."

Sima Yu noticed her cousin walking toward them and knew she was likely anxious from seeing her lose. She said to Lady Liu, "It is fine, it is only one match. If you are tired, go back to your seat and rest."

Lady Liu breathed a sigh of relief and dismounted.

Just as she was about to recommend a lady more skilled than herself, she heard footsteps behind her, followed by a clear, sweet voice.

"Cousin, should I ride this horse?"

Lady Liu turned around to look at the speaker.

It was Mistress Gu, the cousin of Princess Ningxi.

"Yes," Sima Yu nodded slightly and said, "Lady Liu, leave this horse to my cousin."

Lady Liu looked at the slender, graceful young lady before her. Her hand, holding the reins, did not move. This Mistress Gu looked so delicate and soft—could she really play polo well?

Gu Yuechan didn't know what she was thinking. She stepped forward and patted the brown horse she was holding. "It's a pity my 'Liuyu' isn't here, but this horse is not bad either."

It should be a fine breed.

She looked up and smiled. "Lady Liu, give it to me."

"Very well." Lady Liu slowly released the reins and handed her the mallet, unable to help but urge, "Be careful."

Gu Yuechan blinked. This Lady Liu was terrible at polo, but she was thoughtful, so she would temporarily forget that this person had caused her cousin to lose the match.

"Thank you."

She took the mallet and mounted the horse with a nimble motion.

"Cousin, are they going to swap players?" Gu Yuechan sat on the horse and looked at the four members of the Blue team who were chatting and laughing. "When I win in a moment, don't say I'm bullying them for lacking stamina."

The match had ended, and they were not far away; Gu Yuechan's words reached everyone on the field without obstruction.

The four members of the Blue team: "..."

What incredible confidence.

Lady Zhao sized her up and chuckled. "Mistress Gu, wait until you win before saying such things. If you lose in a moment, don't come crying."

"Mistress Gu has just arrived in the capital, so it is understandable she would say such things," the second young master of the Fan family said, showing chivalry. "Lady Zhao, it is only a game, why take it so seriously?"

This fellow couldn't stop looking at a beautiful woman. Before Lady Zhao could offer a sarcastic retort, Gu Yuechan spoke first: "You should take it seriously, at least then you'll lose with dignity."

The second young master of the Fan family thought this Mistress Gu was truly pitiful and cute, and replied nonchalantly, "I will certainly be serious."

An incense stick of time later.

The palm of the second young master of the Fan family, holding the mallet, began to sweat. He looked at the high platform, where three red flags had already been planted, and gritted his teeth.

It had been so long, and they hadn't scored a single goal.

This Mistress Gu had excellent horsemanship, moved with agility, and her strikes were extremely precise. Ordinary people couldn't take the ball from her at all. In the last match, one could say it was back-and-forth, but now they were being suppressed by a young lady. It was truly a great humiliation.

"It seems this Mistress Gu did not speak falsely."

Sima Yan looked at the incomparably bright young lady under the warm sun and said softly, "Awu, look, how many men would not like such a young lady?"

Cheng Wu stood respectfully by her side, her voice low and firm, "Indeed, Your Highness."

chapters.title: Gifts
chapters.content:
The second match naturally ended with a victory for the Red Team.

Lady Zhao’s expression was unsightly as she glanced toward Fan Erlang: "Did you truly give it your all just now?"

Fan Erlang’s mouth twitched. Unwilling to admit that he was inferior to a young lady, he simply remained silent.

"Tsk." Lady Zhao turned her face away in disdain. "If your younger brother, Fan Sanlang, were here, we certainly wouldn't have lost."

Fan Erlang snorted, though he knew this was true.

"It’s a pity he is on duty today..."

"Oh? Fan Sanlang?" Lady Zhao looked toward the main seat on the high platform and said with pleasant surprise, "Fan Erlang, go quickly and swap your brother in. I won’t hold it against you whether you didn't try your best or if you’re just truly useless."

Fan Erlang looked over and saw that the man in the jujube-red round-collared robe standing beside the Grand Princess was indeed his third brother, Fan Yuelin.

Why had he come?

"Grand Princess," Fan Yuelin said, presenting a brocade box. "As you instructed, this is the prize for the polo match that the Sage requested. The Sage ordered me to deliver it to you."

Cheng Wu stepped forward to receive it, then opened it and presented it to the Grand Princess.

Sima Yan took a glance; it was a scroll of a painting, presumably by a famous master.

She raised her hand, signaling Cheng Wu to put it away.

It seemed the Sage was unwilling to come over.

"Grand Princess," Fan Erlang hurried onto the high platform and bowed. "May I have my third brother take my place in the match?"

Sima Yan replied with disapproval, "It is merely for amusement; why be so concerned with winning or losing?"

Fan Yuelin was the legitimate second son of her uncle, the Duke of Ping. He possessed the greatest talent for martial arts, and her uncle had high hopes for him, having long ago stated that he had no intention of marrying a princess. Why let him show off at this polo match?

"It is Lady Zhao who insists I come," Fan Erlang sighed helplessly. "I will go and tell her now."

Fan Yuelin laughed. "Second Brother, it is no shame to lose. That young lady truly has superb skills."

Fan Erlang shot his third brother a sidelong glance and walked away, dejected. It would have been better if he hadn't tried to comfort him.

Upon learning that Fan Sanlang refused to play, Lady Zhao was extremely disappointed. Even after changing players, they still lost the third match.

Seeing that it was nearly noon, Sima Yan ordered them to come up to rest and handed the prizes prepared by the Sage and herself to Ningxi.

Ningxi consulted with the other two and gave the items to Gu Yuechan; without her, they would not have won.

When Gu Yuechan saw that one of the prizes was a landscape painting, she tried to decline it. She was not skilled at appreciating art, and wouldn't it be a waste to give it to her?

It wasn't until her cousin whispered in her ear that this painting could be sold for a lot of silver that she happily accepted it.

She could give it away as a gift later.

The luncheon was held in Fanglin Garden, featuring a winding stream with floating wine cups—elegant and refined.

Grand Princess Lehua was indeed the Sage’s own sister; usually, only the Empress Dowager and the Sage could hold banquets here, but because Grand Princess Lehua wished to use it, the Sage easily granted permission.

Gu Yuechan had played two matches of polo, yet she did not feel tired; on the contrary, she felt much more spirited.

The Great Jin was open-minded, and young gentlemen and ladies toasted and chatted with one another without restraint.

Several gentlemen came to toast Princess Ningxi and took the opportunity to toast Gu Yuechan as well.

Gu Yuechan knew her tolerance for alcohol was poor, so she used tea as a substitute. Lady Zhao noticed this and couldn't help but mock, "Lady Gu actually doesn't drink? I couldn't tell. Could it be that you don't dare to?"

The hot-blooded Gu Yuechan could not stand being provoked.

In any case, her cousin was here; even if she got drunk, it wouldn't matter. She could just sleep at her cousin's mansion.

She ordered a maid to fill her cup with grape wine, tossed her head back, and drank it down with flair. She then held the empty cup out to Lady Zhao with a provocative smile: "I must leave Lady Zhao some face, so you don't lose in every aspect."

Lady Zhao came from a family of military generals and was not one to back down. She simply sat down beside her, and the two began to compete in their drinking capacity.

Just as Sima Yu had finished offering a word of advice, Cheng Wu walked to her side, saying that Grand Princess Lehua was looking for her.

She had no choice but to leave her maid, Chunli, behind to keep an eye on them.

Chunli was unable to keep watch; by the time Sima Yu returned, both ladies were already flushed, their eyes hazy.

Sima Yu angrily pushed her cousin's shoulder, only to be hugged around the waist by the drunkard, who murmured, "Cousin, I... I won't go home today. Mother will... will scold me. You have to help me."

She still had a shred of reason left.

Sima Yu sighed, told Chunli to clear the wine from the table, and went to find her elder sister to bid farewell, intending to take her cousin back to the mansion to rest.

Sima Yan’s expression was gentle, but she did not agree.

"Ningxi, you are the most important person today. If you leave, wouldn't my painstaking efforts be in vain?"

Sima Yu was silent for a moment, then said, "Actually, I..."

Sima Yan’s smile faded slightly. "Ningxi, the envoys from Northern Hu are already on their way. You should understand what this means."

Sima Yu said nothing more, only looking back at her unconscious cousin, and added, "Then may I ask Elder Sister to arrange a room for my cousin and Lady Zhao to rest?"

"Naturally." Sima Yan ordered, "Wu’er, go and arrange it yourself. Be sure it is done properly."

Sima Yu felt relieved. "Thank you, Elder Sister."

The banquet continued, missing only the two drunken young ladies and the Grand Princess’s trusted maid.

Inside Hangu Hall.

The palace maids and eunuchs cleared the food in an orderly, silent fashion.

It was not until Xu He stepped inside with small steps that voices were heard in the hall.

"Sage, Grand Princess Lehua invites you to Fuyue Hall, saying she has an urgent matter to discuss."

Sima Xin said calmly, "The polo match is over?"

"Yes," Xu He replied with his head bowed. "The Grand Princess’s banquet is set in Fanglin Garden. Perhaps Princess Ningxi already has a candidate for a husband, though I do not know why she would invite the Sage to go there."

Logically, it should have been the Grand Princess coming to Hangu Hall to pay her respects to the Sage.

However, the Grand Princess had assisted the Sage greatly, and since she rarely asked the Sage to make a trip, the Sage might grant her this favor.

Sure enough, after a moment, Sima Xin rose and walked out of the hall, having agreed to the Grand Princess’s request.

Xu He hurriedly ordered the sedan chair to be prepared.

After the Sage ascended the throne, Empress Dowager Fan often let Grand Princess Lehua enter the palace to keep her company, so the Sage had allocated Fuyue Hall for the Grand Princess to reside in.

Sima Xin had almost never been here.

Within the palace, the place he spent the most time was Hangu Hall.

The eunuchs outside Fuyue Hall knelt to pay their respects upon seeing the imperial carriage.

Cheng Wu, who had been waiting for a long time, felt inevitably nervous upon seeing the Sage. She knew that what the Grand Princess was doing might anger the Sage, and if so, she would certainly be the first to suffer the Sage’s wrath.

However, it was also possible that the Sage would be satisfied, and the Grand Princess would be able to put a worry to rest.

"Sage," Cheng Wu said, trying her best to steady her voice. "The Grand Princess says, please follow me to the side hall."

Sima Xin’s gaze was cold. "Why?"

Cheng Wu maintained her bowing posture and replied with her head lowered, "She has prepared a gift for you. If you like it, you may take it away directly; if you do not like it, then she will give this gift to someone else."

chapters.title: Chapter 22 Thirsty
chapters.content:
Sima Xin did not move.

The eunuchs and maids in Fuyue Hall dared not breathe loudly, and the courtyard was deathly silent.

"Your Majesty," Xu He whispered, "Shall this servant go in and take a look?"

Cheng Wu, recalling the scene inside, suppressed his fear and bowed. "Your Majesty, Princess Zhang only invites you to enter and observe. She requests that Eunuch Xu wait outside."

Xu He frowned, puzzled by what game Princess Zhang was playing today.

If it weren't for the fact that this maid was acting on the princess's orders, he would have suspected her of ill intentions.

He was about to rebuke Cheng Wu for overstepping—his words were vague, and he was suggesting that His Majesty enter alone. No one in the world dared to dictate how His Majesty should conduct himself.

"Your Majesty's noble body—"

Before he could finish, he saw His Majesty raise his hand, signaling him to stay, then stride toward the side hall.

The door opened and closed, leaving no way to glimpse the secrets within.

Xu He lightly flicked his whisk, his brow furrowed as he turned to Cheng Wu. "What is inside?"

Cheng Wu said nothing, only lowering her head to stand guard by the door.

Xu He couldn’t press her further. He stepped to the door, listening intently for any sounds inside. If anything seemed amiss, he would immediately lead his men in.

Inside the hall, the charcoal fire burned brightly, radiating warmth.

Sunlight streamed through the lattice windows, illuminating the wispy tendrils of incense rising from the censer.

Layers of sheer gauze curtains obscured the graceful figure of the woman reclining on the platform bed.

Sima Xin’s gaze turned cold as he understood his elder sister’s intentions.

He paused mid-step, about to turn and leave, when the woman inside the curtains suddenly let out a soft, weak voice.

"Cousin."

The voice was tender and sweet, lingering like silk.

Sima Xin froze, a flicker of surprise in his eyes.

Warm from the wine, Gu Yuechan’s throat was parched. Hearing the faint footsteps, she groggily opened her eyes and called out for her cousin.

Receiving no answer, she struggled to prop herself up, intending to get a cup of tea.

But her head spun, and her body was too weak. Her hand only brushed the soft gauze before falling limply back down.

The footsteps grew louder, approaching.

Assuming it was her cousin, she softly called, "I want water."

The curtain was lifted.

A tall figure stood by the bed, silently watching the woman on it.

The thin peach-blossom gauze covering her did little to conceal the springtime scenery beneath.

Sima Xin’s expression remained impassive as his gaze swept over the fair skin visible beneath the sheer fabric. "Why are you here?" he asked coolly.

The voice was strangely familiar.

Gu Yuechan lifted her misty eyes to look at the speaker.

It was a man.

Handsomer than any of the young nobles on the polo field today.

After a slow, dull thought, her face suddenly lit up with delight. "Daozhang."

She had been wanting to properly thank Daozhang for a while, but knowing he rarely stayed at the temple, and with her recent busyness, she had set the thought aside.

But how had Daozhang ended up here?

And where was here?

Gu Yuechan slowly scanned the room’s furnishings, her vision blurry, but it didn’t seem to be her room, nor her cousin’s.

Just now, she had been drinking with Lady Zhao in Fanglin Courtyard.

Then… she had gotten drunk. Could this be a side room in Fanglin Courtyard?

Sima Xin saw her confused expression, utterly unaware of how alluring she looked.

The little girl from before had long since grown into a delicate young lady.

He lowered his lashes, his voice deepening. "Lady Gu, this is not a place you should be."

Gu Yuechan didn’t understand what he meant. Another wave of heat surged through her, scattering her thoughts. All she wanted was water, but her body was too weak to sit up.

She couldn’t be bothered to wonder why Daozhang was here. She simply lifted her arm weakly and said softly, "I want water."

Seeing he didn’t move, Gu Yuechan let out a small, displeased hum, feeling he was as cold as before, unwilling to even give her a drink.

She pressed her palm against the bed, trying to sit up.

The light gauze dress was only loosely tied with a silk ribbon, and as she struggled, it came undone, revealing the overflowing white undergarment beneath.

Sima Xin turned away, exhaling slowly. "Wait."

A pot of hot tea sat on the sandalwood table in the inner room. Sima Xin took a teacup, filled it, and carried it back to the platform bed.

He sat on the edge of the bed, leaned forward, and pulled the only brocade quilt over her, covering her skin.

The quilt was thick, and with the charcoal fire burning, Gu Yuechan felt even hotter.

She furrowed her brows, pulling her arm out from under the quilt. "Daozhang, what are you doing?"

Sima Xin looked down, silent. His long fingers held the celadon cup, offering it to her.

Seeing he had poured her water, Gu Yuechan’s frustration eased slightly. She lifted her soft arm to take the cup from his hand.

Her warm skin brushed his fingertips. Sima Xin’s gaze remained fixed on the edge of the quilt, not shifting an inch. Just as he was about to let go, the woman pouted, "I can’t hold it. Daozhang, can you call my cousin over? I want someone to feed me."

Sima Xin closed his eyes briefly, then reached out to pull the woman into his lap, helping her sit up.

The soft, boneless woman obediently let him hold her, slowly drinking the tea he fed her.

Her thirst somewhat quenched, Gu Yuechan still felt unsatisfied. She curled her legs, trying to push the quilt away, but a hand instantly pressed it back down, trapping her.

She pursed her lips, looking at the man restraining her. "Daozhang, I’m hot."

Sima Xin’s gaze darkened. "I’ll have someone take you back."

Back?

Gu Yuechan’s lashes trembled. Suddenly, she remembered that she had finally seen Daozhang and should give him a gift—this way, her father would have someone to look after him at court.

But she hadn’t brought any money today.

She raised her hand to her hair, intending to give him her most valuable gold cicada jade comb, but her fingers found nothing.

Hmm, it was gone.

Gu Yuechan lowered her hand, her fair fingers slowly gripping the black strands of hair falling over her chest. Her gaze shifted, landing on the layers of thin pink gauze draped over her arms, her expression confused.

Sima Xin thought to himself—no need to ask. It must be that his elder sister had gotten her drunk and then sent her here.

He was about to stand up and have her lie back down when the young lady in his arms dazedly tugged at his sleeve and softly asked, "Daozhang, am I dreaming?"

Gu Yuechan tilted her face up at him, her red lips slightly parted. "This isn’t my dress."

Sima Xin didn’t want to say much to a drunk person—she was probably not fully coherent right now, lacking even the basic wariness toward men.

"Yes," he replied perfunctorily.

Gu Yuechan stupidly responded with an "Oh." "If I’m dreaming, then I still want water. Don’t cover me with the quilt, okay? I’m so hot."

Her flushed cheek gently pressed against his cool sleeve. "I want cold water."

Sima Xin’s Adam’s apple subtly rolled. His gaze moved from the peony hair ornament on her forehead down to her moist, red lips.

She had no idea that, to an ordinary man, her actions right now could have unforeseen consequences.

chapters.title: It Was a Dream
chapters.content:
When Xu He heard the woman’s voice from inside, he understood: the Grand Princess intended to present a beauty to the Sage.

The Grand Princess was not ignorant of the Sage’s temperament; how could she have come up with such a foolish plan?

He sighed, estimating that the Sage would be coming out at any moment.

Yet, a long time passed, and the door to the side hall showed no sign of opening. Instead, the Sage was still speaking with the woman.

Could it be that she had sent a beauty so celestial that she had captivated even the Sage, who had been indifferent to women for years?

That would explain why the Grand Princess had acted first and reported later this time.

So, she had been extremely confident in the young lady’s appearance.

Just as he was wondering whether he should have someone prepare water, the door was suddenly opened from within.

Xu He noticed that the Sage’s outer robe was neat, with only slight wrinkles on the sleeves. Since they hadn't been inside for very long, he guessed that the young lady had likely not been favored, though he wondered if she would be arranged to enter the inner court.

He glanced at Cheng Wu, thinking that since the woman was sent by the Grand Princess, it should be Cheng Wu who initiates the inquiry.

As Xu He expected, Cheng Wu asked, "Sage, would you like to keep this young lady?"

"Have her change her clothes. Not a single word of today's events is to be leaked outside." Sima Xin’s expression was cold and somber. He paused for a breath and added, "Invite the Grand Princess to the Hanguang Hall to see me."

Cheng Wu’s heart sank. It seemed the Sage did not intend to keep Lady Gu. Now, she could only hope the Sage would not blame the Grand Princess for the arrangement.

She curtsied and said, "Understood."

The banquet at Fanglin Garden had not yet dispersed. When Grand Princess Lehua heard Cheng Wu’s report, she did not show any disappointment.

She set down her wine cup and asked, "Has Lady Gu been settled properly?"

Cheng Wu replied, "Following the Sage’s decree, I have had Lady Gu re-dressed and arranged for maids to handle the aftermath."

"Look," Grand Princess Lehua smiled lightly. "When has the Sage ever been this considerate?"

If the Sage truly had no interest in Lady Gu, he would have turned and left the moment he saw her; he would not have stayed in the room for so long.

Moreover, ordering that today’s events be kept secret was merely to protect Lady Gu’s reputation.

She stood up gracefully. "I will go to the Hanguang Hall to see the Sage. You stay here; do not let this delay Ningxi’s affairs."

Cheng Wu was worried; the Sage’s expression had been truly grim, and she rarely saw the Sage’s anger so exposed.

However, seeing the Grand Princess’s composed demeanor, she thought that since the Grand Princess was the Sage’s sister, she must understand his mind better. She calmed herself slightly and said, "I obey."

Outside the Hanguang Hall, Xu He stood guard in the corridor, occasionally casting a glance at the tightly closed doors.

Ever since the Sage returned from the Fuyue Hall, he had been left waiting outside, instructed to announce the Grand Princess only upon her arrival.

Leaving no one inside the hall was somewhat unusual.

Half an hour later.

Sima Yan entered the Hanguang Hall to plead guilty.

Inside, Sima Xin had changed into a different outer robe and sat behind the imperial desk. He did not reprimand her, saying only, "Sister, you need not do such things in the future. She already has a suitable match, and I have no romantic intentions toward her. I saw her over a decade ago; in my heart, she is merely a child who has not yet grown up."

His expression was flat, speaking of Lady Gu Liuniang as if she were an insignificant junior.

"From now on, even if she has requests, I will not see her again."

Sima Yan did not question his words, nor did she press for details about the past.

"Since the Sage does not care for her, then so be it. It was my lack of consideration and an overstep in my actions. Rest assured, Sage, such things will not happen again. However, as for that 'suitable match'..." She sighed. "It is not necessarily a good thing. The marriage was decided too early. If Lady Gu marries into that family, I fear she will suffer some hardships. It is a pity for such a frank and delicate young lady."

Seeming to feel she had said too much, Sima Yan rose and bowed. "I should not have let such trifles disturb the Sage’s peace. If there is nothing else, I shall not disturb you further."

Sima Xin nodded. "Go carefully, Sister."

The hall fell silent once more.

Sima Xin picked up a memorial from the desk and opened it; it was a censor impeaching an official for improper conduct.

The content was brief and easy to decide.

Sima Xin stared at it for a long time before suddenly closing the memorial. He tapped his fingers on the desk and said, "Xu He, go and investigate..."

Xu He hurriedly bowed to listen to the command, but the Sage stopped halfway. He waited for a moment, not daring to ask.

The Sage was already in a foul mood today.

"Never mind." Sima Xin reopened the memorial and said something that left Xu He bewildered: "Everything has its own fate."

The sun slanted westward until night swallowed the last trace of light.

When Gu Yuechan woke up, it was pitch black. She did not know the time, nor did she know where she was.

"Cousin?" she called out instinctively.

The sound of a door opening followed. Qiongyu hurried inside, lighting the candles as she said, "My Lady, you are awake. Do you feel unwell anywhere?"

Gu Yuechan was dazzled by the candlelight. She waited two breaths before slowly sitting up. After seeing the furnishings of the room, she said lazily, "My head is a bit dizzy. How long have I slept? Where is my cousin?"

"The Grand Princess has likely already retired." Qiongyu stepped forward to place a soft pillow behind her and gently massaged her temples. "It is nearly the hour of Hai (9-11 PM). The Grand Princess has already sent word to your mother that you are staying at the Princess’s residence tonight. If your mother knew you were reeking of wine, she would surely lecture you again."

She had chosen not to go home precisely because she knew her mother would be displeased.

Gu Yuechan couldn't help but feel some regret. "If I had known, I wouldn't have drunk with Lady Zhao. I can't believe I slept this long. I didn't even get to ask my cousin if she had her eye on any man, nor did I get to tell that Master Xu that my cousin doesn't think much of him at all."

"It won't be too late to ask when the sun rises," Qiongyu said gently. "There is another banquet at the residence tomorrow, and the Grand Princess will be there. Biwen has gone to have food sent over. Eat a little and then rest, so you don't lack energy tomorrow."

Gu Yuechan felt hungry and nodded. "Very well."

It was too late, so Biwen had the kitchen prepare easily digestible porridge and a few side dishes.

After Gu Yuechan finished her meal and Qiongyu and Biwen helped her wash, they extinguished the candles, closed the door, and withdrew.

Although it was nearly the hour of Zi (midnight), Gu Yuechan did not feel sleepy.

She lay on the bed with her eyes closed, but strange scenes flickered in her mind.

It seemed someone had been feeding her water... and then she seemed to have fallen asleep.

She opened her eyes abruptly, remembering that after she got drunk today, she seemed to have seen the Daoist priest.

Gu Yuechan’s eyes were filled with confusion. Was it a dream?

How could the Daoist priest have entered the room where she slept, and even held her...

Those fragments were too blurry. She thought for a moment, deciding that perhaps it was because she had never gone to thank the Daoist priest, and it had become a preoccupation of her heart—so much so that even in her dreams, she could not manage to present the gift she intended for him.

She closed her eyes again, thinking to herself that she must find an opportunity to thank the Daoist priest properly.

The night lingered.

Consciousness blurred.

Peach-blossom-colored silk slipped from her delicate, jade-white shoulders. The charming and alluring woman pressed against the man’s face, her vermilion lips parting slightly: "Daoist, I am so hot. Kiss me."

Sima Xin’s thumb rubbed the small mole at the corner of the woman’s eye, but he did not move.

The woman smiled softly, as if she could see through his thoughts, and took the initiative to kiss his lips.

The faint scent of fruit wine mixed with the warm fragrance of the woman’s body, slowly dismantling his restraint.

Sima Xin suddenly pulled off her silk robe with force, pressing her into the soft brocade quilt.

The woman’s slender fingertips nimbly unfastened his Daoist robe, pressing her skin against his.

The last piece of moon-white undergarment fell to the floor, and the man lowered his head to bite...

Gradually, a fierce sensation surged up his spine... spreading throughout his entire body.

In the end, the woman asked in a sweet, clear voice: "Daoist, do you not like me?"

Sima Xin opened his eyes abruptly.

In the darkness, the lingering sensation had not yet faded.

His expression was somber, far worse than it had been during the day.

After a long time, he coldly called for someone to prepare water.

Bathing in the middle of the night, Xu He assumed the Sage had had a nightmare. But when the palace servants finished tidying the bed, he understood what kind of dream the Sage had had.

For a moment, he did not know whether he should ask if he should summon a concubine to serve the night.

Seeing the Sage’s dark expression, he dared not speak. Fortunately, the rest of the night passed as usual. By dawn, the Sage had returned to his normal demeanor, and Xu He stopped thinking about the matter.

chapters.title: The Wedding Date
chapters.content:
At dawn, Gu Yuechan boarded the carriage and returned home early.

When Zheng Ying saw Sima Yu, her face beamed with joy. She asked with concern, "Did you have a good time yesterday? If there is any young gentleman who catches your eye, your aunt can certainly find someone to inquire about his character."

Sima Yu chuckled softly, "I haven't thought about it yet. If I find someone I like, I will certainly tell you first, Aunt."

Gu Yuechan, who had been left aside, grumbled, "Cousin clearly said she would tell me first."

Sima Yu picked up a cup of water, "I'll tell you both together."

"Alright, don't act like a child," Zheng Ying said, patting her daughter's shoulder. "Your Fifth Sister and Fifth Brother-in-law are back today and are currently speaking with your grandmother. She even brought you a gift; remember to thank her when you see her later."

Gu Yuechan had not seen this Fifth Sister for many years, but they had a good relationship in their childhood. Although she did not like her Second Aunt, she held no ill will toward her Fifth Sister.

Hanyu brought over a box and opened it for her to see; it was a honeysuckle hair ornament made of gold and silver.

After Gu Yuechan had a look, she handed the box to Qiongyu to put away.

"I didn't expect Fifth Sister to still remember my preferences." Gu Yuechan had been tight on money and hadn't bought any jewelry for a long time, so she was naturally happy to receive this gift. "I'll go to Rong'an Hall to pay my respects to Grandmother now."

Sima Yu accompanied her.

Inside Rong'an Hall, Gu Wuniang was sitting beside Old Madam Yuan, speaking in a gentle tone.

With her daughter back, Lü Yanfang was in a very good mood. She asked a few questions about the recent situation of her son-in-law, He Qilang. Hearing him say that everything was well at home, she felt relieved.

The couple had been married for over three years and already had a son. He Qilang held an official position and came from a wealthy family. Although this son-in-law could not compare to the Marquis of Changping’s household, he was considered satisfactory.

When Gu Yuechan entered with Sima Yu, everyone bowed to Sima Yu. Lü Yanfang also showed rare concern, asking if the wedding date between Old Madam Yuan and the Marquis of Changping’s household had been set.

It was no secret in the manor that the Marchioness of Changping had come two days ago to discuss the wedding. Old Madam Yuan said happily, "The wedding date is still under discussion. Even if we are in a hurry, it won't be until next year. Besides, I am reluctant to see Liuniang marry off so soon."

He Qilang said with refined elegance, "Both the Marquis of Changping and the eldest uncle have been promoted, and now the two families are holding a wedding—it is truly a double celebration. Wuniang was always talking about Liuniang when she was at home, but our child was young and could not be away from his mother, so it dragged on until today for me to accompany Wuniang back to the manor."

He gave Gu Wuniang a subtle look, but she turned away and remained silent.

He Qilang’s brow twitched, though his face remained filled with a gentle smile. "Speaking of which, I have met Ye Erlang a few times before. I wonder if he will be coming today?"

Gu Yuechan glanced at him, thinking this man was truly strange.

However, thinking that he was her Fifth Sister’s husband, she replied, "Erlang will naturally come."

The Marchioness of Changping would also be visiting. She just hoped that Ye Dalang and the County Princess of Minghu would have the self-awareness not to come.

He Qilang’s smile deepened. "Then I must have a few more drinks with him later. We will be brothers-in-law after all. I wonder if Ye Erlang would be willing to offer some guidance if I were to ask him for academic advice, for the sake of Liuniang."

Hearing this, Lü Yanfang’s expression soured.

Her own son-in-law was trying to curry favor with Liuniang’s future husband.

However, although He Qilang was older, he was only a *juren*, while Ye Erlang had already passed the *jinshi* examination. It was not entirely inappropriate to ask for advice.

She suppressed her irritation and smiled, "We will all be one family in the future; how could Ye Erlang refuse? What do you think, Liuniang?"

Gu Yuechan replied perfunctorily, "When Erlang arrives, Fifth Brother-in-law can ask him himself."

Although she felt that, given Erlang’s temperament, he certainly wouldn't refuse.

Gu Wuniang’s smile seemed to fade slightly. She glanced at He Qilang before speaking gently to Gu Yuechan, "Sixth Sister, don't trouble yourself. Just let them speak for themselves. You are not yet married; how can you act in your own name? Wouldn't that damage your reputation?"

Hearing her Fifth Sister say this, Gu Yuechan felt a bit embarrassed. "Erlang is kind-hearted, so I imagine he wouldn't refuse Fifth Brother-in-law. The hairpin Fifth Sister gave me today is beautiful; thank you, Fifth Sister."

Gu Wuniang smiled, "I'm glad you like it."

He Qilang was satisfied, thinking that Gu Wuniang said that to help him.

It seemed Wuniang still knew what was important. A husband’s success is a wife’s glory; her helping him was helping herself. Once he could use the influence of the Marquis of Changping’s household to secure a better official position, her life and their son’s life would naturally be better.

The Gu family’s temperament was truly hard to fathom. He had said several flattering things to Old Madam Yuan earlier, but she didn't mention having her eldest son look after him, and Gu Liuniang’s attitude was also quite indifferent.

Only his mother-in-law was more agreeable.

Afraid of saying the wrong thing, He Qilang simply kept a smile on his face and listened to them talk, waiting for the people from the Marquis of Changping’s household to arrive so he could pay his respects.

When it grew dark, the Marchioness of Changping, Lady Xu, arrived with Ye Erlang.

Lady Xu had changed from her previous coldness and was much more affectionate toward Gu Yuechan, as if she truly regarded her as her future daughter-in-law. During the banquet, she chatted and laughed with Zheng Ying, "By this time next year, Liuniang should be part of our family. Lady Zheng, please don't be reluctant; I have been looking forward to this day."

Ye Erlang looked at Gu Yuechan, and the joy on his face could not escape the eyes of those present.

He Qilang raised his glass and offered a few words of congratulation to Ye Erlang. Knowing that this man was Liuniang’s Fifth Brother-in-law, Ye Erlang gave him face by drinking and, following his lead, offered a few words of courtesy.

As Gu Yuechan had said, Ye Erlang was indeed a gentle person. He Qilang was extremely satisfied, feeling that this trip was well worth it.

After the banquet ended, Gu Yuechan and Sima Yu lay together on the pear-wood bed, whispering.

"Cousin, Mother said that Lady Xu wants to set the wedding date for April of next year."

"There are still six months; that is enough time to prepare," Sima Yu said, looking at the top of the canopy. "Do you think it's too slow?"

Gu Yuechan shook her head, "No, I just think the Marchioness’s attitude is very strange. She clearly didn't like me before, but now she acts as if she is very satisfied with me. And Fifth Sister’s husband—I find him no different from those who used to distance themselves from Father but then fawned over him once he gained power. But since he is Fifth Brother-in-law, it’s hard not to associate with him."

Sima Yu was silent for a moment and said, "Yes, it is a pity that sometimes, even if we don't like something, we have to pretend to be satisfied."

Gu Yuechan heard the dejection in her voice and couldn't help but turn to look at her. "Did what I say make you unhappy?"

"No," Sima Yu curled her lips into a faint smile. "Can't you see I'm comforting you? Alright, go to sleep."

Gu Yuechan stared at her for a long time and suddenly asked, "Cousin, have you encountered something troubling?"

Sima Yu pushed her shoulder, "Stop overthinking. I am a Princess; I lack neither gold nor silver, and I have servants in droves. You should worry more about your own affairs, you little pauper."

The words "little pauper" struck a sore spot for Gu Yuechan.

She grumbled, got up to blow out the candle, and laid down to sleep.

chapters.title: Ambush
chapters.content:
A few days after the banquet, Gu Mingtu took up his new post, and the atmosphere in the manor took on a fresh, new look.

The Gu and Ye families began to interact frequently, and those with a discerning eye could see that a happy union between the Gu family’s sixth daughter and the Ye family’s second young master was drawing near.

Zhenyuan Marquis Manor.

After hearing the maid’s report, Xie Peiluo’s expression remained calm.

The Marchioness of Zhenyuan, Lady He, however, looked displeased. She said coldly, "I thought Lady Xu was a clever woman, but it seems she is nothing more than that. Seeing the Gu family on the rise again, she seems to have completely forgotten her previous words."

She looked at her daughter. "Your grandmother asked about you a few days ago. The Prince of Wu is already sixteen, and the Empress Dowager intends to choose a wife for him. You are of a similar age to the Prince of Wu. The Sage has no heirs; although your sister holds the rank of Noble Consort, she has no prince by her side, making her position like a castle in the air. In the future..."

In the future, the throne would likely fall to the Prince of Wu.

"Mother," Xie Peiluo lowered her eyes. "Didn't you say before that I didn't need to marry for an alliance? Besides, the Prince of Wu is barely sixteen, yet his manor is filled with countless concubines, and he already has two children."

Lady He persuaded her, "He is a prince of the blood, and the imperial family has few heirs; it is a good thing that he has children early. In the future, you won't need to be like your sister, with an empty lap. Furthermore, if you marry the Prince of Wu, your children will be the legitimate heirs; those illegitimate sons and daughters are merely matters of giving them a portion of the family property to send them away."

Seeing her daughter unmoved, she pleaded earnestly, "Your grandfather originally favored your fourth cousin, but it was your grandmother who took pity on you and came to speak to me about this."

"If you agree, in a few days, when the Duchess of Ping celebrates her birthday, I will pave the way with her and ask her to mention you to the Empress Dowager. Your sister can also support you. Once you become the Princess of Wu, what will the second young master of the Ye family count for? Even the people of the Changping Marquis Manor and the Gu family will have to bow before you."

Xie Peiluo’s eyes flickered, but she did not immediately relent.

"Even if I cannot marry the second young master of the Ye family, can that Gu sixth daughter get her wish?"

Lady He was puzzled. "Why do you care about that Gu sixth daughter? Even if she marries into the Changping Marquis Manor, the second young master cannot inherit the title. If they are diligent, obtaining a title of honor for her will be the absolute limit."

Xie Peiluo insisted stubbornly, "Mother, many young ladies in the capital know my intentions. If the marriage contract between the Ye and Gu families proceeds as usual, won't others think I have lost to that Gu sixth daughter? I wouldn't have the face to go out to banquets anymore."

Lady He pondered for a moment. Seeing that she would not change her mind, she said helplessly, "I will go see the Marchioness of Changping and see if she has any other ideas."

Only then did Xie Peiluo turn toward her mother, her lips curling slightly. "Mother is the only one who truly cares for me."

By mid-October, the cold winds in the capital began to bite.

Invitations from noble families became increasingly frequent, whether for young ladies to gather for amusement or for some family's celebration.

Gu Yuechan had been idle for a few days. At first, she had forgotten about her plan to send a thank-you gift to the Taoist temple, until her mother told her she was going to the temple with the Marchioness of Changping to burn incense and have her marriage to the second young master of the Ye family divined. Only then did she remember.

It was not right to ask someone for a favor and then cast them aside.

After making a vow at the temple, one must return to fulfill it.

She secretly scolded herself for a moment, but then became troubled over the thank-you gift. She no longer had six hundred taels, so perhaps she should buy some pastries from Xingrongju to bring along.

But to go without gold or silver would seem insincere.

She rummaged through her chests for half a day, and the only thing that suited the status of a Taoist priest was the prize she had won at the last polo match—a painting of a lady.

However, that was a possession of Princess Lehua, and the Taoist priest seemed to know the Princess. If the Princess were to see it, that would be awkward.

She decided to go to her father and pestered him until he gave her a painting of a spring excursion from his collection.

With everything prepared, she boarded the carriage for Yong'an Temple with her maid.

She did not seek to meet the Taoist priest; she only wanted the monks in the temple to pass the gift to him, so he would know that she was a person who knew how to repay kindness and keep her word. That would be enough.

The road to Yong'an Temple remained remote and desolate, and Gu Yuechan had no interest in looking out.

When Biwen bought the pastries, she had picked up a few popular storybooks for her. Leaning against a soft pillow, Gu Yuechan was so engrossed that she almost forgot to eat the new red bean milk pastries from Xingrongju.

"I didn't expect the storybooks in the capital to be so interesting." Gu Yuechan turned a page, and just as she was about to ask Biwen to buy more next time, the horses suddenly let out a shrill neigh.

In an instant, the carriage came to a sudden halt. Gu Yuechan lost her balance and hit the wall of the carriage, letting out a cry of pain.

"Young Lady, we are under attack, be careful!" Lin Qi’s voice sounded stern from outside.

Qiongyu was startled and hurriedly stepped forward with Biwen to steady their young lady, asking nervously, "Could it be bandits?"

If they were bandits, there was nothing to worry about.

What she feared was that these people were hired to do a job.

Outside, Lin Qi ordered two guards to stay by the carriage to ensure the safety of the sixth daughter of the Gu family, while he quickly led the other guards to meet the enemy.

The sound of clashing swords rang out, making everyone feel anxious and fearful.

Biwen, the most timid of them, held Gu Yuechan’s hand, trembling violently. "Young Lady, this is outside the capital. How could anyone dare to intercept the carriage of an official's daughter in broad daylight?"

Though Gu Yuechan was also afraid, with her cousin’s men there, she felt more indignant.

"They must be thrown into prison for daring to rob..."

"Clang!" An arrow shot from afar and embedded itself in the carriage wall. Gu Yuechan stared at the arrowhead, her voice failing her.

"Young Lady." Biwen finally couldn't help but cry out, "Are these people robbing us or trying to kill us?"

Gu Yuechan clenched her hands. Suddenly, the carriage curtain was lifted, and a guard said urgently, "Is the young lady unharmed?"

She nodded blankly.

The guard breathed a sigh of relief. "Young Lady, rest assured, Master Lin is highly skilled in martial arts; those people are nothing to worry about."

Lin Qi was the most trusted guard in Sima Yu’s manor. Sima Yu had been busy lately, but knowing his cousin was going to Yong'an Temple, he had sent him to lead the escort.

It was only a few hours' journey, and Gu Yuechan hadn't expected any trouble. The Great Jin was peaceful and prosperous, and near the capital, almost no one would be foolish enough to commit robbery.

Yet, she had actually encountered it.

After the sounds of battle outside ceased, Lin Qi wiped the blood from his face and came to the front of the carriage to report.

"Sixth Young Lady, they appear to be dead soldiers. We were unable to take any alive."

Gu Yuechan calmed her nerves and slowly stepped out of the carriage.

On the dusty road, a dozen corpses lay scattered. The smell of blood drifted on the wind, accompanied by a nauseating stench.

Gu Yuechan took a difficult breath and forced herself to remain calm. "Then take their bodies back and let the Jingzhao Prefecture investigate where they came from."

Lin Qi replied, "Understood. Does the young lady still wish to proceed to Yong'an Temple?"

They were still a cup of tea's journey away from Yong'an Temple. Gu Yuechan pondered for a moment and asked, "Guard Lin, do you think there will be further danger if we go now?"

"If the young lady's safety is the priority, it would naturally be best to return now," Lin Qi said stiffly. "However, in my humble opinion, the culprits will not send more men so quickly."

Gu Yuechan nodded. "Then let's continue."

She glanced at the arrow embedded in the carriage. "Pull it out."

Lin Qi raised his hand, signaling the guards to do as she asked.

Leaving two men to collect the bodies, the carriage wheels rolled over the blood-soaked dirt road toward Yong'an Temple.

In the swaying carriage, Qiongyu wanted to comfort her young lady, but seeing her head bowed in thought, she didn't seem to be afraid; instead, it was Biwen who was still silently wiping away tears.

Qiongyu thought to herself that the young lady’s courage was truly not to be underestimated; seeing so many dead bodies for the first time, she hadn't even changed her expression.

Fortunately, the young lady was well-prepared this time. If they had encountered this group last time, they might have already been killed.

Thinking about it was truly terrifying.

The carriage stopped in front of Yong'an Temple. Qiongyu lifted the curtain and turned to help the young lady down, only to see her sitting still, staring at her with wide eyes.

She said softly, "Young Lady, what is wrong?"

Gu Yuechan wanted to say her legs were a bit weak, but she felt that would make her appear overly delicate. Last time at the Lishan hunting grounds, she had shot quite a few pieces of game; how could she be frightened by a group of bandits who had already been dealt with?

Or perhaps they weren't bandits. Guard Lin said they might be dead soldiers.

But she had thought for a long time and couldn't figure out who she had such deep enmity with.

"Nothing." She raised her hand for Biwen to help her. "Just tired from sitting."

The gates of Yong'an Temple were closed, and no one was guarding the outside.

Lin Qi stepped forward to knock. Before long, the door was opened from within, and a round-faced Taoist walked out. Just as he was about to say that idlers were not allowed, he caught the strong scent of blood.

The round-faced Taoist looked vigilant. "Who are you, and what is your business here?"

Lin Qi did not answer, but stepped aside to reveal the beautiful young lady behind him.

"Taoist priest, I have business with Taoist Qingxuan." Gu Yuechan’s eyes curved, and she asked politely, "May I ask if he is in the temple?"

The round-faced Taoist recognized her at once as the woman whom Senior Brother Yunfeng had brought into the temple to see the Sage last time.

Senior Brother Yunfeng had instructed that if this young lady came again, he should invite her in.

His attitude softened, and he said to her, "Please follow me."

Gu Yuechan thought she had come at a very opportune time, happening to catch Taoist Qingxuan in the temple. It seemed her luck was not bad.

The little setback on the road was instantly cast to the back of her mind.

As before, only she entered the temple. The round-faced Taoist saw that she was having trouble carrying two wooden boxes, so he took the heavier food box and led her to see his senior brother.

Gu Yuechan followed the round-faced Taoist for a while, then suddenly asked, "Taoist, this temple is in a remote location. Are there often bandits nearby?"

The round-faced Taoist replied without hesitation, "No, Lady Gu need not worry."

If there were such blind fools, his senior brother would likely have had them cleared away within three days.

Gu Yuechan nodded thoughtfully and said as she walked, "I encountered armed villains on the road. I was thinking that when I see Taoist Qingxuan later, I should warn him to tell the other Taoists in the temple to be careful. Although those villains were dealt with by the guards I brought, I fear there may be remnants."

The more she spoke, the more shocked the round-faced Taoist became. He paused and turned to look at her in surprise. "Is what Lady Gu says true? No wonder that person had such a scent of blood on him earlier."

"Naturally, it is true." Gu Yuechan sighed softly. "If I hadn't brought guards this time, I might have been killed. I wanted to go back after such an incident, but since I was almost here and Taoist Qingxuan has helped me so much, I had to come and thank him before leaving."

When she saw Taoist Qingxuan later, she would definitely complain a bit more so he would feel she was very sincere.

If he could help her catch the person behind this more quickly, that would be even better.

The round-faced Taoist looked troubled for a moment but said nothing, gesturing, "Please, Young Lady, my senior brother is just ahead."

"Good." Gu Yuechan assumed the senior brother he spoke of was Taoist Qingxuan, and clutching the painting box, she walked a bit faster.

But when the round-faced Taoist called out to the man in green inside the room, saying that Lady Gu had arrived, Gu Yuechan hadn't yet realized that the person he was leading her to see was not Taoist Qingxuan.

Her gaze swept from left to right, then back again, finally settling on the only man in green in the room.

"Taoist Qingxuan, will you not see me?"

Yunfeng waved his hand, and the round-faced Taoist set down the food box and left quietly.

He pointed to the armchair in the room and said to Gu Yuechan, "Lady Gu, please sit. My senior brother is not in the temple these days, but he has a few words for me to convey to you."

Gu Yuechan walked slowly into the room, sat in the armchair, and thought for a moment, recalling the Taoist name Taoist Qingxuan had called him.

"Thank you, Taoist Yunfeng."

Yunfeng asked, "Would Lady Gu like some tea?"

Gu Yuechan was not in the mood and shook her head. "No need. What does Taoist Qingxuan have to tell me?"

"My senior brother says that you need not come again in the future," Yunfeng said unhurriedly. "Regarding Lady Gu's affairs, my senior brother only mentioned a word in the Sage's ear and did not put forth much effort. Please do not keep this matter on your mind, otherwise, my senior brother will feel uneasy."

Following Yuntan's instructions to tactfully convey the Sage's meaning, Yunfeng felt his attitude was certainly gentle, and his wording was much more polite than the Sage's own words of "tell her she need not come again."

But seeing the young lady's eyes grow moist, he began to reflect on whether his words had been too harsh.

"Lady Gu." Yunfeng was about to offer some remedy when he saw the young woman suddenly stand up and throw the painting box in her hand onto the desk beside him.

With a "thud," it seemed to carry her anger.

"This is a thank-you gift for Taoist Qingxuan." Gu Yuechan lowered her eyes. "Please tell him not to worry; I will not come to disturb him again."

Having said that, she turned and walked toward the door without a hint of reluctance.

Yunfeng was stunned for a moment, feeling that his task had been botched.

He remembered the other thing the Sage had instructed, so he hurriedly got up to follow her, calling out, "Lady Gu, please stay."

Gu Yuechan paused, biting her lip to suppress the sudden surge of grievance in her heart.

"May I ask what else there is?"

He took a simple green pouch from his sleeve and handed it to her. "This contains six hundred taels. My senior brother ordered me to give it to you."

Gu Yuechan did not understand why Taoist Qingxuan suddenly wanted to draw a line with her.

Not only did he not want to see her again, but he even wanted to return the six hundred taels.

Was she really that annoying?

She looked at the pouch in Taoist Yunfeng’s hand, her fingers twitching, but she did not reach out to take it.

"This is incense money I donated to the temple." Gu Yuechan turned around and said in a low voice, "There is no reason to take it back; wouldn't that be disrespectful to the True One? I should be going. Please tell Taoist Qingxuan not to worry; I will act as if I have never met him."

chapters.title: Loss
chapters.content:
Yunfeng held up his hand, listening to the tearful tone in her voice, and thought to himself that things had gone poorly.

This had definitely been a disaster.

Gu Yuechan turned to the side and bowed with her hands folded: "Farewell, Daoist. There is no need to see me out."

Before Yunfeng could return the gesture, she had already hurried over the threshold and disappeared around the corner.

The purse that had not been given away felt like it had grown thorns in his hand. Yunfeng found it quite troublesome; the Sage had not said what to do if Mistress Gu refused to accept it.

He pondered whether he should wait for Yuntan to return to the temple to tell him what happened today and have him report it to the Sage, or if he should report it to the Sage himself as soon as possible...

The round-faced Daoist walked into the room, looking at the dazed man in confusion: "Third Senior Brother? What is wrong with you?"

Yunfeng came back to his senses, put the purse away, and looked up at him: "Did you not run into Mistress Gu? Why didn't you see her out of the temple before coming back?"

The round-faced Daoist scratched his head in confusion: "Ah? Was I supposed to? But Mistress Gu should know the way, right? Besides, she was walking so fast, she passed by me like a gust of wind; I didn't even have time to speak."

Yunfeng: "..." Perhaps he should go to the palace tomorrow; the things Mistress Gu brought also needed to be handed over to the Sage.

"By the way, Senior Brother, just now Mistress Gu said she ran into over a dozen thugs on her way here, and she even asked me if there were any mountain bandits nearby. Senior Brother, do you think anyone would really dare to claim territory around here?"

"Thugs?" Yunfeng frowned: "How is that possible? Did Mistress Gu say what happened to those thugs? Did they run away, or were they captured by her people?"

The round-faced Daoist: "I don't know. Mistress Gu only said they were dealt with. But fortunately, Mistress Gu is unharmed. I've been here for so long, and apart from the Princess Royal, I haven't seen another woman who could meet the Sage. I suppose the Sage must hold Mistress Gu in high regard."

No sooner had he finished speaking than he saw Senior Brother Yunfeng staring at him blankly.

The round-faced Daoist thought he had said something wrong and hesitantly corrected himself: "Could it be that other women have been here before?"

Yunfeng withdrew his gaze, said "no," and then quickly turned to retrieve the painting box Mistress Gu had left behind. After opening it and seeing that there was only one painting inside, he quickly closed it again.

"I am going to see the Sage." He carried the painting box and said as he walked: "You are responsible for looking after the temple."

Hearing that he was going to see the Sage, the round-faced Daoist thought that mountain bandits had truly appeared nearby. He wanted to ask when his senior brother would be back, but he had only managed to say two words before his senior brother had already vanished...

Why was he in such a hurry, just like Mistress Gu?

On the desolate mountain road, only one carriage was traveling.

Qiong Yu looked at her mistress, who had been sullen since leaving the temple, and said softly: "Mistress, did you not get to see him?"

Gu Yuechan leaned against the carriage wall and gave a very low "mm."

"Mistress, you need not be discouraged." Qiong Yu assumed she was disappointed because the trip had been in vain, and comforted her gently: "Didn't that Daoist say last time that Daoist Qingxuan is not often in the temple? You left the painting, and when Daoist Qingxuan returns and sees it, he will surely understand your gratitude toward him."

Qiong Yu would have been better off not saying anything; as soon as she spoke, the tears Gu Yuechan had been holding back for so long suddenly fell.

"He, he won't understand at all."

She sobbed and said indignantly: "To thank him, I was almost hurt by thugs, but he only thinks I am a nuisance. I am not an ungrateful person; when I asked him to put in a good word for Father, I not only gave him all my money but also gave him my favorite pastries."

No one had ever told her not to see them again.

Qiong Yu was truly startled to see her crying.

Since coming of age, her mistress rarely cried in front of others. Even when she felt sad, she would only secretly shed a few tears under her quilt, and by the next day, she would be fine, so they would just pretend not to know.

But today, her mistress was crying because she hadn't seen Daoist Qingxuan.

"Mistress, please don't cry." Bi Wen, seeing her crying, also hurriedly urged: "Daoist Qingxuan must have been away on business. Did someone else say something unpleasant? That surely wasn't Daoist Qingxuan's intention. How could anyone in the world think you are a nuisance?"

"H-how could they not?" Gu Yuechan covered her eyes with her sleeve and cried: "He had his junior brother tell me... never to come again. Isn't that just thinking I'm a nuisance? And those people on the road today—someone is clearly against me and wants me dead."

Seeing her crying until she was out of breath, Qiong Yu feared she would hurt herself, so she racked her brains to comfort her: "Mistress, the Master has already returned to the imperial court. To be honest, there is no longer any need for you to see the Daoist. Besides, you encountered danger on this trip. There is no need to come to such a remote place in the future, and you can avoid such things happening again. Mistress, why must you be so sad about this?"

"Yes, yes," Bi Wen echoed: "Mistress, we don't even care to come here. There are many fun places in the capital, and there won't be such rampant thugs there. After you go back, you can invite people to play polo, enjoy the scenery, and drink tea. Isn't that much more interesting than coming here?"

The two sang in harmony, painting the idea of not coming here as a wonderful thing.

Gu Yuechan knew they made sense, and although she still couldn't bring herself to be happy, she gradually stopped her tears.

She took the handkerchief Qiong Yu handed her, carefully wiped her eyes, and adjusted her makeup in the mirror.

"It's fine not to come."
