Thinking that she had actually ruined her makeup by crying, Gu Yuechan said with embarrassment and annoyance: "Anyway, I am a person who keeps her word, but if he doesn't want to accept it, I can't force it on him, can I? I won't have to save money anymore. Tomorrow I will go to the East Market to buy pearl hairpins; I won't save my money to give to him."

She picked up the storybook she had been reading halfway through and tried hard to put that person out of her mind.

Although he was the only one who, without any relation to her, was willing to help her when her family lost power, he now wanted to draw a line between them, and she would not lose her dignity by pestering him.

Gu Yuechan's fingers pressed heavily on the corner of the book. She thought, perhaps he was afraid she would beg him to put in a good word for her father again in the future.

He just found her troublesome.

Thinking of this, Gu Yuechan closed the book in irritation and closed her eyes to rest.

The carriage did not head toward the Gu residence but went to Sima Yu's mansion instead.

Something had happened on the road, and Gu Yuechan wanted to consult her cousin first. After all, it was her cousin's guards who had fought those people; she had to ask for her opinion on whether to report it to the Jingzhao Prefecture or investigate it privately.

However, Sima Yu was out on business today and had not yet returned, so Gu Yuechan stayed at the Princess's mansion to wait for her and sent someone to inform her mother.

At the same time, Yunfeng successfully entered the palace and brought his senior brother, Yuntan, along.

In the Hanguang Hall, Yunfeng reported Mistress Gu's words to the Sage word for word and presented the items Mistress Gu had sent for the Sage.

Xu He took the food box and the painting box and whispered: "Sage, do you wish to look at these, or...?"

Sima Xin tapped the table lightly.

That meant he wanted to see them. Xu He held the items and placed them on the imperial desk.

chapters.title: Investigation
chapters.content:
Xu He opened both brocade boxes, and Sima Xin looked calmly at the items inside.

Pastries, and a painting.

They were nothing rare or exotic.

Seeing the Sage staring at the scroll, Xu He, being very perceptive, asked for instructions: "Sage, shall I open it?"

Sima Xin shifted his gaze away, his voice cold and desolate: "No need, put it away."

Having misread the imperial intent, Xu He quickly packed the items away to make amends.

Yun Feng saw that the Sage did not care about the gifts from Miss Gu, and for a moment, he doubted if he had guessed wrong. Upon careful reflection, if the Sage truly had any feelings for Miss Gu, why would he have told her not to come to the Taoist temple to seek him out again?

If it weren't for that remark from Yun Kang, he wouldn't have gone down the wrong path.

"Sage, there is one more matter. On her way here, Miss Gu encountered over a dozen thugs not far from the Taoist temple. I do not know where these people came from; should we investigate this thoroughly?"

Since the Sage had no feelings for Miss Gu, he focused his report on whether these people might have been targeting the Sage.

Sima Xin’s eyes turned icy: "Was Miss Gu injured?"

Yun Feng: "I believe not."

"Believe?" Sima Xin frowned at him: "Since you knew she encountered thugs, why did you not ask?"

Yun Feng: "..."

By the time he found out, Miss Gu had already left in anger; if he had chased after her, wouldn't he have been making a nuisance of himself?

What exactly was the Sage’s intention? He didn't want to see Miss Gu, yet he was concerned about whether she was injured?

Seeing his junior brother stunned, Yun Tan stepped forward to smooth things over: "Sage, Yun Feng told me on his way here that he only learned of this from Yun Kang after Miss Gu had already left. Since Yun Feng did not notice anything amiss when he saw Miss Gu, it is clear she was not injured, though she was surely frightened."

He lowered his head slightly: "If the Sage is concerned for Miss Gu's safety, I am willing to make a trip to the Gu residence."

Concerned?

Sima Xin felt the word was inappropriate; he simply disliked accidents that fell outside his control.

"For bandits daring enough to attack the daughter of a Vice Minister to appear in the capital region is no small matter." His demeanor returned to calm, and he said coldly: "Order the Jingzhao Prefecture to investigate this strictly. If they encounter difficulties, have the Dali Temple assist. I want results within three days."

He paused for a breath and added: "Do not make a scene of this. Yun Tan, you shall oversee it."

Yun Feng and Yun Tan bowed in unison and acknowledged the order.

Once outside the palace gates, Yun Feng complained in a low voice: "You didn't make it clear to me earlier. I thought that if the Sage didn't want to see the young lady again, he surely didn't care about her."

Yun Tan rested his hand on his sleeve, his tone puzzled: "Did I not make it clear? I told you to convey the Sage's meaning gently, yet you made her cry, and you didn't even notice that people were causing trouble near the temple. With the Master away, you have become increasingly lax."

"I was very tactful already." Yun Feng felt aggrieved. He had always been gentle and polite with others, but no matter how tactfully the Sage's words were phrased, they couldn't change the message of "do not come again."

Who could be happy hearing that?

"Senior Brother, do you think the Sage cares about Miss Gu or not? If he cares, why would he not want to see her?"

Yun Tan curled his lips slightly: "I am not the Sage, how would I know? Whether the Sage cares for Miss Gu is known only to the Sage. You should not gossip or speculate on the Sage's intentions; the Sage most dislikes others acting on their own initiative."

Yun Feng nodded: "I understand. When I return to the temple, I will have people check if there are any other suspicious individuals in the vicinity."

After the two parted ways, Yun Tan boarded a carriage and ordered it to the Jingzhao Prefecture.

Li Yuncheng, the Governor of Jingzhao, knew he was a confidant of the Sage and held an imperial decree, so he dared not be negligent.

But this task...

Li Yuncheng showed a hint of confusion: "Then where are these thugs now? Who did they attack? Are there any victims? Master Yun, one cannot solve a case without any clues."

Yun Tan smiled gently: "Master Li, please remain calm. This matter occurred near Yongan Temple, and there are many things that cannot be known to outsiders. For now, just investigate if there have been any anomalies in the capital region these past few days. Tomorrow, I will provide you with the details of the incident."

Hearing this, Li Yuncheng’s brow relaxed. That was more like it; otherwise, he would have had to push this task onto the Dali Temple.

As the sun dipped below the horizon, the Princess's residence welcomed a rare guest.

In the front hall, Sima Yu looked at the person before her, feeling utterly puzzled. Why would this person come to her residence?

After returning to her estate, she learned of what her cousin had encountered on the road and was just about to order Lin Qi to send the corpses to the Jingzhao Prefecture to request the Governor to investigate who dared to harm her cousin.

If she hadn't sent Lin Qi, her cousin might have met with disaster today.

She was just about to head to the Jingzhao Prefecture office in a fury when a maid came to report that Master Yun from the Taichang Temple requested an audience.

Yun Tan was from Yongan Temple and deeply trusted by the Sage; she had never had any dealings with him, and Sima Yu could not think of a reason for him to seek her out.

"Grand Princess." Yun Tan came straight to the point: "May I request to see Miss Gu the Sixth? I heard that a group of thugs appeared in the outskirts of the capital today. This matter should have been handled directly by the Jingzhao Prefecture, but the location where these people appeared is unfortunate—it is too close to the Sage's former residence. Given its connection to the Sage, we must be cautious."

So it was about this.

Sima Yu nodded: "Even if Master Yun hadn't come, I would have gone to the Governor myself. It is perfect; you may take the corpses of those people with you. I wonder how soon Master Yun can provide a result?"

Yun Tan: "Three days."

He spoke so readily that Sima Yu didn't know what to say.

Could it be that those thugs weren't targeting her cousin, but were related to the Sage?

"To investigate this as quickly as possible, could the Grand Princess please ask Miss Gu the Sixth to come out for a moment?" Yun Tan reiterated his request, smiling slightly: "The sooner we find out who is behind this, the sooner Miss Gu the Sixth will be safe."

"That is only natural."

Before the truth was revealed, no one knew if those people were trying to assassinate her cousin or if there was another motive.

Sima Yu instructed Chun Li to invite Gu Yuechan over.

"Many thanks, Grand Princess." Yun Tan smiled.

Sima Yu offered a polite remark, then ordered a maid to serve tea and asked him to wait a moment.

She had nothing to say to the Sage's close associates, and the hall was so quiet that only the sound of teacups tapping against the table could be heard.

Sima Yu thought that her cousin had not been back in the capital for long and was troubled by her uncle's affairs, so she had been cooped up in the estate; she shouldn't have made any enemies.

How could she encounter an assassination attempt just by going to Yongan Temple?

Her peripheral vision inadvertently swept over the hem of Yun Tan's Taoist robe, and she suddenly remembered her cousin saying unhappily today that the Taoist priest who helped her had forbidden her from seeking him out again.

This Master Yun was also from Yongan Temple and was a confidant of the Sage...

She furrowed her brows slightly. What kind of relationship could he have with Taoist Priest Qingxuan?

"Cousin."

Gu Yuechan walked into the hall, trying to muster a smile: "Chun Li said someone came to investigate my attack, you..."

Before she could finish, she saw the man sitting in the sandalwood chair.

"It's you?" Gu Yuechan pursed her lips, and the faint smile on her face vanished instantly.

Sima Yu’s gaze also turned sharp. Could it be as she suspected—that this man was the one who went by the name Taoist Priest Qingxuan? What was he trying to do?

"Miss Gu the Sixth." Yun Tan stood up and bowed to her: "My junior brother has already told me about today's incident. Please, Miss Gu the Sixth, tell me the details of the attack, and if you have any suspects, so that I may discuss with Governor Li where to begin the investigation."

Gu Yuechan had not expected that the person coming to investigate this matter would be the junior brother of Taoist Priest Qingxuan.

chapters.title: Clues
chapters.content:
Gu Yuechan was still angry, and she couldn't help but feel a lingering resentment toward anyone associated with Daoist Qingxuan.

However, she also knew that this person had come to help her uncover the truth, so both reason and etiquette dictated that she treat him with courtesy.

After a moment of internal struggle between reason and emotion, she sat down silently to the right of her cousin and said listlessly, "Let Guard Lin explain it. I have been in the carriage with my maid the whole time and don't know much. As for suspects, I don't have any leads for now."

Sima Yu turned slightly. Instead of calling for Lin Qi, she lowered her voice and asked her cousin a question first: "What is his relationship with Daoist Qingxuan?"

Gu Yuechan replied, "They might be fellow disciples."

Last time, when this Daoist came to tell her that Daoist Qingxuan wanted her to stay in the capital with peace of mind, he had referred to Daoist Qingxuan as his senior brother.

Sima Yu breathed a slight sigh of relief; at least he was not Daoist Qingxuan himself.

If he had sent someone to tell her cousin during the day that they need not meet again, only to come and speak with her at night, she would certainly have suspected him of harboring ill intentions.

She sat up straight and spoke in a gentler tone: "Master Yun, why don't you let my guard assist you in investigating this matter? My cousin has always been kind to others. Honestly, I don't know who would want her dead. However, my people said that their martial arts were not those of ordinary men; they seemed to have undergone formal training and were willing to die, which is why no one was left alive."

"It is indeed difficult when there are no survivors," Yun Tan said, calmly observing the woman sitting in the chair with her head bowed. "Has Lady Gu the Sixth been injured?"

Gu Yuechan lowered her eyes and answered every question, though her words were very brief.

"No."

Yun Tan nodded and withdrew his gaze. "Then Lady Gu the Sixth can think it over these next two days: has anyone ever shown you any malice?"

Gu Yuechan gave a soft "Mm."

Sima Yu could see that she was in low spirits, perhaps still dwelling on Daoist Qingxuan's words. Thinking that she wouldn't be able to provide any clues for now, she let her go back first and sent someone to summon Lin Qi.

Gu Yuechan did not want to stay long, so she offered a brief word of thanks and left with Qiongyu.

Back in her courtyard, she lay on the chaise longue, her gaze resting quietly on the dim candlelight.

Seeing that her mistress had returned from the Princess's quarters in an even worse mood, Biwen tugged gently on Qiongyu's sleeve, signaling her to find a way to help.

Qiongyu’s gaze fell suggestively on the storybooks on the table.

Although she felt these books were not proper reading material, it was the only way to divert her mistress's attention for now. When her mistress read them during the day, she seemed to briefly forget her sorrows.

Biwen understood.

She picked one from the pile of books on the table based on its title.

"Mistress," Biwen said, walking to the side of the chaise longue and eagerly handing over the book. "Take a look at this one; it's quite interesting."

Gu Yuechan swept a faint glance over the book and turned away, uninterested.

"I'm not in the mood."

Biwen said dejectedly, "Then what would put you in the mood, Mistress?"

Gu Yuechan didn't know either.

"Perhaps, once I know who ordered those people."

Her cheeks puffed out slightly, revealing a hint of distress. "That Master Yun told me to think about who might harbor malice toward me. Sigh, do you two have any leads?"

Qiongyu and Biwen both wore thoughtful expressions.

People with malice toward their mistress.

Madam Lü in the manor had always looked down on her, but Madam Lü was her uncle's wife; even if she disliked her, it was impossible for her to hire assassins.

Outside the manor... there were quite a few.

Previously, the Marchioness of Changping was dissatisfied with her, but ever since the head of the household took up the post of Vice Minister of Revenue, the Marchioness's attitude toward her had improved significantly. She was her future mother-in-law, so she shouldn't have done such a thing.

The rest were merely petty squabbles between young ladies, which could hardly be considered deep grudges.

"Could... could it be the Second Lady of the Xie family?" Biwen asked cautiously. "Isn't it said that she likes Master Ye? If something happened to you, wouldn't she get her wish?"

Gu Yuechan had almost forgotten about that person.

"But the Second Young Master doesn't like her. Even without me, would she necessarily be able to marry him?"

Qiongyu also felt suspicious of the Second Lady of the Xie family. The Zhenyuan Marquis Manor was powerful; if they wanted to harm her mistress, they would have plenty of resources at their disposal. The fact that they struck while her mistress was on the way to Yong'an Temple meant they must have known her itinerary in advance.

"It is at least a possibility," she said gently. "Mistress, since we are investigating, we cannot let any clue slip by. If it isn't the Second Lady of the Xie family, the Jingzhao Prefecture won't wrongly accuse her."

Gu Yuechan pondered for a moment and felt that Qiongyu made sense. It was just providing the Jingzhao Prefecture with a few directions to investigate, not declaring anyone guilty herself.

"Then write down everyone I have spoken to since I returned to the capital. Tomorrow, I will have my cousin give it to Master Yun."

She thought that this way, nothing would be missed.

It wasn't as if someone would want her dead just because they had spoken to her twice.

Qiongyu choked for a moment, and Biwen’s eyes went blank. People she had spoken to... how could she possibly remember them all?

The two looked at each other, thinking that since it concerned their mistress's safety, they would write down as many as they could.

They struggled through the day and finally handed the list to their mistress before dark the next day.

Gu Yuechan scanned it quickly and suddenly said, "Add Daoist Qingxuan as well."

She gave a soft huff. "I must be impartial."

Qiongyu thought to herself that her mistress was clearly still angry. If Daoist Qingxuan were involved in this, Master Yun would have already tried his best to suppress the matter.

Moreover, Daoist Qingxuan had no reason to assassinate her mistress.

However, it was better to go along with her mistress to avoid making her sad again.

"I will add it, then." Qiongyu reached out to take the paper filled with names from her hand, but Gu Yuechan pulled it back, saying sullenly, "Forget it, I was just joking with you."

Her fingers pinched the rice paper, and as she looked at the dense list of names, she seemed to sigh.

"I am not one to return kindness with enmity."

Qiongyu looked at the young lady, whose brows and eyes revealed a few traces of sorrow, and suddenly understood why her mistress was so sad.

Her mistress had been beautiful since childhood and came from a prestigious family. She had been held in the palm of everyone's hand since she was small; there were only people her mistress didn't want to associate with, and very few who didn't want to pay her any mind.

After Consort Zheng passed away, her mistress's temperament hadn't changed much, but she had finally experienced the taste of being neglected, and she cherished those who had not distanced themselves from her during that time even more.

Daoist Qingxuan had helped her mistress during this period, and her mistress was likely truly grateful to him in her heart.

It was a pity that the words Daoist Qingxuan had sent through others had truly hurt her mistress's heart.

However, her mistress had always been open-minded; surely, it wouldn't be long before she could let go of this Daoist.

chapters.title: Results
chapters.content:
The list reached Yun Tan’s hands. The people on it were connected to the Zhenyuan Marquis Estate, the Changping Marquis Estate, the Duke of Ping’s Estate, and General Zhao’s Estate...

With only two days left before the deadline set by the Sage, even if he had heaven-defying abilities, it would be impossible to question each of these people one by one.

Li Yuncheng, seeing the troubled look on his face, assumed the person who had formed a grudge with the young lady of the Gu family was someone extraordinary. He leaned over to peek while offering comfort: "Since this is a case the Sage deems important, surely no one would dare not cooperate with you, Lord Yun..."

His voice cut off abruptly after seeing the contents of the paper, then rose sharply.

"So many?"

Li Yuncheng felt a bit dizzy: "Is this Young Lady Gu capable of making so many enemies?"

Yun Tan replied, "They have only spoken; whether there is a grudge or not will only be known after investigation." He turned his head and asked, "Lord Li, have you discovered the origins of that group?"

Li Yuncheng said solemnly, "That group bore no markings, but the coroner has examined their bodies. Several did not die from external injuries, but from a poison called 'Thousand-Machine Powder.' I suspect this matter is related to the chaos caused by Prince Cheng five years ago. I have already ordered men to go to the Supreme Court to review the documents."

Yun Tan was quite surprised: "Prince Cheng?"

"Lord Yun is shocked, and so am I. Logically speaking, even if there were remnants of Prince Cheng’s faction, they should have been rendered powerless. To think they could reappear and cause trouble near the capital."

Li Yuncheng’s expression was grave: "Although Young Lady Gu is the victim, since it involves Prince Cheng’s rebels, this matter can likely no longer be defined as a simple vendetta. With such a major issue, three days is far too tight. Lord Yun, could you intercede with the Sage and ask for an extension?"

Prince Cheng’s rebels should have been wiped out entirely; how could they be connected to Young Lady Gu?

If that were truly the case, the severity of this case would be on an entirely different level.

Yun Tan said, "If that is indeed the case, we must naturally report it to the Sage and request the assistance of the Dark Star Camp. However, until the Sage speaks, Lord Li, you must still hurry."

The Dark Star Camp managed intelligence for the Great Jin and served as the Sage’s eyes and ears, responsible only for handling major court affairs.

Li Yuncheng knew this meant he had agreed. He breathed a sigh of relief; if it were truly the remnants of Prince Cheng causing trouble, three days would certainly not be enough.

But it was strange to think about—how could Young Lady Gu, a sheltered young woman, be involved with Prince Cheng’s remnants? Could it be...

Li Yuncheng asked, "Lord Yun, do you think it’s possible that Vice Minister Gu once had some connection with Prince Cheng? If that’s the case, our search direction might be wrong. Why not question Vice Minister Gu? Perhaps there will be new clues."

After reading the list, Yun Tan put the paper away and said in a gentle tone, "Lord Li, before there is evidence that this case is related to Prince Cheng’s remnants, it is better not to alarm too many people. The Sage might be displeased."

He cupped his hands and said, "I will go report to the Sage first. Lord Li, farewell."

Left behind, Li Yuncheng frowned. Why would the Sage be displeased? It was just asking Vice Minister Gu a few questions. Surely, as the father of Young Lady Gu, he wouldn't be unaware of this matter. Could that really be considered alarming?

However, he didn't expect that before he could find Vice Minister Gu, he would be sought out by him instead.

Gu Mingtu had only learned of his daughter’s danger yesterday. His wife had suggested that until they knew who was trying to harm Zhaozhao, it would be safer for her to stay at the Princess’s Estate, where there were guards, rather than at home.

The implication was that if the mastermind couldn't be caught, his daughter would be trapped in the Princess’s Estate indefinitely, unable to go out.

Fearing that the Capital Prefecture did not take the case seriously, he had come specifically to ask the Prefect Li about the progress of the investigation.

Hearing him ask about the progress, Li Yuncheng became vigilant and replied with a smile, "This case is being personally overseen by the Sage; it is not convenient to disclose. Please forgive me, Lord Gu."

Gu Mingtu: "...The Sage is overseeing it?"

The Sage was busy with a thousand tasks a day; how could he have the leisure to look into an attack on a minister’s daughter?

He looked suspiciously at the tight-lipped Li Yuncheng: "Is there no lead?"

Li Yuncheng refused to disclose: "Vice Minister Gu, please do not make things difficult for me. I can only report this matter to the Sage."

No matter how Gu Mingtu probed, Li Yuncheng only had one answer: "I cannot disclose it."

Helpless, Gu Mingtu had no choice but to leave. Upon returning to the estate, he spoke to Zheng Ying about it and sighed, "I don't know what major case this has become entangled in."

Zheng Ying was also worried: "Ningxi said there would be results within three days, and tomorrow is the last day. During the day, Lady Xu came looking for Zhaozhao, saying she wanted to renovate the new bridal chambers for the second son and Zhaozhao, and wanted to ask what Zhaozhao liked. I told her she went to visit her cousin and wouldn't be home for a few days. Not returning home for so long is starting to arouse suspicion."

She could not find peace for a single day as long as she didn't know who wanted to harm Zhaozhao.

"In two days, I will go to Ningxi’s place to see her." Zheng Ying was afraid her daughter would be anxious.

Gu Mingtu naturally agreed.

Inside the Princess’s Estate.

The young woman about whom the couple was so worried was smiling happily as she fed a fruit to her beloved Lion-Steed horse.

"Cousin, after tomorrow, can I go out and play?"

Sima Yu replied, "If things go smoothly, naturally you can. I’m just afraid that Lord Yun was only boasting. If Lord Yun doesn't come tomorrow, I will have Lin Qi go to the prefecture office to ask."

Gu Yuechan’s movements as she fed the horse slowed, and the smile on her face faded slightly.

"Lord Yun is the Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; why is he in charge of this?" She lowered her eyes and said, "Is it because I had the accident on the way to Yong'an Temple?"

Sima Yu curled her lips: "Who knows? Probably just bored."

In any case, she would never say that it might be because of Daoist Qingxuan.

Her cousin had been sad for two days because of this person. She had brought her to the horse track today to cheer her up; it would be best if her cousin never had to hear that name again.

Gu Yuechan: "...Oh."

She thought to herself that her cousin was truly even worse at speaking than she was.

But since she was her cousin, she would just smile it off.

As for whether Lord Yun was boasting, she should know by tomorrow.

Ever since Li Yuncheng discovered that this matter might be related to Prince Cheng’s rebels, Yun Tan had been so busy he didn't even have time to sleep. The Sage wanted discretion, so he had to run to every office himself to consolidate intelligence. Only then did he arrive at the Princess’s Estate before the 7:00 PM deadline on the third day.

In the front hall.

Upon learning that Lord Yun had arrived, Gu Yuechan hurried there with her cousin. As soon as she sat down, she looked at Yun Tan eagerly, waiting for him to reveal who was so heartless as to be against her.

Yun Tan did not beat around the bush: "Princess, Young Lady Gu, this case has been initially clarified. The people who attacked Young Lady Gu were remnants of Prince Cheng’s faction. They have infiltrated the capital region in the last two years and have been looking for opportunities to rebuild their power."

Sima Yu looked skeptical, secretly thinking that perhaps he hadn't found any results and was using Prince Cheng’s remnants to fool her.

Her cousin didn't even know Prince Cheng; when Prince Cheng rebelled, she wasn't even in the capital. Why would Prince Cheng’s remnants want to assassinate her cousin?

"And the person who instigated it..." Yun Tan’s gaze swept over the confused young woman: "...should be the Marchioness of Changping."

Gu Yuechan was still thinking about Prince Cheng’s remnants. She didn't know much about the rebellion, but she had been far away in Qingzhou at the time; she shouldn't have been involved in Prince Cheng’s affairs.

Yun Tan’s words brought her back to reality.

Her red lips parted slightly, her face full of shock.

Yun Tan lowered his eyes slightly. He remembered that when the Sage learned of this, he was also mostly shocked, but then seemed to have a sudden realization.

The Marchioness of Changping, as the future mother-in-law of Young Lady Gu, had actually dealt such a cruel blow to her.

The marriage between their two families would likely not be able to proceed.

chapters.title: Summons
chapters.content:
"The Marchioness of Changping..." Sima Yu pondered for a moment and asked, "Why would she do such a thing?"

Yun Tan took a sip of tea to soothe the dryness from his long journey before replying, "I do not know. The case has already been transferred to the Court of Judicial Review. She was arrested and taken in for questioning under the charge of colluding with the remnants of Prince Cheng's faction. I expect we will know the reason in a couple of days."

Having said what needed to be said, he stood up and added, "If Her Highness or Lady Gu have any further questions, you may send someone to find me after the case is concluded. I will certainly tell you everything I know. It is getting late, so I shall take my leave."

Sima Yu glanced at her distracted cousin and nodded, "Take care, Magistrate Yun."

With only the two of them left in the hall, Sima Yu watched her cousin quietly and said softly, "If you are sad, there is no need to hold it in. Crying in front of me is nothing to be ashamed of."

Gu Yuechan blinked, "Why would I cry?"

Sima Yu scrutinized her expression closely. She truly did not seem sad; even the surprise from just a moment ago had almost vanished.

"You..." she hesitated, "Do you realize that because the Marchioness of Changping has done this, your marriage to the Second Young Master Ye may no longer be possible?"

Gu Yuechan frowned, "Oh, that's true. My mother will certainly not agree to it."

Fearing that her cousin might be foolish enough to still want to marry him, Sima Yu said in a low, stern voice, "It is fortunate that you and the Second Young Master Ye are not yet married. If you had already married into that family, I fear your life would truly be in danger. There are plenty of fine gentlemen in the capital; just break off this engagement and find someone else. At the very worst, your cousin will support you for the rest of your life."

Gu Yuechan was amused, "Cousin, you aren't my mother."

"I am being serious with you." Sima Yu sat up straight and looked at her with a grave expression, "No matter how good the Second Young Master Ye is, the Marchioness of Changping is the mother who bore him. Since this matter has reached the Court of Judicial Review, it will absolutely not end well."

If this had been handled privately, given the relationship between the two families, they might have been able to take a step back for various reasons.

But since it involved the remnants of Prince Cheng's faction and was being tried by the Court of Judicial Review, the matter was no longer under their control.

Perhaps even the Emperor would learn of this case.

Gu Yuechan was silent for a long time before nodding gently.

"The Marchioness of Changping has never liked me; I know that. So, the fact that she did this doesn't make me sad—I don't like her either. It's just that the Second Young Master has always treated me very well, and I actually feel a bit..."

She paused, then continued, "A bit afraid that he will be heartbroken."

Sima Yu was not worried about the Second Young Master Ye's heartbreak. Just as she was about to say something disparaging about him to dispel any potential softness in her cousin's heart, she heard her cousin huff indignantly before she could speak.

"Lady Xu is truly hateful." Gu Yuechan felt the Second Young Master was pitiful. She cupped her face in her hands and sighed for him, "It's a pity. The Second Young Master won't be able to marry a woman as beautiful and talented as me."

Sima Yu: "..."

Her cousin's mindset made her previous worries seem entirely superfluous.

With a blank face, she stood up and said to her narcissistic cousin, "It's late, go to sleep."

Gu Yuechan curled her lips and smiled at her, "Alright, Cousin. Also, since the person behind this has been found, I should return home tomorrow. If I stay too long, my father and mother will worry."

Sima Yu nodded, "I will accompany you back tomorrow."

She had heard that her uncle and the Marquis of Changping were close friends. If her uncle were to wrong her cousin for the sake of the Marquis, she would have to argue the case firmly.

Gu Yuechan did not know her thoughts and assumed her cousin was worried about danger on the road home. Touched to the point of tears, she tugged at her cousin's shawl, "Cousin, you are so kind."

After the two returned to their respective rooms, the smile on Gu Yuechan's face slowly faded.

She sat on the couch, a slight ache in her chest.

The candlelight reflected her figure, appearing somewhat lonely.

Seeing that her mistress looked unwell, Qiongyu asked softly, "My Lady, did Magistrate Yun not find anything?"

"No." Gu Yuechan slumped listlessly over the table, "I'm just feeling a bit tired. Let's talk about it tomorrow; I want to sleep."

So he had found out, but the person involved was troubling her mistress.

Qiongyu said no more. Since her mistress had already bathed, she let down the hair that had been simply pinned up, blew out the candles in the outer room, and withdrew with Biwen.

In the quiet inner chamber, Gu Yuechan gazed vaguely at the rug on the floor, her heart filled with confusion about the future.

How much of an impact would this matter have?

She had no way of predicting it.

However, it wasn't her who had done wrong. Gu Yuechan straightened up and walked toward the bed; why should she be anxious because of this?

The last candle flickered out, and the room fell into complete silence.

Meanwhile, the Marquis of Changping's residence, located two wards away from the Princess's mansion, was in chaos.

Ye An, the Marquis of Changping, sat wearily in a sandalwood armchair and said to his two sons in the hall, "You two go back first. After the morning court session tomorrow, I will go to request an audience with the Emperor."

"Father." Ye Zheng's expression was urgent, "Could it be that someone wants to harm you and thus framed Mother? The people from the Court of Judicial Review only said Mother was involved with rebels, but they refused to say why. Will the Emperor believe your words? What if—what if the Emperor would rather kill the innocent by mistake..."

"Second Son." Ye An's voice was cold and heavy, "Is the Emperor someone you can discuss?"

Ye Zheng lowered his head, knowing he had spoken wrongly. This was tantamount to saying the Emperor was not a wise monarch.

"I am only worried about Mother, Father."

"Yes, Father." Ye Yan stepped forward to relieve his brother, "My younger brother is only worried and has lost his composure. If Mother is truly being wronged, I believe the Court of Judicial Review will clear her name."

Ye An closed his eyes in annoyance, "I hope so. Go back; you won't be able to come up with a solution here."

The two brothers left one after another. After walking out of Zhangwen Hall, Ye Yan offered a few words of comfort to Ye Zheng, telling him to wait for news from their father and that he believed their mother would never collude with Prince Cheng. There must be a misunderstanding, and at the very worst, he would ask the County Princess to try and petition Prince Kang.

Ye Zheng sighed, thanked him sincerely, and walked wearily back to his own courtyard.

Once the others were out of sight, under the moonlight, the corners of Ye Yan's mouth flattened, devoid of any warmth.

This stepmother of his—she wouldn't really do something so treasonous, would she? It didn't matter if she wanted to die, but she shouldn't drag the Marquis of Changping's residence down with her.

When the sky was just beginning to brighten, carriages lined up in front of the Imperial Palace, all belonging to officials preparing to enter for the morning court.

Ye An held his ivory tablet, walking along the palace path with a troubled mind. He had no interest in conversation, even when he saw Gu Mingtu.

Gu Mingtu thought he had encountered some difficulty and intended to ask him after the court session. The two families were to be in-laws and were linked in their interests; if there was truly a difficulty, he could help offer some advice.

Unexpectedly, after the court session, the Emperor's attendant, Eunuch Xu, asked the two of them to stay behind and wait in the Hanguang Hall for the Emperor's questioning.

chapters.title: Breaking the Engagement
chapters.content:
Since the Emperor ascended the throne, this was the first time Gu Mingtu had been summoned to the Hanguang Palace.

He had no inkling as to why he had been summoned. The matters discussed in court recently had little to do with the Ministry of Revenue, and he could not tell if the Emperor’s summons boded well or ill.

Ye An, who accompanied him, understood exactly why he was being summoned by the Emperor and assumed that Gu Mingtu was being implicated because of him.

"Brother Gu," Ye An said in a hushed voice, "You are likely being dragged into this because of me. This matter has nothing to do with your family; you need not worry too much."

With the attendant Xu present, Gu Mingtu could not say much, but a look of worry appeared in his eyes. What on earth had happened to Brother Ye?

Stepping into the Hanguang Palace, the two men bowed respectfully.

From the head of the hall came the Emperor’s clear, dignified voice: "Rise. Zhou Ling, explain it to the two of them."

Gu Mingtu straightened up and only then noticed there was another person in the hall—it was the Minister of the Grand Court of Justice.

"Yes, Your Majesty." Zhou Ling turned his gaze toward the two men who had entered. "Vice Minister Ye, the Grand Court of Justice interrogated the Marchioness of Changping throughout the night yesterday. The Marchioness has confessed to instructing the remnants of the Prince of Cheng’s faction to ambush and attack the Sixth Lady of the Gu family on the outskirts of the capital. However, she insists that she did not know the identities of those men, claiming she only took them for hired assassins paid to abduct the Sixth Lady of the Gu family, so as to have a pretext to break off the engagement with the Gu household."

Ye An’s expression went blank. "Abduct... the Sixth Lady? Done by the Xu woman?"

Zhou Ling narrowed his eyes. "Vice Minister Ye, that is a question I should be asking you. The Sixth Lady of the Gu family is betrothed to your household’s second son. I hear the wedding date was already set for the eighteenth of the fourth month, and it was the Xu woman herself who came to your home to finalize it. What, then, was the true purpose of the Marchioness hiring people to abduct the Sixth Lady? Or is it that the Marquis’s household is colluding with the remnants of the Prince of Cheng’s faction, intending to use the Sixth Lady of the Gu family as a bargaining chip to force Vice Minister Gu or the Grand Princess Ningxi to do your bidding?"

Seeing him link the Marquis’s household with the remnants of the Prince of Cheng’s faction, Ye An broke into a cold sweat. Treason was a crime punishable by the execution of one’s entire clan; at this moment, he could not even spare a thought for the Sixth Lady.

"Lord Zhou, I know nothing of this. The Sixth Lady and my second son are childhood sweethearts with deep affection for one another; she is like a daughter to me. Had I known the Xu woman harbored such schemes, I would certainly have stopped her. As for the remnants of the Prince of Cheng’s faction, I know even less."

He bowed toward the imperial desk. "I beg Your Majesty to discern the truth."

Zhou Ling retorted angrily, "Do you think you can wash your hands of this with a mere 'I don't know'? The people who found the remnants of the Prince of Cheng’s faction were your own household servants. As the head of the Marquis’s household, how could you be completely unaware?"

"Zhou Ling," Sima Xin said.

Zhou Ling hurriedly straightened his posture and lowered his head. "Your Majesty, Vice Minister Ye refuses to disclose anything. I request permission to search the Marquis’s household."

Ye An bowed even lower. He believed that a clear conscience needed no fear, but hearing the word "search," he could not help but worry if there truly were remnants of the Prince of Cheng’s faction hidden within his estate.

Sima Xin’s gaze swept calmly over the three officials in the hall, finally resting on the one who had remained silent. "Vice Minister Gu, what is your opinion?"

What was Gu Mingtu’s opinion?

If he were not standing in the Hanguang Palace, he would certainly have given this man, Ye An, a sound beating.

He and his wife had been worried for days, terrified that Zhaozhao might encounter danger again, and despite racking their brains, they had found no leads. Yet, the culprit was right before his eyes.

But in the presence of the Emperor, he had to suppress his fury. Holding his ivory tablet, he replied respectfully, "I beg Your Majesty to seek justice for my daughter. I was blind and foolish to believe that the Marchioness of Changping truly cared for the Sixth Lady, which led to this disaster. Had we broken off this engagement sooner, the Sixth Lady might not have suffered this ordeal."

"Oh?" Sima Xin’s eyes were calm. "Does Vice Minister Gu believe that what the Xu woman said is true?"

Gu Mingtu replied, "The matter is complex. Lord Zhou does not know the inside story, so naturally, he finds the Xu woman’s words absurd."

He had known Ye An for nearly forty years; he knew exactly what kind of person Ye An was.

As for Zhaozhao’s affairs, he would settle them privately. In the imperial court, he could not bear to see the Marquis of Changping’s household destroyed over this.

"Your Majesty, please discern the truth," he said slowly. "The Marchioness did indeed show dissatisfaction with this marriage, and I also had intentions of dissolving the engagement with the Marquis’s household. However, the engagement had been set for many years, and I feared that breaking it off rashly would hurt the young ones. Later, seeing the Marchioness treat Zhaozhao with kindness, I set my mind at ease. I did not expect it to be merely a delaying tactic."

Ye An had not expected Brother Gu to be willing to speak for him at such a time, and his heart was filled with complex emotions. If only he had realized the Xu woman’s intentions sooner, things would not have escalated to the point of reaching the Emperor.

Zhou Ling frowned. This Vice Minister Gu was actually willing to speak for Vice Minister Ye, but if the two were accomplices, then the Xu woman’s actions would make no sense.

The hall fell silent.

A moment later, Sima Xin lowered his eyes and said in a flat tone, "Since Vice Minister Gu has said so, Zhou Ling, the matter of the search shall be discussed later. The officials of the Marquis of Changping’s household are to suspend their court duties and are forbidden from leaving the capital. We shall wait until the investigation is clear before deciding on the punishment. You may withdraw."

The three men bowed and retreated.

Once outside the Hanguang Palace, Ye An wanted to say a few words of gratitude to Gu Mingtu. He had just uttered "Brother Gu" when he heard the other man snort coldly, "I dare not accept it. The engagement between the Sixth Lady and your second son is hereby dissolved. I hope that, in consideration of the suffering the Sixth Lady has endured, you will be decisive and return the tokens of betrothal."

Ye An had no face left to argue. He sighed dejectedly, "Very well."

Inside the Hanguang Palace, Xu He served the Emperor fresh tea and stood quietly to the side.

The Emperor preferred silence, and the palace maids and attendants moved with light steps. The vast palace was as quiet as a cold night.

Sima Xin picked up the memorials piled on the imperial desk and suddenly said, "She is likely going to cry again."

Xu He looked up in surprise. She? Who?

After the Emperor said this abruptly, he did not speak again. Xu He was filled with confusion but dared not ask. After thinking for a long time, a person suddenly came to mind.

The Sixth Lady of the Gu family.

Last time at the Yong'an Temple, he heard the Emperor say: "What are you crying for?"

Afterward, the Emperor granted her request.

Later, when Daoist Yunfeng came to report to the Emperor and he relayed the message to the Sixth Lady of the Gu family that she need not return to the temple, she seemed to have tears in her eyes.

The Emperor had said nothing at the time, only remaining silent for a long while.

Later, he only showed a hint of abnormality when he learned that the Sixth Lady of the Gu family had encountered danger, yet he had no intention of seeing her.

Xu He glanced quietly at the Emperor. His expression was unchanged, and his hand holding the brush was steady and firm.

That sentence seemed to be nothing more than a casual remark from the Emperor.

But he had been by the Emperor’s side for eight years; if it were anyone else, it might have been an unintentional comment.

He struggled for a moment, feeling he should still try to discern the Emperor’s will, even though he seemed to have been misinterpreting the Emperor’s intentions lately.

"This is actually a good thing for the Sixth Lady of the Gu family. A moment of heartbreak is better than wasting a lifetime. However, good marriages often come late; if the Sixth Lady can come to terms with it, she should be happy."

Sima Xin closed the memorial he had finished reviewing, leaned back against the chair, and looked on with calm eyes. "Childhood sweethearts, hearts in harmony—what a pity."

Xu He could not hear a hint of pity in that.

However, he did not dare to speak again.

The hall returned to silence. Sima Xin picked up his teacup and ordered, "Invite Grand Princess Lehua to the palace tomorrow. I have already made a decision regarding the candidates for her consort that she submitted."
